posts.title: CD47-SIRPα as a Therapeutic Target in Sarcoma: A Systematic Review of Expression, Preclinical, and Clinical Evidence
posts.authors: Xiao M, Guo C, Yang Q
posts.summary: PRISMA systematic review of 50 studies on the CD47-SIRPα 'don't eat me' innate checkpoint in sarcoma. CD47 expression is subtype-dependent and bimodal, and is consistent in chordoma and angiosarcoma, but only two single-arm interventional trials have enrolled sarcoma patients.
key_points: CD47 blockade consistently increased macrophage phagocytosis in preclinical models, and combinations outperformed single agents.
Certainty of evidence was low for expression and patient-cohort data and very low for preclinical and interventional data.
The authors call for a harmonised immunohistochemistry standard and a biomarker-selected trial with an internal comparator.

posts.title: Base composition reflects RNA polymerase II displacement
posts.authors: Barone GEF, Stanley JT, Ramirez D, et al.
posts.summary: A probabilistic mixture model of nascent RNA-seq across gene bodies is used to study Pol II termination and displacement across cell types and species. Genes fall into two classes with conserved base-composition patterns near the displacement site, and the classes respond differently to perturbations that cause readthrough.
key_points: The mixture model quantifies Pol II dynamics across entire gene bodies from nascent RNA-seq.
Both classes share an upstream T-rich region; one also has a GC-rich region around the displacement site.
T-rich-only genes are more affected by heat shock, viral infection, kinase inhibition and arsenic.

posts.title: TFXcan reveals transcription factor programs driving GWAS loci
posts.authors: Adeluwa T, Salazar-Magaña S, Sumner S, et al.
posts.summary: TFXcan correlates genetically predicted transcription-factor binding with phenotypes to nominate TF-tissue pairs behind GWAS loci. Its Enpact component combines Enformer and IMPACT to infer personalised TF binding from genotype. In a prostate cancer risk analysis across 700 TF-tissue pairs it implicates multiple TFs at risk loci.
key_points: Enpact infers personalised TF-binding events from genotype using a deep-learning approach.
Matrix decomposition groups TF-tissue pairs into candidate driver programs.
The prostate cancer case study identifies TF programs at risk loci.

posts.title: Standardizing spatial transcriptomic analysis for infectious diseases with STID
posts.authors: Qin Y, Peng Y, Chen Q, et al.
posts.summary: STID is a standardised Seurat- and Python-based framework for spatial transcriptomics of infectious disease. It adds an infection-specific data structure with pathogen background correction, infection-associated spot and niche identification, and multi-sample comparative and temporal analyses.
key_points: Infection-specific, extensible data structure built on the Seurat ecosystem.
Pathogen background correction and niche identification.
Applies to bacterial, viral and parasitic infections.

posts.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor-pHLA binding prediction
posts.authors: Zhu X, Lu J, Lu Y, et al.
posts.summary: The authors present Hi-TPH, a large hierarchical TCR-pHLA dataset with an on-the-fly method for generating non-binding examples. Protein language models fine-tuned on it (Hi-TPH-PLMs) give a 19.2% gain over state-of-the-art tools on an external wet-lab test set.
key_points: Hierarchical dataset with an unbiased non-binder selection method.
The hierarchy is used to dissect how TCR and HLA components contribute to binding prediction.
Dataset and models are released publicly.

posts.title: Multi-View State-Space Modeling for Zero-Shot circRNA-miRNA Interaction Prediction
posts.authors: Wei MM, Wang L, Huang YA, et al.
posts.summary: MV-S2M is a multi-view state-space model that predicts circRNA-miRNA interactions, including for circRNAs or miRNAs never seen in training. It builds disease-mediated semantic subgraphs and uses structure-aware diffusion to enrich molecular priors, and reports state-of-the-art results on benchmark datasets in zero-shot and conventional settings.
key_points: Targets zero-shot interaction prediction rather than only known pairs.
Combines structure-aware diffusion, meta-path semantic subgraphs and state-space modelling.
Cold-start evaluations show how generalisation differs across unseen-entity settings.

posts.title: Si-scRNA-seq: Enabling ambient-stable single-cell transcriptomics through spatially confined biosilicification
posts.authors: Zhou L, Ruan T, He Y, et al.
posts.summary: Spatially confined biosilicification encapsulates cellular RNA in a nanoscopic silica layer so single-cell samples can be stored at room temperature. Transcriptomes stay highly faithful to fresh samples after 7 days (R=0.95), and the method resolved cell heterogeneity in clinical lung, liver and ovarian cancer specimens.
key_points: RNA half-life at 25 °C is extended to 54.8 days, a 685-fold gain.
A silicification inhibitor prevents cell aggregation and over-crosslinking while keeping RNA accessible.
Compatible with mainstream scRNA-seq platforms.

posts.title: Brr2p-mediated unwinding of U4/U6 is promoted by a mutually exclusive internal stem loop in U4 and involves destabilization of the 5' stem-loop of U4
posts.authors: Nielsen KH, Johnson B, Das A, et al.
posts.summary: Yeast genetics and in vitro assays show how the helicase Brr2p unwinds U4/U6 to activate the spliceosome. Destabilising mutations in U4 stem I, stem II and the 5' stem loop suppress an unwinding-deficient brr2 mutant.
key_points: Brr2p disrupts both U4/U6 stems in vivo.
Brr2p displaces Prp31p from the U4 5' stem loop in vitro.
A conserved internal U4 stem loop that is mutually exclusive with stem I promotes unwinding.

posts.title: Inferring somatic copy number aberrations from spatial transcriptomics data to study early cancer development
posts.authors: Honig F, Brochen C, Basha M, et al.
posts.summary: A computational framework infers somatic copy number aberrations from Xenium spatial transcriptomics data and maps cell populations sharing an SCNA profile. It recovers known CNAs in ovarian, cervical and breast cancer, and in high-grade serous ovarian cancer finds an intermediate fallopian-tube epithelial population with early transformation features.
key_points: SCNAs inferred from Xenium data define spatially coherent clones.
SCNA-defined populations recapitulate known copy number alterations and pathology in three cancer types.
The HGSOC fallopian-tube population shows early transformation with immune remodelling.

posts.title: Quantifying epigenetic reprogramming and cellular plasticity in preneoplastic lesions reveals dedifferentiation as a key precancer hallmark
posts.authors: Teschendorff A, Tham JK
posts.summary: PLASTIC is a pan-tissue framework that quantifies cellular plasticity and epigenetic reprogramming from scRNA-seq and builds Waddington-like landscapes to flag high cancer-risk states. Across preneoplastic tissues the high-risk state shows increased dedifferentiation, even relative to its fetal counterpart.
key_points: Works on scRNA-seq from any tissue.
Predicts metaplasia in lung cells from smokers.
The risk signature is validated in independent data.

posts.title: Detecting context-dependent selection on cancer driver genes with DiffDriver
posts.authors: Zhou J, Zhang Q, Song L, et al.
posts.summary: DiffDriver is a statistical method that tests whether selection on a driver gene differs across individual-level contexts such as clinical traits or immune subtype. It models mutation-rate variation across bases and individuals and uses sequence functional information to gain power.
key_points: Reduces false positives and improves power over current methods in simulations.
24.3% of driver genes show differential selection for at least one clinical trait.
8.2% of driver genes differ between immune subtypes.

posts.title: CATFISHR: integration of transcriptome and inferred CNV profiles for comprehensive malignant cell identification
posts.authors: Shukla P, Mannino M, Hofer M, et al.
posts.summary: CATFISHR is a semi-automated workflow that combines expression similarity, inferred CNV profiles and consensus cell typing to classify malignant cells in scRNA-seq against high-confidence references. It was tested on seven scRNA-seq cohorts and one Visium sample.
key_points: Balanced accuracy is above 0.85 in 6 of 8 cohorts.
It recovers 'Hidden' malignant cells that standard QC metrics do not explain.
In Visium, Hidden spots contain histologist-confirmed malignant cells.

posts.title: DNA methylation is a key determinant of response to targeted and immune checkpoint therapies in metastatic renal cell carcinoma
posts.authors: Jeanneret F, Schoch S, Ballester P, et al.
posts.summary: A meta-analysis of DNA methylation from 727 ccRCC tumours identifies a hyper-methylated subtype (15% of tumours) with shorter survival. A nine-gene-ratio expression classifier predicts the subtype (AUC 0.96 in an independent cohort).
key_points: The hyper-methylated subtype is proliferative, DNMT3B-high and TET2-low.
Predicted hyper-methylated tumours do worse on sunitinib.
No such difference was seen on immune checkpoint-based regimens.

posts.title: Predicting Pre-treatment Resistance or Post-treatment Effect? A Systematic Benchmarking of Single-Cell Drug Response Models
posts.authors: Shen L, Sun X, Zheng S, et al.
posts.summary: A benchmark of single-cell drug response prediction models on 26 scRNA-seq datasets (over 760,000 cells, 12 cancer types, 21 agents), including two lineage-tracing datasets with validated response labels. Performance is much higher in cell lines than in tissue and no method dominates.
key_points: Treatment-associated states are easier to separate than pre-sensitive and pre-resistant states.
Pre-existing resistance signals are detectable but subtle.
scDEAL performance depends on the training-label definition and architecture.

posts.title: OmniRE-seq: A Dual-Method Framework for Decoding RNA Editing Dynamics in Disease and Therapy
posts.authors: Hang Y, Liu H, Li W, et al.
posts.summary: OmniRE-seq pairs RE-seq for bulk RNA-seq and scRE-seq for single-cell data to quantify RNA editing at locus, gene and burden level. It is applied to murine sepsis, MDS, drug-treated melanoma and colorectal cancer, where cell-type-specific editing is resolved.
key_points: A standardised bulk and single-cell toolkit for RNA editing quantification.
Cell-type-specific editing patterns resolved in colorectal cancer.
Integrated analysis nominates convergent editing signals and therapeutic targets.

posts.title: Somatic evolution of cancer genes in sex chromosomes
posts.authors: Marco A, Akachukwu AC, Ratcliff JS
posts.summary: The authors adapt population-genetics models of haploid and diploid adaptation to somatic evolution and test them on COSMIC mutations. In male patients X-linked tumour suppressors show a higher loss-of-function to synonymous ratio than autosomal ones, with no such difference in females.
key_points: Hemizygous male X means a single hit can inactivate an X-linked tumour suppressor.
X-linked tumour suppressors also show more frequent complete loss in males.
Ploidy and chromosomal context can be built into models of somatic evolution.

posts.title: Chromosomal instability drives continual flux in cancer genomes
posts.authors: Guscott MA, Lumeau A, Gallagher AD, et al.
posts.summary: Single-genome sequencing of individual cells across 34 cancer cell lines and organoids tracks de novo copy number alterations. CIN generates one to five new CNAs per cell cycle, scales with genomic complexity and rises after whole-genome duplication.
key_points: New CNAs are largely stochastic along the genome, with negative selection against large ones.
Whole-genome duplication acutely raises CIN.
Chemotherapy drives convergent recurrent CNAs while CIN stays high.

posts.title: Nonsense-mediated decay constrains transposable element-driven evolutionary innovation
posts.authors: Plowman T, Kassiotis G
posts.summary: Long-read RNA-seq of cell lines after NMD inhibition gives an NMD-extended transcriptome of about 217,000 transcripts, roughly 80% unannotated. NMD-regulated transcripts are enriched for exonization of LTR and LINE elements, mainly as alternative isoforms of annotated genes.
key_points: NMD-silenced TEs are younger and more diverged, with less conserved splice sites.
NMD activity is elevated in lung cancer and linked to better survival in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
Alu-exonizing isoforms of DDX49, NEIL3 and SETDB1 give stable proteins with distinct activity.

posts.title: Quantification method affects replicability of eQTL analysis, colocalization and TWAS
posts.authors: Head ST, Bresnahan ST, Chang YH, et al.
posts.summary: The authors re-analyse GTEx data (48 tissues, 7 phenotypes) to test how the choice of transcript annotation and quantification method changes eQTL, colocalization and TWAS results. Both choices strongly affect eQTL detection and expression prediction, and the differences carry through to colocalization and TWAS calls.
key_points: Annotation and quantifier choice substantially change eQTL detection and expression prediction.
The differences carry into colocalization and TWAS results.
Results agree across pipelines mainly for longer genes, genes with more isoforms and highly heritable genes.

figure.caption: The same RNA-seq data are quantified with two annotation and tool combinations, giving partly overlapping sets of eQTL, colocalization and TWAS calls.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Intron retention regulates STAT2 function and associates with immunotherapy response in lung cancer
posts.authors: Englander RP, Brugiolo M, Devoucoux M, et al.
posts.summary: Long-read RNA-seq of primary lung adenocarcinomas mapped alternative splicing and found more than 149,000 full-length isoforms, over half unannotated. Retained introns in STAT2 give altered protein isoforms that regulate interferon signalling and correlate with survival after anti-PD-L1 therapy.
key_points: More than 149,000 full-length isoforms were found, over half unannotated.
Many of the new isoforms are in immune and type I interferon genes.
STAT2 intron retention acts as an interferon regulatory axis linked to anti-PD-L1 response.

figure.caption: STAT2 pre-mRNA is either spliced to the canonical form or keeps its intron, giving an altered isoform that feeds into type I interferon signalling in lung tumours.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: hnRNPA2B1 sustains antitumor T cell immunity and enhances cancer immunotherapy through IDR-dependent stabilization of chromatin-regulatory transcripts
posts.authors: Liu S, Gao W, Hu M, et al.
posts.summary: An in vivo CRISPR screen identifies hnRNPA2B1 as a regulator of CD8+ T cell fitness. It forms nuclear puncta and stabilizes chromatin-organization RNAs, which keeps chromatin accessible and restrains terminal exhaustion.
key_points: hnRNPA2B1 is enriched in proliferative, intermediate-exhausted T cells and tracks with favourable outcomes.
Knocking it out in CD8+ T cells accelerates exhaustion and weakens checkpoint-blockade response.
It acts through disordered-region-dependent RNA stabilization.

figure.caption: With hnRNPA2B1 the T cell nucleus holds puncta and stable chromatin-regulatory RNAs and resists exhaustion; without it those RNAs are lost and exhaustion comes faster.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Single-cell tumour phylogenetics
posts.authors: Gawron J, Kuipers J, Li A, et al.
posts.summary: Reviews the models and assumptions behind methods that reconstruct tumour phylogenies from single-cell sequencing. It covers recent algorithmic advances, their use in basic and clinical oncology, and open challenges.
key_points: The nature of single-cell tumour data needs bespoke phylogenetic models.
Covers methods and their use for individual cancers and patient cohorts.
Outlines open challenges and future applications.

posts.title: Regulatable in vivo gene expression via adaptamers
posts.authors: Bryant J, Herron L, Doctor Y, et al.
posts.summary: The adaptamer is a compact (under 120 bp) RNA switch that pairs a small-molecule-responsive aptamer with ADAR-mediated editing of a stop codon to control translation. It works in cell lines and human T cells, and AAV-delivered adaptamer-controlled FGF21 reversed obesity and liver steatosis in mice.
key_points: Cleavage-free, post-transcriptional control with no exogenous protein machinery.
Works in multiple cell lines, including human T cells.
AAV-delivered FGF21 under adaptamer control reversed obesity and hepatic steatosis in mice.

posts.title: Integration-free and cluster-free detection of localized differential gene coexpression in single-cell data with DiCoLo
posts.authors: Li R, Yang J, Su PC, et al.
posts.summary: DiCoLo finds changes in gene coordination between conditions without clustering cells or aligning them across conditions. It builds optimal-transport gene graphs and compares their connectivity, outperforming existing methods on benchmarks and, on mouse hair follicle data, revealing gene programs behind dermal condensate differentiation.
key_points: No clustering or integration is needed, so it works for small subpopulations and under batch effects.
It outperforms existing methods across multiple benchmarks.
Applied to hair follicle development, it finds perturbation-driven gene programs.

posts.title: GBZ-base and GAF-base: Indexed pangenome file formats
posts.authors: Sirén J, Paten B
posts.summary: SQLite-backed indexed formats comparable to GBZ and GAF, for interactive use directly from disk. GBZ-base extracts local subgraphs efficiently, and GAF-base extracts all alignments to a subgraph and is the smallest sequence-to-graph alignment format.
key_points: Indexed, disk-based access instead of batch loading.
Fast local subgraph extraction.
The smallest sequence-to-graph alignment file format.

posts.title: mChIP-seq for multiplex epigenomic profiling uncovers cancer-specific histone features in cellular and circulating nucleosomes
posts.authors: Sun C, Zhang Q, Yan J, et al.
posts.summary: A multiplexed ChIP-seq method that uses one-step sample indexing and a pool-and-split strategy, and works on cellular and cell-free samples. It profiled H2A.Z and 10 histone marks across nine cancer cell lines, and the cell-free version showed distinct cfDNA fragment patterns in breast cancer plasma versus healthy controls.
key_points: Cheaper and more efficient multiplexed profiling.
H2A.Z and H3K4me3 correlate less at promoters in cancer cells.
cf-mChIP-seq is a liquid-biopsy approach.

posts.title: Patient Sociodemographic Factors Impact the Breast Cancer Microenvironment
posts.authors: DeWitt JT, Jimenez-Tovar D, Oropeza E, et al.
posts.summary: A new HR+ breast cancer transcriptomic dataset enriched for Black patients, controlled for healthcare access and education. Tumours from Black women showed more collagen deposition and unfavourable T-cell signatures, which were more strongly tied to poverty burden than to race or ancestry, with STAT4 as a candidate master regulator.
key_points: A transcriptomic resource that fills a representation gap.
Collagen deposition patterns are partly tumour-cell intrinsic.
The poverty-associated immune phenotype is replicated across independent datasets.

posts.title: Early and accurate detection of ovarian cancer by profiling cell-free mitochondrial DNA fragmentomics in multi-ethnic population
posts.authors: Guo X, Gong Z, Li Z, et al.
posts.summary: A multi-centre machine-learning study using plasma cell-free mtDNA fragmentomics. The detection model reached AUC 0.987 in training and above 0.979 in validation, and a second model separates malignant from benign adnexal masses (AUC 0.982).
key_points: 91.67% sensitivity for stage I at 95% specificity.
The benign-versus-malignant model outperforms serum biomarkers.
Performs well in a Chinese minority cohort.

posts.title: Phenotype-cloud reorganization shapes cancer progression and therapeutic adaptation
posts.authors: Zhang Y, Ji J, Gao M, et al.
posts.summary: A graph-neural-network progression coordinate plus Field-Flow-Front analysis of breast cancer finds a fragmented intermediate state that stabilises into an interface-remodelling Front. Chemotherapy depletes the pretreatment phenotype cloud and enriches convergent survivor states, and pan-cancer dependency analysis points to an integrin-FAK vulnerability.
key_points: Proliferation and invasion programmes decouple during progression.
The transition is recovered across molecular, protein and functional systems.
Survivor-state accessibility is partly encoded before treatment.

posts.title: Extrachromosomal circular DNA formation follows a 10.5-bp periodicity reflecting the minor groove orientation around nucleosomes
posts.authors: Zabala A, Ascension AM, Bagger FO, et al.
posts.summary: Short-time Fourier transform of eccDNA length distributions across 25 datasets resolves ~180 bp and 10.5 bp periodicities. Breakpoints fall preferentially in linker DNA and where the minor groove faces the histone surface.
key_points: Chromatin geometry is a determinant of eccDNA biogenesis.
The analysis spans multiple species, tissues and assays.
It gives a structural basis for eccDNA length periodicity.

posts.title: GOLDEN: Gene expression and allele-informed decomposition for genetic heterogeneity in spatial transcriptomic data
posts.authors: Paik H
posts.summary: An allele-aware multitask network classifies spots as target, non-target or mixed and estimates target fractions in spatial transcriptomics. On synthetic benchmarks built from semi-allogeneic single-cell profiles it reaches r = 0.977 and MAE 0.045.
key_points: It resolves interindividual (non-clonal) mixtures at spot level.
Predictions are consistent on real spatial data and genetically validated.
A simulation framework is released.

posts.title: Calibration of AlphaGenome Variant Impact and SpliceAI2 scores as PP3/BP4 evidence for missense, non-coding, and synonymous variants
posts.authors: Babazade A, Dolas Y, Duzenli T, et al.
posts.summary: Calibrates the AlphaGenome Variant Impact score and SpliceAI2 as graded ACMG PP3/BP4 evidence for missense, non-coding and synonymous variants. Both reach moderate to strong evidence near exons, and the evidence thresholds depend on whether ClinVar benign classes or population variants serve as controls.
key_points: AlphaGenome's score does not beat its AlphaMissense component for missense variants.
SpliceAI2 discriminates better in two classes and in a splicing assay.
ClinVar likely-benign counts changed ~60-fold at 20 nt from the exon without a change in measured splicing.

posts.title: Optimal transport reveals unresolved cells in single cell multi-omics
posts.authors: Piran M, Vafaee F
posts.summary: An explicit optimal-transport coupling between modalities scores per-cell match uncertainty and upgrades existing integration and label-transfer tools without retraining. It was evaluated on 78 dataset pairs covering 10 integration and 10 label-transfer tools.
key_points: The ambiguity score gave the larger, more consistent gain than the coupling itself.
Removing ambiguous cells beat random removal in 98% of integration tests and 91% of label-transfer tests.
Ambiguous cells are mostly rare or transitional populations.

posts.title: A clinically annotated proteomic and histological resource of 1,000 colorectal cancers
posts.authors: Qoku A, Ullrich N, Miranda F, et al.
posts.summary: Deep proteomics of 1,000 treatment-naive colorectal cancers defines six proteomic subgroups, splitting the chromosomally unstable class into three, including an indolent group and a rare adverse-outcome group. Subgroups transfer to an independent cohort, and the paired slide images set benchmarks for inferring subgroup from morphology.
key_points: It is the largest proteomically profiled CRC cohort to date.
Subgroups associate with outcome, chemotherapy-associated survival, drivers and predicted drug response.
All data are stated as released openly.

posts.title: Developmental origins of thymic B-cell lymphomas
posts.authors: Rai S, Yin Y, Fujisawa M, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell multiomics and spatial profiling define a thymus-specific CCL17 and germinal-centre-like B-cell differentiation programme, recreated in vitro. A malignant state in primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma (PMBCL) shares its features and sits at early clonal positions in B-cell-receptor phylogenies.
key_points: The B-cell trajectory is distinct from canonical germinal-centre differentiation.
The programme is redeployed during thymic B-cell lymphomagenesis.
The finding extends across human B-cell lymphomas.

posts.title: METTL1 gene dosage and catalytic activity define a targetable vulnerability in pediatric cancers
posts.authors: Liu PY, He S, Panasenko O, et al.
posts.summary: METTL1 copy-number gain and high expression mark METTL1-dependent paediatric tumours. Cas13-mediated mRNA degradation impairs colony formation and lowers translation efficiency of genes enriched in codons decoded by m7G-modified tRNAs.
key_points: Catalytic activity is required to rescue cells from METTL1 silencing.
MYC, MYCN and MCL-1 proteins fall on METTL1 loss.
It synergises with BCL-xL inhibition.

posts.title: RNA m6A mediates de novo DNA methylation and heritable epigenetic silencing in human cells
posts.authors: Divekar NS, Phan NT, Palma LG, et al.
posts.summary: Genome-wide CRISPR screens and proximity proteomics show the m6A writer complex is recruited to chromatin with DNA methyltransferases and histone repressors during establishment of heritable silencing. Inhibiting m6A during the pluripotent transition impairs de novo DNA methylation and derepresses transposable elements.
key_points: It links the epitranscriptome to the establishment of DNA methylation.
The m6A writer is recruited to chromatin during the transient establishment phase.
TE upregulation threatens genome integrity during early development.

posts.title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics
posts.authors: Martínez-de-Morentin X, Khan SA, Maillo A, et al.
posts.summary: The authors benchmark 11 image-based, transcriptomics-based and multimodal cell segmentation methods on 15 datasets from 5 spatial transcriptomics technologies, covering 12 human and mouse tissue types. They introduce biologically informed metrics for segmentation quality, transcript recovery, cell composition, morphology, expression purity and spatial organisation.
key_points: Performance varies substantially across datasets, technologies and evaluation criteria, with trade-offs between segmentation completeness, transcriptomic fidelity and biological interpretability.
Segmentation choice shapes downstream results, including cell-type specificity, transcript contamination and ligand-receptor inference.
A unified Nextflow pipeline supports standardised evaluation and method selection.

figure.caption: The same tissue with the same transcripts is segmented three ways (image-based, transcript-based, multimodal), giving different cell boundaries that are scored on recovery, purity, composition and spatial layout.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: High false sign rates in transcriptome-wide association studies
posts.authors: Gerlach PA, Milind N, Spence JP, et al.
posts.summary: The authors measure how often transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) get the direction of a gene's effect wrong. They use plasma protein levels, where more expression should mean more protein, and loss-of-function burden tests for complex traits as references for the expected sign.
key_points: TWAS showed a false sign rate of 23% for plasma proteins and 33% for complex traits.

The proposed cause is eQTLs in non-trait-relevant tissues that tag haplotypes carrying distinct, tightly linked regulatory variants that drive the GWAS signal, so the right gene is flagged with an unreliable sign.
TWAS-based direction-of-effect estimates should be interpreted with caution, and the reliability of TWAS more broadly is questioned.

figure.caption: An eQTL in another tissue is tightly linked to the GWAS variant, so TWAS borrows the eQTL's expression sign and can call the right gene with the wrong direction compared with a loss-of-function test.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: CauTrigger: deciphering biological system state transitions by hierarchical causal decomposition
posts.authors: Zhang C, Cai D, Aihara K, et al.
posts.summary: CauTrigger is a hierarchical deep latent variable model that uses do-calculus to find causal triggers of state transitions and predict perturbation outcomes across several regulatory layers. It separates causal from spurious latent factors to rebuild the regulatory hierarchy from observational data.
key_points: It outperforms existing methods at identifying causal triggers and forecasting system-level responses on synthetic and real datasets with multilayer regulatory structure.
Applied to single-cell multi-omics and gut microbiome data, it prioritises candidate triggers and uses in silico perturbations to generate testable hypotheses.
The authors present it as a general-purpose framework for causal discovery in complex biological systems.

figure.caption: Observed state changes are confounded, so a marker looks linked to the state while the true trigger acts through layered regulators, and in silico perturbation of the trigger predicts the shift.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
posts.authors: Nimo J, Fritzsche S, Valdes DS, et al.
posts.summary: openDVP is an open-source end-to-end workflow for deep visual proteomics (cell-type-specific, spatially resolved proteomics). It combines MCMICRO, QuPath and napari with scverse formats (AnnData, SpatialData) and offers a fast-track pipeline and an AI-powered pipeline for segmentation and spatial analysis.
key_points: It was applied to three archival tissue studies: human placenta, early-stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer.
Spatial single-cell phenotypes are integrated with exploratory proteomic measurements.
The authors introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighbourhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

posts.title: Multiomic characterization of microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer reveals distinct biology and targetable vulnerabilities
posts.authors: Sadanandam A, O'Farrell AC, Miller IS, et al.
posts.summary: The study integrates multiomic data from about 2,000 tumour samples, including 316 microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancers not profiled before, with about 4,500 molecular profiles and 195,246 single cells or nuclei. A machine-learning tool, iPhenMap, links the molecular programs to phenotype.
key_points: It reveals programs including replication stress, right-sided biology, glutaminolysis-driven metabolic reprogramming, and MYC-E2F networks tied to epigenetic remodelling and perineural invasion.
In RAS-mutant MSS CRC, tumoroid and xenograft models support FAK, PDK1/2 and proteasome inhibition combined with MEK blockade.

posts.title: Molecular functions, cellular responses and pathological implications of the RNA modification N6-methyladenosine
posts.authors: Kang Z, Zhang F, Ming G-L, et al.
posts.summary: A review of the m6A RNA modification: how writers and erasers set it, how readers turn it into effects on splicing, stability, localisation and translation, and how it reaches chromatin function. It covers cellular stress responses, metabolism and antitumour immunity.
key_points: m6A deposition is shaped by chromatin environment, transcription and RNA processing.
Dysregulated m6A is linked to brain disorders and cancer.
The review highlights small-molecule inhibitors and precise editing technologies as translational prospects and outlines remaining challenges.

posts.title: Conventional Skull Base Chordoma in a Ugandan Adult Male, Presenting with Prolonged Headache: A Case Report
posts.authors: Okello MM, Mutumba M, Kalungi S, et al.
posts.summary: Case report of a 49-year-old man with more than a year of progressive headache and one episode of facial numbness. CT showed a destructive midline skull base mass involving the sphenoid and ethmoid sinuses, and biopsy was consistent with conventional chordoma.
key_points: Immunohistochemistry was positive for EMA, pan-cytokeratin and S100 and negative for CK7, CK20 and CD34, with a Ki-67 index below 5%.
Brachyury staining was unavailable, which the authors note as a limitation.
Surgery was planned but the patient was lost to follow-up; the authors stress prompt imaging for prolonged headache in resource-limited settings.

posts.title: scTHREAD: a cell-resolved long-read transcriptome database with linked isoform, poly(A), junction, and allelic evidence
posts.authors: Fu ZC, Yan Y, Wu C, et al.
posts.summary: scTHREAD is an open database of single-cell long-read transcriptomes: 453 runs from 34 human and mouse datasets, 923,389 cells profiled on Oxford Nanopore and PacBio. A uniform workflow keeps isoform, poly(A)-site, splice-junction and allele-aware counts linked to their study, run, cell type and cell.
key_points: It catalogues 12,471,531 run-transcript observations, 30% carrying one of 210,341 distinct Ensembl transcript IDs, with precomputed differential usage where coverage allows.
It recapitulates known cell-type-specific isoform patterns and finds reproducible monocyte versus T-cell differences in CCND3, CUTA and PSMB8 junction usage across three cohorts and two technologies.
Data are available through a web interface, bulk downloads and an API.

posts.title: LRP2: A proteogenomics pipeline for long-read informed protein isoform analysis and discovery
posts.authors: Schertzer MD, Lewandowski JT, Watts EF, et al.
posts.summary: LRP2 is a modular Nextflow pipeline that takes long-read RNA-seq through isoform discovery, ORF prediction, peptide identification and protein inference, to test which RNA isoforms are translated into stable proteins.
key_points: It scales transcript discovery to hundreds of samples with PacBio Isocall, cleans artefacts with SQANTI QC and classifies predicted proteomes with CPAT and SQANTI Protein.
It runs differential expression and usage analysis with edgeR, DRIMSeq and a long-read adaptation of LeafCutter, and adds DDA and DIA mass-spectrometry evidence through FragPipe.
Deterministic splice-junction identifiers allow cross-dataset comparison of novel isoforms.

posts.title: SomatiX: accurate and efficient somatic SNV detection from matched tumor-normal long-read DNA sequencing
posts.authors: Liu Z
posts.summary: SomatiX is a deep-learning caller for somatic SNVs from matched tumour-normal long-read DNA sequencing, built on an allele-aware pileup representation.
key_points: It beat DeepSomatic and ClairS in F1 across most Oxford Nanopore benchmark conditions and was competitive on PacBio data.
On held-out chromosome 1 cancer cell-line benchmarks (at least 3 supporting reads, VAF at least 0.05), mean F1 was 0.986 for ONT and 0.988 for PacBio.
It was strongest for low-VAF SNVs on ONT data, with a compact model and the fastest runtime of the tools compared.

posts.title: Long-read RNA sequencing identifies non-coding isoform switching as a regulator of cell fate
posts.authors: Fort V, Khelifi G, He R, et al.
posts.summary: Long-read RNA sequencing during somatic cell reprogramming identifies new isoforms and shows tight regulation of non-coding isoforms across cell state transitions.
key_points: A novel long non-coding RNA, Snhg26, switches isoform during reprogramming and enhances conversion towards the pluripotent state.
Knock-down of Snhg26 in mouse and human pluripotency models shows it is important for acquiring pluripotency.
The work provides a resource on full-length isoform usage during cell fate change.

posts.title: DR-GEM enables self-supervised machine learning for single-cell embeddings and annotations
posts.authors: Yeh CY, Sun MW, Zhu D, et al.
posts.summary: DR-GEM is a self-supervised meta-algorithm for single-cell and spatial embeddings that uses reconstruction error to redirect the model towards patterns it missed, followed by balanced consensus learning. The authors argue existing methods equate abundance with importance and miss rare cell types and states.
key_points: It outperforms existing methods at recovering rare cell types, filtering noise and mitigating cell-level and patient-level underrepresentation.
It was tested on synthetic and real single-cell, spatial transcriptomics and Perturb-seq data, including uncovering held-out genetic and spatial features.

posts.title: simPIC: flexible simulation of single-cell ATAC-seq paired-insertion counts from individuals to populations
posts.authors: Chugh S, Shim H, McCarthy DJ
posts.summary: simPIC is a fast, memory-efficient simulator of single-cell ATAC-seq paired-insertion counts across individuals and populations. It models cell groups, batch effects and genotype-dependent accessibility so population-scale methods such as chromatin accessibility QTL mapping can be tested against known ground truth.
key_points: Across multiple datasets and cell types it closely matches real data distributions.
It scales to cohort sizes that current simulation tools cannot handle.

posts.title: scSpatial: an atlas for single-cell spatial omics
posts.authors: Sun H, Bei Y, Zhu Z, et al.
posts.summary: scSpatial is an atlas of single-cell spatial omics with expert-curated cell annotations and spatial mappings, freely accessible without login.
key_points: It curates over 1,800 tissue sections from 630 projects across 16 spatial technologies, with more than 20 million spatially resolved cells annotated to 173 Cell Ontology types.
It offers spatial gene expression atlases, cell-type distribution maps, spatially variable genes, expression correlations and pathway-level spatial activity.

posts.title: High-throughput droplet-based enzymatic DNA methylome profiling enables single-cell resolution of epigenetic heterogeneity
posts.authors: Li G, Yang Y, Li Z, et al.
posts.summary: scEM-seq is a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome method that ligates barcodes in one emulsification step and converts cytosines after emulsification, reducing DNA loss compared with bisulfite-based approaches.
key_points: It profiles tens of thousands of single cells per experiment with moderately improved CpG coverage compared with other droplet-based methods.
In peripheral blood it resolves major immune lineages; in prostate cancer tissue it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures.

posts.title: The revised diploid genome sequence of an individual human: A workflow for near telomere-to-telomere assemblies using only Oxford Nanopore Technologies Simplex-reads
posts.authors: Lok S, Lau TNH, Tong AHY, et al.
posts.summary: HuRef2.0 revises the first diploid human genome assembly using only Oxford Nanopore Simplex reads and hifiasm, with a workflow that gets close to telomere-to-telomere continuity from standard DNA without ultra-long reads or proximity ligation.
key_points: Three flowcells (about 103x) gave 26 contigs with 23 chromosomes gapless and a final T2T assembly after local assembly of two ChrY gaps, with base accuracy above Q60 and an NG50 of 2.36 Mb for phase blocks.
A single flowcell (about 35x) still gave an assembly more contiguous than GRCh38.p14, and PacBio HiFi reads gave less contiguous assemblies than error-corrected ONT reads at equal coverage.

posts.title: Single-cell TimeLapse-seq reveals MTA is an essential retrotransposon orchestrating mouse zygotic genome activation
posts.authors: Wu Y, Shi H, Yan R, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell TimeLapse-seq (scTL-seq) detects allele-resolved nascent RNA in individual mouse embryos, giving a transcriptional atlas of genes and transposable elements during zygotic genome activation.
key_points: Transcription at the pronuclear stage is largely maternal, and Mouse Transcripts type-A (MTA) elements are transcribed in oocytes and highly active at that stage.
MTA knockdown disrupts zygotic gene activation, dysregulates hundreds of TE subfamilies and arrests embryos at the 1-cell stage.
The authors identify 662 TE-driven chimeric transcripts and propose maternal factors such as NOBOX as MTA regulators.

posts.title: Reference-free isoform discovery links unannotated RNA processing to disease risk
posts.authors: Buen Abad Najar CF, Xie D, Feng R, et al.
posts.summary: Torino is a computational framework that learns RNA processing patterns directly from population-scale RNA-seq by non-negative matrix factorisation of coverage variation across samples, without transcript annotations.
key_points: Across seven vertebrate species it found hundreds of genes with conserved tissue-biased coverage patterns, and it captures intronic coverage consistent with intron retention that junction-based methods miss.
In GTEx, QTL mapping found thousands of coverage-pattern QTLs, many colocalising with disease risk loci.
In 1,193 brain samples it shows widespread increased intron retention in Alzheimer's disease, including a risk variant raising intron retention in KNOP1.

posts.title: corrdeconv corrects deconvolution's misreading of disease cell states as abundance, overturning benchmarks and outperforming every published deconvolution method
posts.authors: Jiang H, Gao F, Liu P, et al.
posts.summary: The authors argue that cell abundances inferred by deconvolution of bulk RNA, DNA methylation and spatial data are not measurements, because disease-state shifts can create, erase or reverse inferred cell changes. They propose corrdeconv, which chooses corrections by count-refuted effects and gene-list errors.
key_points: Same-person measurements from 8,465 people and specimens in 26 diseases refuted 1,119 of 2,660 blood disease effects from 28 methods (42%), most of which passed per-sample correlation.
In the R4RA trial, histology replaced 13 of 20 patients in the tocilizumab-favoured subgroup and erased the drug-by-B-cell interaction.
corrdeconv ranked first against every published method scored, with 46% fewer refuted effects than the DREAM winner without target-cohort counts.

posts.title: REFCON: Reference-free and robust copy number inference in single-cell tumor transcriptomes
posts.authors: Gencturk MM, Cicek AE
posts.summary: REFCON is a deep-learning model that infers copy number from each cell's own expression, without comparing against a reference of normal cells, which avoids results that depend on which cells are analysed together.
key_points: It was evaluated on more than 410,000 held-out cells from cell lines, organoids and 112 tumours of nine cancer types across seven technologies.
It agreed more closely with single-cell DNA than existing methods, was unaffected by sample composition and labelled far fewer normal cells as aneuploid.
In patient-derived organoids with no normal cells it gave consistent profiles across passages and tracked clonal evolution.

posts.title: Whole-genome sequencing reveals tumor T-cell infiltration associated with immunotherapy outcomes
posts.authors: Usset JL, Lee HW, Jones R, et al.
posts.summary: The CIDER T-cell score estimates tumour T-cell infiltration from whole-genome sequencing by counting unique reconstructed T-cell receptor CDR3 sequences, tested in 8,275 metastatic tumours from the Hartwig cohort.
key_points: It agreed with an RNA-based T-cell signature (r = 0.80) and the DNA-based ImmuneLENS metric (r = 0.92).

In 647 immune checkpoint inhibitor-treated patients, higher scores were associated with response and better overall survival (HR 0.56), with weaker or no association in 2,432 untreated patients, pointing to a predictive effect.
It is nearly uncorrelated with tumour mutational burden (r = 0.035) and improves stratification when combined with it.

posts.title: Unimeth: A unified transformer framework for accurate DNA methylation detection from nanopore reads
posts.authors: Wang S, Xiao Y, Tao S, et al.
posts.summary: Unimeth is a transformer framework that jointly processes raw nanopore signals and basecalled sequences to predict 5mC and 6mA at all target sites in read patches, trained in signal pre-training, methylation fine-tuning and site-level calibration phases.
key_points: It was evaluated on public and in-house data from 14 organisms, R9.4.1 and R10.4.1 chemistries, and wild-type, mutant and enzyme-treated samples.
It improved plant non-CpG 5mC detection, reduced false positives in low-methylation samples and kept performance for 5mCpG; it was also validated on an Alzheimer's disease brain sample.
For 6mA it reduced background calls while retaining signal for nucleosome profiling.

posts.title: Individual-level expression deconvolution and assessment of cross-sample variation
posts.authors: Kang K, Xie K
posts.summary: CDSeq2 combines reference-informed Bayesian deconvolution with gene-type prioritisation to estimate individual-level cell-type expression from bulk RNA-seq.
key_points: In brain benchmarks it gave accurate RNA-fraction estimates and recovery in excitatory neurons comparable to BayesPrism.
Prioritisation supported continuous-phenotype and cell-type-specific eQTL analyses; in 40 synthetic cohorts, retaining 40% of candidate profiles raised eQTL precision from 77.6% to 92.6%.

posts.title: Alignment-free discovery of conserved RNA structures in the human genome
posts.authors: Sumi S, Makino K, Onoguchi M, et al.
posts.summary: RLMHelix scores helices in single sequences, before any alignment, using language-model dependencies and thermodynamics, and a distilled version scans the transcribed human genome for candidate conserved RNA structures.
key_points: It ranks known RNAs higher than conventional thermodynamic scanning; two-thirds of 15,821 candidates are new to four earlier genome-wide screens, yet agree with in-cell probing.
Higher scores were associated with more binding by double-stranded RNA-binding proteins in eCLIP data and exploratory pull-downs.

posts.title: A Pan-Cancer Benchmark of Clustering Strategies for Patient-Specific Gene Regulatory Networks
posts.authors: Sarantidis P, Belova T, Kuijjer M
posts.summary: The study benchmarks feature-selection and clustering approaches for patient-specific gene regulatory networks (PANDA and LIONESS) across 9,778 primary tumours from 33 cancer types, comparing gene expression, gene indegrees and full TF-gene edge-weight networks.
key_points: Twenty combinations of four feature-selection methods and five clustering algorithms were evaluated with consensus clustering.
Standard-deviation feature selection with k-means performed best for both network-derived representations while staying computationally efficient.
Network-derived clusters showed clinical, biological and prognostic associations complementary to those from expression alone.

posts.title: CliP: subclonal architecture reconstruction of cancer cells in DNA sequencing data using a penalized likelihood model
posts.authors: Jiang Y, Yu K, Ji S, et al.
posts.summary: CliPP estimates mutation cellular prevalence and fuses compatible estimates into clusters with a pairwise fusion penalty, without fixing the number of clusters, to reconstruct subclonal architecture from bulk DNA sequencing. This is a revised version (v3) of a 2021 preprint.
key_points: It was competitive with PhylogicNDT and PyClone-VI on simulations of 5,256 tumours and much faster, analysing the whole PCAWG and TCGA cohorts in about an hour.
In PCAWG it reached a concordance correlation of 0.93 with the consensus and 96.3% agreement on driver clonal versus subclonal calls.
Applied to 5,424 TCGA tumours across 31 cancer types, it annotates driver clonality for 13,960 high-confidence driver mutations, and a web app is provided.

posts.title: Robust Chromosome Segmentation in Sparse Single-Cell Whole-Genome Sequencing Using a k-Segment Constrained Hidden Markov Model
posts.authors: Ridgley T, Chovanec P, He S, et al.
posts.summary: A k-segment constrained hidden Markov model limits the number of state transitions to call loss of heterozygosity (LOH) from phased heterozygous sites in sparse sci-L3 single-cell whole-genome data.
key_points: Against orthogonal sci-L3-Strand-seq segmentation, it reached 86% LOH recall and 88% precision.
Haplotype-aware analyses supported genuine LOH in 68-78% of sampled apparent false positives, so true precision may approach 96%.

posts.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells
posts.authors: Karbalayghareh A, Pelzer B, Chin CR, et al.
posts.summary: DynaVelo is a generative neural ordinary differential equation model that learns the joint dynamics of gene expression and transcription factor motif activity from single-cell multiome data. It recovers the bifurcating trajectories of wild-type mouse germinal centre B cells and shows how they change when Arid1a or Ctcf is lost.
key_points: Because it learns the vector field, the model can be perturbed in silico, giving cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks that recover known TF-to-gene edges.
In silico perturbation of Arid1a-heterozygous germinal centres nominated Ctcf, Stat3 and Bcl6 as rescue targets.

In vivo experiments in double-heterozygous mice confirmed rescue of the Arid1a-het dark-zone phenotype for all three, and multiome profiling of Arid1a;Ctcf double-hets showed the predicted shift toward wild-type dynamics.

figure.caption: A wild-type germinal centre B-cell trajectory forks into two branches, an Arid1a-het trajectory is shifted off it, and in silico perturbation of Ctcf, Stat3 or Bcl6 predicts rescue that was confirmed in mice.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Genome-wide detection of genotype-environment interactions at biobank scale with fastGxE
posts.authors: Ning C, Zhou X
posts.summary: fastGxE is a scalable genome-wide test for genetic variants whose effects depend on environmental factors. It controls for polygenic effects, polygenic interaction effects and noise heterogeneity, and stays robust to the number of environmental factors involved.
key_points: It is 32.98-126.49 times faster than existing approaches, which makes biobank-scale GxE scans practical.
Applied to 32 physical traits and 67 blood biomarkers in the UK Biobank, it found 7 loci for physical traits (4 novel) and 18 for blood biomarkers (12 novel).
Performance was assessed with extensive simulations as well as the UK Biobank analysis.

figure.caption: Two reaction-norm plots: genotype effects that keep the same gap across environments (main effect only) versus lines that diverge with environment (genotype x environment), the signal fastGxE tests for.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Protein arginine methylation promotes global 3'UTR shortening in proliferating cells
posts.authors: Griffith L, Capitanchik C, Moore S, et al.
posts.summary: Arginine methylation drives global 3'UTR shortening, which promotes oncogenic short isoforms. Inhibiting asymmetric and symmetric dimethylation together reverses the shift in human cancer cell lines, patient-derived organoids and activated mouse T cells.
key_points: Arginine methylation promotes PCF11 association with the cleavage and polyadenylation machinery, allowing efficient processing of weak proximal poly(A) sites.
Affected transcripts have high GC content, large distances between alternative poly(A) sites and a position-dependent sequence code.
The authors suggest the shortening could be used to stratify patients for PRMT-targeting therapies.

figure.caption: With PRMTs active, methylated PCF11 joins the cleavage machinery at a weak proximal poly(A) site and gives a short 3'UTR isoform; with PRMTs inhibited the distal site is used and the long isoform returns.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
posts.authors: Reinkemeier CD, Manero-Carranza M, Farouni R, et al.
posts.summary: The recordanelle is a single-component synthetic organelle, built from a mitochondrial membrane anchor, a condensate assembler and a poly(A)-binding protein, that records the transcriptome in living human cells. It recruits and protects mRNAs for days.
key_points: It can be engineered to sample up to 90% of endogenous mRNAs and protect them over several days.
Transient transcriptional responses from inducible promoters or interferon signalling are preserved over time at the single-cell level.
This gives a non-disruptive, unbiased way to read out a transcriptional history rather than a single snapshot.

posts.title: Genome-wide analyses identify 60 loci associated with liver triglyceride content
posts.authors: Jamialahmadi O, Mowlaei S, Gelev KZ, et al.
posts.summary: A genome-wide association meta-analysis of MRI-derived liver triglyceride content in 71,488 UK Biobank participants of European ancestry roughly doubles the sample size of earlier studies. It identifies 60 independent loci, 31 of them new.
key_points: SNP-based heritability is estimated at 25%, and fine-mapping nominated candidate effector genes at 48 loci; 14 of the 31 new loci replicated in a metabolic liver disease meta-analysis (42,163 cases).
The top versus bottom polygenic risk score decile had 2.71-fold higher odds of cirrhosis and 7.47-fold higher odds of hepatocellular carcinoma.
Plasma proteins linked to the score were enriched for metabolic remodelling and inflammatory pathways.

posts.title: Spatial multi-omic atlas profiles early organogenesis of a Carnegie stage 12 human embryo
posts.authors: Wang LJ, Yang H, Song J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors build spatial transcriptomic and metabolomic maps of a Carnegie stage 12 human embryo, co-registered with embryonic anatomy into one spatial multi-omic framework.
key_points: Unsupervised clustering of the spatial transcriptomic data found 17 cell populations covering the major organ primordia.
The liver primordium contains spatially separable hepatocyte- and cholangiocyte-primed programmes, and cardiac outflow tract and sinoatrial node progenitors were detected.
Integrating gene and metabolite abundance links transcription factors to metabolic pathways in lineage specification.

posts.title: Refining indel- and structural variant-trait associations with LAVrefiner
posts.authors: Xia X, Wu J, Gao Z, et al.
posts.summary: LAVrefiner is a scalable, sequence-aware method that splits overlapping sequence-resolved structural variants and indels into non-overlapping refined components. It outputs genotype matrices that work with standard SNP-based analyses.
key_points: In tandem repeat regions it supports motif-aware allele comparison and repeat copy-number estimation.
Applied to 1000 Genomes variants it produced 224,708 refined variants.

Models combining its copy-number estimates with refined variants gave the highest heritability estimates and prediction accuracy for gene expression in STR and VNTR regions, and eQTL mapping found an independent VNTR signal at TFRC.

posts.title: The Vizitig pangenome and pantranscriptome explorer
posts.authors: Degardins B, Paperman C, Marchet C
posts.summary: Vizitig is a platform for real-time exploration and querying of DNA and RNA sequence de Bruijn graphs across many samples. It builds compacted colored de Bruijn graphs from raw reads and references and serves them through an interactive web interface.
key_points: A query language combines sequences of any size, genomic features such as gene or exon IDs, and experimental factors such as sample or abundance thresholds.
On-demand subgraph loading lets it handle up to 20 assembled human haplotypes on a laptop.
Case studies recover fusion transcript breakpoints from long and short reads and explore variation in yeast, rice, nematode and human pangenomes.

posts.title: XenoMix: Estimating mouse content from DNA methylation data of Patient-Derived Xenograft models
posts.authors: Esmaeelpour N, Mücke O, Altun G, et al.
posts.summary: XenoMix is a light-weight R tool that quantifies mouse DNA contamination in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) samples directly from DNA methylation microarray data, using the sequence homology between human and mouse genomes.
key_points: On ground-truth mixtures the estimates correlate with the truth at Pearson r above 0.99.
In real PDX data it found varying contamination from biological and technical sources.
The estimated contamination can be added as a confounder in downstream analyses; it is also a module in RnBeads.

posts.title: ARCHER-LD: Rapid Long-Range Linkage Disequilibrium Calculations at Biobank Scale using GPU Acceleration
posts.authors: Kumar R, Singhal P, Zhang D, et al.
posts.summary: ARCHER-LD uses multi-GPU distributed computing to calculate R2 for every variant pair in a dataset, so LD can come from a study's own samples rather than external reference panels.
key_points: On chromosome 22 of 30x 1000 Genomes WGS, eight consumer GPUs took under 10 minutes versus over 80 minutes for PLINK on a 64-thread CPU (about 8x).
In the Penn Medicine Biobank, chromosome 1 took 49 minutes versus 22.7 hours with PLINK (about 28x).
The full LD matrix of the 30x 1000 Genomes data (about 120 million variants) was computed in under 6 hours on 512 A100 GPUs.

posts.title: MR-MAS: an end-to-end multi-agent system for autonomous Mendelian randomization analysis
posts.authors: Wei W, Fan Y, Li L, et al.
posts.summary: MR-MAS is an automated Mendelian randomization system built on a multi-agent LLM architecture. It links data acquisition, causal effect estimation, interpretation and manuscript drafting into one workflow, backed by a structured Mendelian Randomization Knowledge Base.
key_points: Across test scenarios it ran stably and reproduced several literature-supported causal signals.
Causal estimates were consistent across repeated runs and different model backends.
Knowledge-base guidance improved trait retrieval and code repair.

posts.title: Learning chemical-induced gene expression perturbations with WAVE
posts.authors: Lv T, Chen B, Dai X, et al.
posts.summary: WAVE is a deep learning framework (a beta-variational autoencoder) that predicts chemical-induced gene expression profiles from drug structure plus the basal transcriptional state of bulk cell lines or single cells.
key_points: It predicts profiles for compound and cell-line combinations that were never tested, supporting in silico perturbation screens.
It is used for drug discovery and repurposing.
In lung adenocarcinoma it identified potentially effective compounds.

posts.title: HRDPath: an explainable multi-model deep learning architecture for predicting homologous recombination deficiency from histopathology
posts.authors: Wu CI, Banda K, Arora R, et al.
posts.summary: HRDPath is a patient-level deep learning model that predicts homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) status in high-grade serous tubo-ovarian carcinoma from whole slide images, with no extra molecular testing.
key_points: Across three cohorts it reaches an AUC of 0.846; using multiple slides per patient and targeted optimisation lifts sensitivity and specificity to 0.90.
An interpretability pipeline links HRD-positive tumours to morphological changes at cell and tissue level.
It is proposed as an accessible digital biomarker where genomic HRD tests are costly or slow.

posts.title: ImmunEscpMap: a gene-centered knowledgebase for immune escape in cancer and viral infection
posts.authors: Jiang S, Ma S, Feng Y, et al.
posts.summary: ImmunEscpMap is a gene-centred knowledgebase that puts cancer and viral-infection evidence into one immune-escape framework, to help prioritise genes from fragmented databases, literature and omics studies.
key_points: The release holds 55,711 gene-evidence records (53,911 from 37,193 PubMed articles and 1,800 from 709 GEO accessions) covering 667 genes.
Evidence is organised into eight immune-escape mechanisms and 14 viral contexts; the cancer branch integrates multi-omics and clinical outcomes.
A web interface offers search, browsing, gene pages and bulk download.

posts.title: Actionable genetic landscape and dynamics in circulating DNA from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer
posts.authors: Leshchiner I, Medford AJ, Cha J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors study 15,564 Guardant360 cell-free DNA samples from 12,827 patients with metastatic breast cancer, assigning samples to subtypes with a trained random forest model.
key_points: Most patients carry variants tied to therapy resistance or targetability, including PIK3CA, ESR1, PTEN and AKT1.
Frequencies of several actionable alterations differ from primary disease, and multiple variants per gene suggest independent resistant clones.
The cohort size allows analysis of allele co-existence, exclusivity and allele-fraction correlations.

posts.title: Pseudouridylation landscape across 42 nuclear-encoded tRNAs
posts.authors: Barry ML, Abu-Shumays RL, Barnes LE, et al.
posts.summary: The authors annotate pseudouridine sites in budding yeast tRNAs with nanopore direct RNA sequencing of seven pseudouridine synthase knockouts and with BACS chemical sequencing.
key_points: Nanopore data confirmed 32 existing sites and predicted 10 new ones; BACS confirmed all 10 and found 11 more.
The combined map covers 126 sites (21 novel) and the enzymes responsible across all 42 nuclear tRNA isoacceptors.
Mass spectrometry and primer extension showed no change at position 37 on Pus3 loss, although nanopore signal changed there, a caution for reading direct RNA signal changes.

posts.title: Scale-resolved correlation functions unify spatial omics across platforms and resolutions
posts.authors: Ilin M, Singh Y, Mages SW, et al.
posts.summary: SCOTE (Spatial COvariance TEnsors) quantifies the spatial relationships of all feature pairs across all length scales, from molecule coordinates or binned counts. It separates platform artefacts from biology across spatial omics technologies.
key_points: Platform artefacts show up as scale-localised features.
Molecule-level functions resolved a knockout effect in mouse spleen that cell-level analysis missed.
A billion-molecule whole-transcriptome section runs in 26 minutes on one GPU; tissue area and replicates, not molecule depth, set the statistical error.

posts.title: On technical biases in imaging spatial transcriptomics
posts.authors: Chen C, Borm LE, Pascual-Reguant A, et al.
posts.summary: The authors sort biases in imaging spatial transcriptomics into experimental sources (preservation, spatial sampling) and computational ones (z-stack registration, field-of-view stitching). Using public datasets they show how these biases compound.
key_points: The taxonomy covers the whole measurement pipeline.
They propose a unified count-modelling framework for the sources of variance.
They call for better experimental design and knowledge sharing.

posts.title: Benchmarking large-scale single-cell RNA-seq analysis
posts.authors: Billato I, Pages H, Carey V, et al.
posts.summary: The authors benchmark Seurat, OSCA, scrapper, Scanpy and rapids_singlecell on datasets of 1.3 and 4.2 million cells, plus four labelled datasets for clustering accuracy. They also compare six SVD algorithms for PCA and CPU versus GPU runs.
key_points: The GPU method (rapids_singlecell) was 15 times faster than the best CPU method.
OSCA and scrapper had the highest clustering accuracy (ARI up to 0.97).
Choice of highly variable genes and the PCA implementation drive most of the differences.

posts.title: DCSMAP: A Hybrid Linear-Pangenome Framework for Accurate and Efficient Read Alignment
posts.authors: Yang Q, Wan R, Gong C, et al.
posts.summary: DCSMAP aligns reads linearly, then uses an XGBoost classifier to pick unreliable reads and remap them to a personalised pangenome graph, followed by indel realignment. About 14.8% of read pairs are remapped.
key_points: Across 17 GIAB runs, variant-calling errors fell 46.7% versus BWA-MEM2 and 8.4% versus vg personalised pangenome alignment.
Reference bias is comparable to full pangenome alignment.
It is 2 to 2.5 times faster than the personalised-pangenome workflow.

posts.title: LongVerse: verified AI agents for Nanopore and PacBio DNA methylation analysis
posts.authors: Liu Y, Zhang Q, Li S
posts.summary: LongVerse agents turn one English sentence into haplotype-resolved DNA methylation calls from Nanopore or PacBio reads by supplying arguments to a pinned pipeline, with no code written. On HG002, agent and expert calls were identical.
key_points: Agent and expert calls were byte-identical (r = 1.000) and agreed with bisulfite sequencing (r = 0.943 and 0.884).
Runs cost $0.12 to $0.54.
A consensus agent that admits any per-site caller cut error by 10.7% against the best published caller.

posts.title: Fast and accurate resolution of ecDNA sequence using Cycle-Extractor
posts.authors: Faizrahnemoon M, Luebeck J, Hung KL, et al.
posts.summary: Cycle-Extractor takes a breakpoint graph built from short or long reads and extracts the cycle with the maximum length-weighted copy number, using a mixed-integer linear program. It is compared with CoRAL, Decoil and AmpliconArchitect.
key_points: Accuracy matches CoRAL and beats AmpliconArchitect and Decoil, at about 40 times the speed of CoRAL.
On a PC3 MYC ecDNA, Nanopore data gave a 4.2 Mbp reconstruction versus 690 kbp from short reads.
CRISPR-CATCH confirmed the large ecDNA molecule.

posts.title: ResponseVerdict overturns computationally validated immunotherapy signatures, recovers their missed responders and outperforms every published response predictor
posts.authors: Jiang H, Liu P, Gao F, et al.
posts.summary: The authors re-evaluate 1,566 published immune checkpoint blockade expression signatures in 2,045 treated patients and find no predictive ability (AUC 0.515). They show TIDE orients many signatures the wrong way, and ResponseVerdict orients and selects scores using measured response in other cohorts.
key_points: A median of 44% of random gene sets pass the usual validation.
AUROC is 0.14 higher than TIDE.
The authors report more responders per 100 enrolment slots across trials; the claims are bold, so the methods are worth checking.

posts.title: SPATNIC enables H&E-grounded cancer-cell identification across spatial and single-cell transcriptomic modalities in colorectal cancer
posts.authors: Sakai SA, Nomura R, Ohira M, et al.
posts.summary: SPATNIC is a variational autoencoder that labels single cells as cancer or normal. It is trained on Xenium cells annotated by a pathologist from matched H&E, and matches or beats existing tools in colorectal tumours and liver and lung metastases.
key_points: It transfers zero-shot across Visium, Visium HD, CosMx, Xenium, MERSCOPE and scRNA-seq.
It found a rare POU2F3 tuft-like cancer stem cell population in public atlases, linked to worse survival.
It separates cancer from normal epithelium in rectal cancer before and after chemoradiotherapy, enabling per-patient ADC target screening.

posts.title: WRN deficiency generates oncogenic rearrangements at TA-rich tandem repeats
posts.authors: Wang M, Pan H, Samarkina A, et al.
posts.summary: WRN loss destabilises native, unexpanded TA-rich tandem repeats, which become fragile sites for chromosome breakage and rearrangement. In melanoma this recurrently produces an identical 15.7 Mb deletion that activates TERT.
key_points: The same rearrangement class occurs in WRN-deficient cancers of other types.
The deletion also disrupts CDKN2A/B and NF1.
The work combines genomic analysis of tumours with experiments.

posts.title: Billi: Provably Accurate and Scalable Bubble Detection in Pangenome Graphs
posts.authors: Bhat SG, Mahajan D, Jain C
posts.summary: The authors define panbubble and hairpin bubble formalisations that allow cyclic subgraphs and prove strict nesting. They give an exact algorithm plus a heuristic, implemented in Billi.
key_points: The heuristic scales to HPRC releases 1 and 2.
At the recurrent human Y-chromosome inversion locus, Billi recovers the inversion with its nested variants.
Existing methods miss parts of the variation or misrepresent the nesting.

posts.title: T2G: fast and accurate transcriptome to genome BAM liftover for short and long read RNA sequencing
posts.authors: Rudler DL, Mahmud S, Cleynen A, Shirokikh NE
posts.summary: T2G converts BAM files aligned to the transcriptome back to genome coordinates while keeping CIGAR strings, tags and per-base RNA modification calls. It works for nanopore direct RNA, ribosome footprinting and Illumina RNA-seq.
key_points: Transcriptome alignment plus T2G gave higher on-target specificity and more accurate splice junctions than direct genome alignment.
It removed the systematic assignment of reads to processed pseudogenes (8.5-fold fewer in a reanalysed RBP experiment).
Keeping isoform identity reveals isoform-specific modification levels that genome alignment pools.

posts.title: RiboTxAlign maps and quantifies ribosome footprints using sample-specific transcript references
posts.authors: Ueda H, Kaneda A
posts.summary: RiboTxAlign maps Ribo-seq reads to a compact reference built from sample RNA-seq (StringTie2 assemblies plus GENCODE) and allocates multimapping reads with a two-stage EM. It estimates transcript-level footprint abundance.
key_points: With long-read RNA-seq references, primary genomic placement in simulations was 98.70% (HEK293T) and 95.38% (mouse brain), 17 and 20 points above STAR.
Log TPM correlation with simulation truth was 0.9784 in HEK293T, versus 0.9702 for RiboMap and 0.8844 for DeepShape-prime.
The references were 63.32% (human) and 47.49% (mouse) smaller than GENCODE protein-coding references.

posts.title: Biological and technical spatial variation in spatial transcriptomics
posts.authors: Jackson KC, Gorin G, Pachter L
posts.summary: The authors add a spatially variable capture term to a bursty transcription model, so that biological spatial variation can be separated from technical noise. It is implemented in a program called stipple.
key_points: Spatially variable genes can reflect technical artefacts as well as biological function.
The model distinguishes the two sources of variation.
stipple is shown to help identify and interpret spatial expression variation.

posts.title: Deciphering Spatial Cellular Organization through RNA-Anchored Multi-Omics Deconvolution
posts.authors: Bai Y, Guan X, Xiong S, et al.
posts.summary: SMODER deconvolves spots from spatial multi-omics assays by treating the transcriptome as the main determinant of cell identity and adding protein, chromatin or histone-mark layers in a constrained way.
key_points: It outperformed existing methods in accuracy and spatial coherence in simulations and real protein, chromatin accessibility and histone modification datasets.
It also denoises the extra modalities and allows cell-type-aware analysis of regulatory programs.
Applied to spatial CUT&Tag-RNA-seq and RNA-ATAC-seq, it shows spatially resolved epigenetic repression and cis-regulatory links.

posts.title: Order Matters: Ambient RNA correction confounds doublet detection in single-cell RNA sequencing
posts.authors: Meier M, Howitt G, Grima CV, et al.
posts.summary: Using engineered and multiplexed datasets, the study tests three ambient RNA correction tools (decontX, soupX, CellBender) with up to six doublet detectors. Doublet detection works best when run before ambient RNA correction.
key_points: The exception is CellBender, which did not hurt doublet detection.
decontX and soupX remove proportionally more ambient RNA from doublets, partly masking the doublet signal.
The authors recommend calling doublets first unless CellBender is used.

posts.title: Non-exonic read content reorganises lncRNA co-expression networks in renal and other cancers
posts.authors: Youssef G, Han N
posts.summary: In 1,062 renal cancers, the leading lncRNA co-expression axis tracked the fraction of non-exonic reads at Spearman rho 0.90. Without adjusting for it, most of the lncRNA network merged into one module.
key_points: 9 of 25 TCGA cancer types had a lncRNA-specific axis and 4 showed network collapse.
Intronic lncRNAs tracked the metric more than intergenic ones in all 25 types.
The surviving renal modules added no discrimination over TNM and grade.

posts.title: 2,234 attempts to harmonize a multi-platform B-cell lymphoma bulk transcriptomic dataset: ComBat is superior by cross-batch prediction quality
posts.authors: Nikitin D, Arakelyan A
posts.summary: The study re-scores 2,234 harmonization approaches on 7,174 B-cell lymphoma transcriptomes with 87 metrics grouped into classes. The best approach depends strongly on which metric class is used.
key_points: Leave-one-batch-out prediction of lymphoma subtypes favoured the ComBat family (84 of its top 112 places).
A marker-panel agreement class picked only MNN and Scanorama, which corrupted biology by correlation.
The authors propose a six-step recipe for choosing metric classes and thresholds.

posts.title: Cytoplasmic localization of 5hmC reveals RNA hydroxymethylation in breast cancer
posts.authors: Wen J, Del Bel Belluz L, Ottaviani S, et al.
posts.summary: Immunoassays and digital pathology show a cytoplasmic 5hmC signal in breast cancer cell lines and tissue, and an RNase-sensitive ELISA indicates it reflects hydroxymethylation of total RNA and mRNA.
key_points: The signal was enriched in triple-negative and grade 3 tumours and correlated with cytoplasmic TET2/TET3.
TET3 expression was associated with RNA-processing and spliceosomal transcripts.
TET3 knockdown in three TNBC lines reduced a subset of these targets, supported across 70 DepMap breast lines.

posts.title: PETRO enables robust estimation of on-target perturbation effects in Perturb-seq
posts.authors: Sun Z, Kang H, Keles S
posts.summary: PETRO estimates target-level Perturb-seq effects while allowing an unknown minority of guides to have arbitrary off-target effects, using agreement among replicate guides.
key_points: Sequence-associated off-target bias persisted after pooling cells across guides in CRISPRa and CRISPRi datasets.
In simulations PETRO nearly matched pooling in power without off-target effects, and recovered on-target effects when pooling stayed biased.
In cortical Perturb-seq, most ZNF219 pathway enrichments from pooling rested on a single guide.

posts.title: The landscape of gene loss and missense variation across the mammalian tree informs on gene essentiality
posts.authors: Liao C, Ye R, Ivankovic F, et al.
posts.summary: The authors build two constraint metrics from 462 mammalian genomes: GISMO, which weights gene loss by evolutionary distance to humans, and GISMO-mis, which measures missense constraint across mammals. Both track human constraint estimates yet are independent of coding length, so they pick up essential short genes that human-only metrics miss.
key_points: Both metrics correlate with human loss-of-function, missense and dosage constraint from large sequencing studies.
The most constrained deciles are enriched for rare-variant associations in schizophrenia, autism and neurodevelopmental disorders, and for common-variant heritability.
GISMO also improves prioritisation of recessive disease genes.

figure.caption: Orthologue presence, loss and missense changes across a mammalian tree feed two scores, GISMO (distance-weighted gene loss) and GISMO-mis (missense to synonymous ratio), which flag essential genes including short ones.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Multiancestry conditional and joint analysis applied to GWAS summary statistics
posts.authors: Wang X, Wang Y, Yang J, et al.
posts.summary: Manc-COJO extends conditional and joint analysis to multiancestry GWAS meta-analyses to find statistically independent association signals. In simulations and real data it detects more independent signals with fewer false positives than single-ancestry GCTA-COJO and ad hoc multiancestry adaptations.
key_points: Manc-COJO:FIX is a follow-up algorithm that finds ancestry-specific independent associations.
The C++ implementation is over 120 times faster than GCTA-COJO.
It takes LD references from individual-level genotypes or precomputed matrices, so it works when data sharing is limited.

figure.caption: Summary statistics from three ancestries and an LD reference go into Manc-COJO, which returns independent associations; Manc-COJO:FIX then separates ancestry-specific ones.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing
posts.authors: Lusi RF, Moncayo von Hase S, Model C, et al.
posts.summary: ALTER fuses human AGO2 to a C-to-U deaminase and uses guide RNAs that remodel target RNA structure, giving a programmable RNA editor built on a human protein rather than a Cas13 scaffold. In HEK293T cells it edits mRNA targets about 1.9-fold more than the Cas13 editors CURE and RESCUE.
key_points: Transcriptome-wide RNA-seq shows similar or lower off-target editing than the Cas13 editors.
Machine learning models predict far fewer immunogenic peptides from ALTER.
The system fits a validated AI-directed deimmunisation workflow.

figure.caption: Human AGO2 fused to a deaminase is guided by a guide RNA to a target cytidine in mRNA, converting C to U, in contrast with non-human Cas13 editors.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat
posts.authors: Gómez-Banoy N, Barrero JA, Pinheiro de Carvalho LR, et al.
posts.summary: Using records from 101,243 patients at a cancer centre, the authors define the clinical associations of brown adipose tissue (BAT). A machine learning approach semi-automatically quantified BAT activity in about 8,700 patients.
key_points: Cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT.
Higher BAT activity was linked to lower odds of cardiometabolic disease and healthier white fat distribution.
Angiotensin receptor blocker use was associated with BAT presence, and losartan raised brown adipocyte activity and energy expenditure.

posts.title: Small variant calling in the era of long-read sequencing
posts.authors: Zheng Z, Sedlazeck FJ, Luo R
posts.summary: A review of how deep learning has reshaped small variant calling from long reads, covering germline, de novo, somatic and mosaic variants and both DNA and RNA sequencing. It also covers combinations with alignment-, assembly- and pangenome-based strategies.
key_points: Long reads resolve repetitive regions but have different error profiles from short reads.
The review charts the path to complete telomere-to-telomere profiling of small variants.
It calls for new benchmarking approaches for newly accessible repetitive regions and complex variants.
