posts.title: BEAR-GRN: Systematic assessment of single-cell multi-omics-based gene regulatory network inference methods
posts.authors: Karamveer K, Moeller E, Valensi H, et al.
posts.summary: BEAR-GRN provides standardised datasets, curated ground-truth networks and a unified pipeline for benchmarking gene regulatory network inference from paired scRNA-seq and ATAC-seq. Using it, the authors assess current multi-omics methods in human and mouse cell types.
key_points: Choice of ground truth strongly affects measured performance.
LINGER and DIRECT-NET show the highest overall accuracy and stability.
Current methods are mostly RNA-driven; chromatin accessibility adds limited independent signal.

posts.title: Distilling Direct Effects via Conditional Differential Gene Expression Analysis
posts.authors: Gu J, Skelton A, Staley J, et al.
posts.summary: Across three RNA-seq datasets, including a genome-scale Perturb-seq experiment, only a small fraction of differentially expressed genes have direct effects on the trait. The authors introduce conditional differential expression analysis (CDGE), which tests conditional rather than marginal association for each gene.
key_points: CDGE uses the GhostKnockoff procedure with lasso regression and controls the false discovery rate.
It works on summary statistics from existing DGE pipelines and accommodates batch effects.
CDGE genes mediate the effects of most other DE genes and are more enriched for known interactions and pathways.

posts.title: Integration of polygenic risk with single cell methylation data using met-scDRS
posts.authors: Li X, Shi Z, Hou K, et al.
posts.summary: met-scDRS extends scDRS to integrate GWAS-derived disease genes with single-cell methylomes, scoring disease relevance for each cell. Applied to a public human brain single-cell methylome dataset for 75 traits, it recovers expected cell-type enrichments.
key_points: The method is well calibrated and powered in simulations.
It finds within-cell-type heterogeneity in psychiatric disease risk along the brain spatial axis.
Genes whose methylation tracks disease relevance are enriched in synaptic pathways.

posts.title: Meta-analysis of 990 EBV genomes identifies EBER2 SNP7048 and its interaction with HLA-A*11:01 driving nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk
posts.authors: Wang CY, Yao F, Zhang X, et al.
posts.summary: Whole-genome sequencing of 388 EBV isolates with matched host exomes, plus a meta-GWAS across three cohorts (990 EBV genomes), identifies EBV strains carrying an EBER2 variant (SNP7048) as the main viral determinant of nasopharyngeal carcinoma risk.
key_points: High-risk strains account for about 68% of attributable risk in Southeast Asia and associate with NPC across all cohorts.
Lacking the protective host HLA-A*11:01 allele while carrying a high-risk strain gives a 30.9-fold increase in risk.
Phylogenetic analysis shows the high-risk strains spread geographically.

posts.title: Delocalized DNA holes imprint mutation position in mismatch-repair-deficient cancers
posts.authors: Sung J-Y, Cheong J-H
posts.summary: In mismatch-repair-deficient gastric, colorectal and endometrial tumours, G>T substitutions inside guanine runs fall mostly at the 5' guanine and rarely at the 3' guanine. The profile matches the charge density computed for a delocalized electron hole in DNA without fitting.
key_points: The asymmetry is near identical across the three cancer types and also appears in MMR-knockout cells.
It persists among clonal mutations, and the only free parameter is the transfer integral.
Guanine ionization energy does not predict where C>A substitutions occur.

posts.title: A pan-cancer catalog of mutagenesis at transcription factor binding sites
posts.authors: Sahay H, Duan Y, Gordan R
posts.summary: Somatic mutations from over 4,000 tumours across 15 tissues are used to map mutation patterns at binding sites of 655 transcription factors, grouped into 276 motif clusters. Enrichment is tested at single-nucleotide resolution against sequence and local background mutation rates.
key_points: Nearly a third of TF-cluster and tissue pairs show significant enrichment, most widely in melanoma.
Mutational signatures implicate processes beyond UV, including ageing, deamination, oxidative damage and tobacco.
The catalog helps interpret and prioritise non-coding mutations.

posts.title: Determining cellular phylogeny and migration at high resolution in spatial genomics
posts.authors: Zhang D, Jiang Y, Yu X, et al.
posts.summary: StarTrak calls somatic variants and reconstructs lineages at single-pixel resolution in spatial data. A neural network combines nuclear and mitochondrial mutation evidence, spatial proximity, histology and transcriptomic state to cope with dropouts.
key_points: Works across tissues and spatial platforms, especially spatial ATAC-seq.
In tumour sections it infers migration of mutated cells into adjacent non-malignant tissue and builds region-specific lineage trees.
It finds tumour regions with near-identical transcriptomes but distinct mutational profiles.

posts.title: Variable sparsity non-negative matrix and tensor factorization algorithms and their applications in cancer genomics
posts.authors: Pham T, Zhong J, Hwang J, et al.
posts.summary: vsNMF enforces sparsity explicitly with a projective step on each column of W and row of H after every NMF update, instead of leaving it as a byproduct. Users tune solutions between parts-based overlapping features and partitional soft clustering.
key_points: Improves interpretability of tumour subtypes and pathway activation.
The representations can integrate datasets or define tumour states.
The idea is extended to tensors (vsNTF) with sparsity set per dimension.

posts.title: The Multi-scale Copula Index (MCI): a new information-theoretic measure of association and its applications in functional cancer genomics
posts.authors: Pham T, Meneses-Cime K, Ma J, et al.
posts.summary: MCI is an information-theoretic association measure for cancer omics variables that needs no density estimation or parameter tuning. It targets contextual associations that are strong only in a subset of samples, where Pearson-type methods assume linearity and Gaussianity.
key_points: Claims lower computational cost, more power at small sample sizes and robustness to outliers.
Captures directionality and symmetries in the association.
The Cumulative Entropy Diagram visualises MCI between a reference vector (phenotype, pathway, drug response) and all genomic features.

posts.title: MetaSplice: an ensemble pathogenicity predictor for intronic splice variants
posts.authors: Liu X
posts.summary: MetaSplice is a gradient-boosted ensemble that combines SpliceTransformer and Pangolin predictions with conservation, exon context and gene-level constraint to rank intronic SNVs by pathogenicity. It was trained on 413,199 ClinVar variants and tested on 46,112 newly classified ones.
key_points: Among non-canonical variants it reached an AUPRC of 0.919 versus 0.757 for SpliceAI.
It detected 92.8% of splice-altering variants in experimental splicing assays at a 1.2% false-positive rate.
The author derives a candidate PP3/BP4 rule for ACMG evidence.

posts.title: Predicting cell-state-specific gene regulation from DNA across species
posts.authors: Liu H, Mao S, Gallent T, et al.
posts.summary: Bolero is a sequence-to-function model whose parameters are conditioned on atlas-scale cell-state embeddings, so it predicts cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance from DNA. It was trained on 10.7M cells from 33 datasets across six mammals.
key_points: Matches or exceeds specialised models and resolves closely related cell states.
Extrapolates to cell states absent from training and traces non-coding variant effects to cell types.
Generalises to species excluded from training, with predictions across 84 mammals.

posts.title: Elevated polyadenylated histone gene transcription in human cancer
posts.authors: Paranal RM, Bryson TD, Rios Rios GN, et al.
posts.summary: A quantitative PCR assay in cell lines, backed by more than 1,400 RNA-seq datasets from human cancers, shows pervasive accumulation of polyadenylated histone transcripts, normally restricted to S-phase. More than 70% of patients show tumour-specific increases.
key_points: The alternative processing preferentially enriches histone H2B across more than 8,300 tumours.
Disrupting nuclear components that keep RNAPII at histone genes increases polyadenylated histone transcripts.
S-phase histone genes appear to be transcribed in an unscheduled way during gap phases in cancer.

posts.title: SPEAR: Spatial Epitranscriptomic Analysis by Mass Spectrometry Reveals Localized RNA Modification Remodeling During Glioma Progression
posts.authors: Mateus S, Attina A, Bigot K, et al.
posts.summary: SPEAR couples laser microdissection with a redesigned LC-MS/MS pipeline to quantify dozens of RNA modifications directly from FFPE tissue, from regions as small as 0.1 mm2. It resolved anatomically defined signatures in mouse brain.
key_points: In human diffuse gliomas with low- and higher-grade foci in one specimen, methylated RNA modifications decrease together in higher-grade regions.
The change is masked in bulk analysis and reproducible across patients.

posts.title: X-SPEAR: An Extensible Framework for Spatial Panel Evaluation and Refinement
posts.authors: Patel R, Duong B, Patel V, et al.
posts.summary: X-SPEAR designs targeted gene panels for platforms such as Xenium by combining DART marker selection (short Boolean gene rules trained with detection efficiency in mind) with probe-level off-target assessment.
key_points: On held-out Xenium data from ovarian cancer, mouse brain and cervical cancer, DART beat Wilcoxon, COSG and NS-Forest by 0.04 to 0.18 macro-F1.
It matches the best Wilcoxon accuracy with 42 to 69% fewer genes and is robust to losing single probes.
posts.code: open-source Python package (link not given in abstract)

posts.title: H3K4me1-Mediated Epigenomic Priming of Chemoresistant Tumor States in Ovarian Cancer
posts.authors: Landais Y, Bertorello J, Puerto MP, et al.
posts.summary: Multimodal single-nucleus RNA and histone profiling of longitudinal biopsies from 16 patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer shows that chemoresistant states exist before therapy. Programs that persist or expand under chemotherapy are already enriched for H3K4me1 at baseline.
key_points: Tumours comprise a limited set of functional states that evolve reproducibly under chemotherapy.
Proliferative and IFN-responsive states are depleted, while TNFα- and EMT-associated programs persist or expand.
Baseline tumour composition is associated with survival, and fibroblast remodelling accompanies malignant adaptation.

figure.caption: Before chemotherapy, TNFα- and EMT-associated tumour states already carry H3K4me1; after chemotherapy the IFN and proliferative states are depleted while those primed states persist or expand.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Inherent electrochemical activity of extrachromosomal DNA hub shapes spatial redox environment in nucleus
posts.authors: Qin L, Wu T, Qiao S, et al.
posts.summary: In human cancer cells and mouse models, ecDNA hubs create an electrochemical environment that reduces oxidised glutathione (GSSG) to GSH without an enzyme. The GSH forms a protective cloud around the hubs, shielding ecDNA from damage and sustaining oncogene expression.
key_points: The mechanism was found with metabolomics, biochemistry and imaging assays.
Spermidine, which disrupts the interfacial environment of ecDNA hubs, upsets their redox balance and drives tumour death.
The work describes a self-reinforcing loop that maintains ecDNA in an oxidising tumour nucleus.

figure.caption: An ecDNA hub reduces GSSG to GSH and sits inside a protective GSH cloud; spermidine disrupts the hub interface, the redox balance is lost and tumour cells die.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Spatial Transcriptomics on a Diverse Pancreatic Cancer Cohort Reveals Race-Related Differences in Tumor Subtypes and Immune Microenvironments
posts.authors: Wu Y, Sålas-Escabillas DJ, Xie A, et al.
posts.summary: Whole-exome sequencing, spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics were used to compare pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma in Black African American and Non-African American patients. Driver mutations did not differ, but tumour subtypes and immune microenvironments did.
key_points: Tumours from Black African American patients had fewer classical-subtype cells and more intermediate/hybrid-subtype cells, with no change in basal-like cells.
They also showed more B cell and fewer myeloid cell interactions.
A validation cohort showed larger and more numerous tertiary lymphoid structures in these tumours.

posts.title: Molecular predictors of minimal residual disease in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with quadruplet therapy
posts.authors: Magrangeas F, Cherkaoui M, Bessonneau-Gaborit V, et al.
posts.summary: Genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of 423 newly diagnosed myeloma tumours from the MIDAS trial links molecular features to measurable residual disease (MRD) after Isa-KRd induction. A multimodal random forest predicted MRD status better than clinical or genomic models.
key_points: Whole-genome sequencing found known (APOBEC, chromothripsis) and new genomic instability phenotypes, validated in MMRF.
New driver alterations were validated across three external cohorts (1,451 cases).
DNA methylation defined nine MRD-linked subgroups; the multimodal model reached an AUC of 0.77.

posts.title: A health-system-scale, episode-resolved multimodal atlas of cancer cachexia
posts.authors: Castillon VJ, Xie AX, Boscenco S, et al.
posts.summary: Longitudinal clinicogenomic data from 52,236 MSK-IMPACT patients were repurposed to define episodes of cachectic weight loss and link them to outcomes, serology and tumour genotype. The authors then built a model to predict impending cachexia risk.
key_points: Cachectic episodes cluster near disease progression and predict worse outcomes in nearly all cancer types.
Somatic genotypes, including TP53 mutation across several diseases, were linked to more frequent cachexia.
The model for lung, colorectal and prostate cancer was validated in an external Dana-Farber cohort (n = 5,785).

posts.title: Identification and characterization of neoplastic cells in keratin-positive giant cell-rich tumors
posts.authors: van der Linde M, Chrisinger JSA, Demicco EG, et al.
posts.summary: Single-nucleus RNA sequencing and Xenium spatial transcriptomics were used to find the neoplastic cells of keratin-positive giant cell-rich tumour (KPGCT), a newly described bone and soft tissue tumour. The cells were compared with tenosynovial giant cell tumour.
key_points: A minority population co-expressing keratin and the fusion partners was identified as the likely neoplastic cells, with no synovial markers.
Most of the tumour is macrophages and multinucleated giant cells, pointing to CSF1-CSF1R signalling.
The neoplastic cells show Hippo pathway activation, and the results support testing CSF1R inhibitors.

posts.title: Development of CRISPR/Cas13-based analytical tools to study RNA-protein interactions
posts.authors: Yamamoto K, Shikata S, Hao Y, et al.
posts.summary: The authors combined BiFC, NanoBiT and split-TurboID with RNA-targeting dCas13 to record, monitor and discover RNA-protein interactions. They tested the tools on the NEAT1-NONO interaction in paraspeckles.
key_points: BiFC-dCas13 gives a quantitative fluorescence record of NEAT1-NONO interaction events, and NanoBiT-dCas13 reads out dynamic changes reversibly.
Split-TurboID-dCas13 identified the m6A reader YTHDC1 as a paraspeckle-associated protein.
BiFC-dCas13 was reconfigured to detect other RNA-protein pairs.

posts.title: RNAffinityDB: a curated database of experimental RNA-protein binding affinities
posts.authors: Lin W, Chen Z, Li Y, et al.
posts.summary: RNAffinityDB curates 10,016 construct-resolved RNA-protein binding affinity records from 1,055 publications, each tied to one protein construct and one single-stranded RNA sequence. It is aimed at sequence-affinity analysis and affinity-model development.
key_points: It covers 3,057 protein constructs and 4,638 RNA sequences and keeps non-binding observations.
Records link to UniProt and to AlphaFold 3-predicted complex structures.
The web interface supports retrieval by protein or RNA and semantic queries on function.

posts.title: The PAXT connection is a modifier of rare codon-enriched protein expression
posts.authors: Niehoff T, Peterson J, Li S, et al.
posts.summary: A targeted sgRNA screen with rare- versus common-codon fluorescent reporters identified the PAXT connection, a nuclear complex that sends transcripts to the exosome, as a modifier of rare codon-enriched gene expression.
key_points: Losing a PAXT component raised mRNA levels and stability, and protein output even more, for rare codon reporters.
Transcriptomics and proteomics showed the same preferential rise for endogenous proteins from long, poorly expressed rare-codon mRNAs.
PAXT is proposed as a genetic suppressor of poorly expressed rare-codon genes.

posts.title: DNA-BFN: Bayesian Flow Networks for Generative Modeling of Regulatory DNA Sequences
posts.authors: Yu H, Du Q, Wei L, et al.
posts.summary: DNA-BFN generates regulatory DNA sequences by iteratively updating per-position nucleotide distributions, a diffusion-like process that never adds noise to the discrete sequence.
key_points: It outperformed state-of-the-art baselines across eight regulatory sequence datasets spanning species, scales and lengths.
It preserves sequence feature statistics and regulatory patterns and supports few-shot design.
Sampling is faster than the baselines.

posts.title: scRBP infers cell-specific RNA-binding protein regulons from single-cell transcriptomes at gene and isoform resolution
posts.authors: Ma Y, Tang M, Sriram V, et al.
posts.summary: scRBP infers motif-supported RNA-binding protein regulons from short- and long-read single-cell data at gene and isoform resolution, split by transcript region, and scores their activity per cell.
key_points: Built from 20,746 motifs for 616 RBPs, it recovered targets across 223 ENCODE eCLIP datasets.
Across 30 tissues, 3'UTR-associated stability factors separated from intron-dominant splicing regulators.
In CRISPRi Perturb-seq data, inferred targets were enriched among genes responding to RBP knockdown (161 RBPs).

posts.title: Pan-cancer remodeling of reactive oxygen species homeostasis: distinct roles of the ROS-generation and antioxidant arms in immune context and outcome
posts.authors: Xie K, Xuan Y, Sun R, et al.
posts.summary: A cell-line ROS phenotype measured with a gold-nanocluster array was generalised to public transcriptomes through a 107-gene program, then scored across pan-cancer tumour and normal tissue.
key_points: Generation and antioxidant arms are both up in tumours but dissociate in biology.
The balance score tracks low immune infiltration, carried by low generation-arm activity.
Adverse outcome was attributable to the antioxidant arm, and the program separated tumour from normal in held-out cohorts.

posts.title: ALBIS: simulation of multi-resolution and multi-dimensional spatial transcriptomics data
posts.authors: Matthias JH, Yao J, Hicks SC
posts.summary: ALBIS simulates spatial transcriptomics from an in silico 3D tissue with ground-truth molecule and cell coordinates, then cuts it into 2D sections at cell, bin and spot resolution.
key_points: Several resolutions come from one molecular realisation, so methods can be compared across resolutions.
Spatial domains, cell type composition, batch effects, resolution and tissue scale can be varied.
It is meant for stress-testing spatial methods under known conditions.

posts.title: Mitigating genotype-driven bias improves atlas-scale single-cell DNA methylome profiling
posts.authors: Song X, Diacofotaki A, van der Veer BK, et al.
posts.summary: In pooled single-cell bisulfite data, donor C-to-T variants are misread as unmethylated cytosines. Masking variant positions before methylation quantification reduces this confounding.
key_points: Tested on a sciMET human blood dataset (10 donors, 25,674 nuclei).
Masking lowered donor-associated effects in clustering and cut spurious sample-specific differentially methylated regions.
Benchmarking showed better batch mixing and preserved biology.

posts.title: RNA evidence supports clinical stage antibody drug targets in oncology
posts.authors: Pozzobon D, Khusial N, Spreafico R, et al.
posts.summary: A bulk and single-cell RNA ranking framework scored 4,532 surfaceome targets across six solid tumour indications for tumour specificity, normal-tissue safety and blood sink, and was tested against clinically pursued antibody targets.
key_points: Single-cell specificity gave higher odds ratios than bulk for clinical-stage and approved targets.
Adding safety and blood sink features made the single-cell score strongest.
Performance varied by indication, with breast cancer weaker.

posts.title: Spatial context of cellular heterogeneity in triple-negative breast cancer reveals actionable subtypes
posts.authors: Mesrizadeh Z, Mukund K, Yang L, et al.
posts.summary: Bulk and spatial transcriptomics with cellular mapping across a large TNBC cohort defined three reproducible ecosystem subtypes with distinct spatial microenvironments.
key_points: The subtypes are immune-exhausted (linked to checkpoint therapy), fibrotic/hypoxic, and metabolically reprogrammed.
Spatial profiling showed subtype-specific organisation at tumour centres and invasive edges.
Multiplexed imaging independently supported the immune-infiltrated versus stromal-excluded architectures.

posts.title: Spatially resolved tumor-microenvironment architecture defines therapeutic response in unresectable hepatoblastoma
posts.authors: Mesrizadeh Z, Ningappa M, Ranganathan S, et al.
posts.summary: Visium spatial transcriptomics (11 tumours) and CosMx single-cell imaging (3 tumours) on post-chemotherapy hepatoblastoma explants link spatial architecture to relapse.
key_points: Relapse-prone tumours had a centralised, TME-dominated organisation with SPP1+ macrophages, fibroblasts and MDK-LRP1 signalling.
Non-relapse tumours showed compartmentalised tumour-immune interactions.
Resection samples had lower tumour cell state heterogeneity.

posts.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals interferon pathway enrichment in early relapsing serous carcinoma
posts.authors: Niemeyer F, Aho N, Hanninen S, et al.
posts.summary: Spatial transcriptomics of matched adnexal and omental samples from nine HGSC patients, grouped by platinum-free interval, shows an interferon-driven phenotype in short-interval tumours.
key_points: Differences between short and longer platinum-free interval tumours were mostly site-agnostic.
C3, IFI27 and BST2 were consistently associated with short intervals, and C3 was validated by RNA in situ hybridisation.
High C3 expression was linked to shorter platinum-free survival in two public cohorts.

posts.title: A multimodal precision oncology platform integrating genomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional drug screening expands therapeutic options in pediatric brain tumors
posts.authors: Huang X, Qiao Y, Black GS, et al.
posts.summary: A tiered framework combining deep whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA-seq and ex vivo drug screening was applied to 17 children with malignant CNS tumours.
key_points: Functional screening gave every patient at least one high-confidence targeted or chemotherapy nomination.
scRNA-seq found an average of 37 druggable targets per patient, a fourfold rise in high-confidence recommendations.
Functional classes matched outcomes in 8 of 10 evaluable cases, an exploratory result.

posts.title: AmpliconSuite: an end-to-end workflow for analyzing focal amplifications in cancer genomes
posts.authors: Luebeck J, Liefeld T, Wong IT, et al.
posts.summary: AmpliconSuite is a toolkit that finds focal amplifications in cancer whole-genome sequencing, including extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA), breakage-fusion-bridge cycles and other amplification modes. Its ecContext module categorises ecDNA structures to help explain how they formed.
key_points: Predictions were validated against metaphase FISH for 175 probed genes across 72 models.
Analysis of 6,506 pan-cancer patient samples revealed ecDNA-mediated oncogene co-amplification preferences.
AmpliconRepository, a community-contributable platform, lets users compare results across more than 15,000 public samples.

figure.caption: Focal copy gains in tumour whole-genome data are sorted by AmpliconSuite into ecDNA, breakage-fusion-bridge and other amplification types, and ecContext then categorises ecDNA structures to infer how they formed.

posts.title: Functional diversification of the cephalopod proteome by RNA editing
posts.authors: Moen JM, Richards AL, Krogsaeter EK, et al.
posts.summary: Coleoid cephalopods show the highest known levels of ADAR-mediated RNA editing, but the effects of most recoding events were unclear. Integrating proteomics with biochemical and cellular assays across the Doryteuthis pealeii proteome, this study shows how recoding changes protein behaviour.
key_points: Proteomics confirmed translation of 7,997 recoded sites.
Recoding alters protein stability, subcellular localisation, post-translational modifications and enzymatic activity, and can create or remove modification sites.
Recoding the E3 ligase MARCHF5 changes widespread substrate ubiquitylation and perturbs mitochondrial homeostasis.

figure.caption: ADAR converts adenosine to inosine in squid mRNA, recoding the protein; recoding changes stability, localisation, modification sites and activity, and recoded MARCHF5 shifts substrate ubiquitylation and disturbs mitochondria.

posts.title: The molecular heterogeneity and clinical impact of genomic driver alterations in prostate cancer
posts.authors: Pellegrina D, Kiriy D, C L Cheng K, et al.
posts.summary: Using the Pan Prostate Cancer Group whole-genome dataset of 1,001 men, this study integrates small mutations, structural variants and copy number alterations to find recurrent driver alterations in 961 primary prostate tumours. At least one recurrent somatic or germline alteration was found in 97% of tumours.
key_points: Structural variation can hijack onco-enhancers of solute carrier genes, with SLC30A4 as a prominent example.
FOXA1, MDM4, COL5A1, TP53 and BRCA1 alterations stratify with metastatic disease, and additional drivers are enriched in African-ancestry tumours.
One quarter of tumours carry genome-informed therapeutic targets, and four oncotypes were defined, two of them with shorter metastasis-free survival.

posts.title: Decoding coupled epigenetic-fragmentomic signals in circulating cell-free DNA for interpretable cancer diagnosis
posts.authors: Wang Y, Hou Y, Liu X, et al.
posts.summary: This study asks whether methylation sequencing of plasma cell-free DNA preserves fragmentomic signals and how methylation and fragmentation are coupled. It defines plasma-derived methylation haplotype blocks (MHBs) as interpretable units and builds FAME, a multimodal cancer-detection model.
key_points: Canonical fragmentomic patterns were partially preserved in WGBS and EM-seq relative to conventional WGS, with preservation varying by feature.
Methylation levels were associated with fragment length and end-motif patterns, and MHBs showed tissue-associated regulatory features.
FAME and its genome-wide-augmented version FAME-GW performed robustly in cross-validation and independent validation against THEMIS, SPOT-MAS and DELFI, with FAME-GW strongest overall.

posts.title: Conditional diffusion for single-cell Hi-C data imputation and enhancement with scHiC-Diff
posts.authors: Liu W, Fang Z, Du X, et al.
posts.summary: scHiC-Diff is a conditional diffusion framework that imputes and enhances sparse single-cell Hi-C contact maps, treating them as masked images modelled with a Diffusion Transformer. It aims to separate technical dropouts from genuine absences of chromatin contacts.
key_points: Tested on two simulated and three real scHi-C datasets, it improved recovery of chromatin interaction patterns and downstream analyses over existing methods.
It is designed to avoid the smoothing and restrictive likelihood assumptions of existing methods, which can obscure fine-scale chromatin structure.
On a developmental scHi-C dataset it improved reconstruction of chromatin organisation and chromatin loop detection.

posts.title: CellDiffusion: Enhancing scRNA-seq data integration with accurate inference of cell-cell association
posts.authors: Liu YC, Huang Z, Lu SL, et al.
posts.summary: CellDiffusion is an unsupervised graph-based model that propagates cellular features through a diffusion process and learns a cell-cell attention network to integrate scRNA-seq datasets across batches. It applies cell-specific correction while preserving cell types and developmental trajectories.
key_points: It aims to separate genuine biological variation from technical noise, avoiding misaligned cell populations or uncorrected batch effects.
Validated across various datasets, including the human endometrium across the menstrual cycle.
The framework also improves label transfer, clustering and trajectory inference.

posts.title: cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level
posts.authors: El Kassem G, Westphal C, Doebel M, et al.
posts.summary: cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout) inserts genetic variants into endogenous genomic loci with prime editing, then compares variant frequencies in cDNA and genomic DNA to measure effects at the RNA level. It is a scalable way to study post-transcriptional consequences of variants, including variants of uncertain significance.
key_points: It works across diverse karyotypes and genomic loci.
Synonymous marker edits commonly used in prime editing screens can themselves alter RNA processing and confound the interpretation of variant effects.
It provides a framework for interpreting RNA-altering variants in cancer and other diseases.

posts.title: Telomere length of both parents contributes to heritable POT1 cancer-predisposition syndrome
posts.authors: Martin A, Lu R, Blake A, et al.
posts.summary: Using a nanopore sequencing approach with haplotype-specific telomere length resolution, this study examined telomere inheritance in families carrying germline POT1 mutations. Telomeres from both parents were elongated in carriers.
key_points: Offspring preferentially inherit their longest telomeres from the carrier parent, consistent with extensive germline elongation, while shorter telomeres mostly come from the non-carrier parent.
In carrier and non-carrier siblings, telomeres from both parents were elongated in POT1 carriers, with preferential elongation of the shortest telomeres.
The authors propose a mechanism of genetic anticipation in which POT1 mutations progressively deplete short telomeres that enforce telomere-based tumour suppression.

posts.title: EvoNiche: a comprehensive database for dissecting tumor niche dynamics and spatiotemporal evolution within the cancer ecosystem
posts.authors: Zhao H, Yin X, Wang S, et al.
posts.summary: EvoNiche is a database that integrates 91 matched spatial and single-cell transcriptomic datasets across 35 cancer types to dissect regional tumour niche dynamics and spatiotemporal trajectories. It covers 712 tissue sections and 58 single-cell datasets and identifies 5,609 spatial niches.
key_points: It provides tissue-level and cell-level trajectories, spatially organised cell composition, region-specific molecular programmes and cell-cell interactions.
It prioritises region-specific and transition genes as candidate genes across pan-cancer and immunotherapy cohorts.
It is intended as a resource for studying tumour ecosystem organisation, progression and therapeutic response.

posts.title: Chemically stabilized long antisense oligonucleotides perturb RNA exosome function
posts.authors: Hofacker DT, Gackstatter S, Deisling V, et al.
posts.summary: Proximity biotinylation proteomics identifies the RNA exosome catalytic subunits DIS3 and EXOSC10 as modification-sensitive binders of long, chemically stabilised single-stranded RNA drugs. Binding correlates with exosome impairment.
key_points: Impairment shows up as stabilised promoter upstream transcripts and accumulated ribosomal RNA processing intermediates, with reduced cell viability.

Oligonucleotides longer than 24 nucleotides can impair exosome function, and inhibition depends on how ribose and backbone modifications are arranged; bulky 2'-MOE residues or mesyl phosphoramidate linkages mitigate it.
ADAR-recruiting oligonucleotides can be designed that keep editing activity while minimising exosome interference.

posts.title: A Germline-Encoded lncRNA-Mitochondrial Axis Rewires Oxidative Phosphorylation to Drive Progression in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma
posts.authors: Duan G, Xu W, Jiang W, et al.
posts.summary: Whole-genome sequencing and transcriptomes of matched ccRCC tumour and normal kidney were integrated with cross-ancestry GWAS, eQTL, TWAS and fine-mapping to find germline regulatory variation behind ccRCC susceptibility. LINC02068 emerged as a genetically regulated tumour suppressor, with rs234043 prioritised as the candidate causal variant.
key_points: The rs234043 risk allele recruits HOXC8 and represses LINC02068 transcription; low LINC02068 is linked to adverse outcomes.
LINC02068 localises to mitochondria, binds the co-chaperone DNAJA3 and promotes its destabilisation, dampening oxidative phosphorylation.
Allele-specific editing and rescue experiments support an rs234043-HOXC8-LINC02068-DNAJA3 axis, and mitochondrial complex I inhibition suppressed ccRCC cell migration and proliferation.

posts.title: Cerebrospinal fluid and plasma circulating tumor DNA dynamics as a biomarker of response during trastuzumab deruxtecan treatment in patients with breast cancer with leptomeningeal disease
posts.authors: Fitzpatrick A, Shanmugalingam T, Haider S, et al.
posts.summary: Serial CSF and plasma samples from seven patients with breast cancer leptomeningeal disease in cohort 5 of the phase II DEBBRAH trial (trastuzumab deruxtecan) were profiled for ctDNA tumour fraction by ultra-low-pass whole-genome sequencing and for mutations by UMI-based targeted sequencing. CSF ctDNA looks like a sensitive, dynamic marker of leptomeningeal disease burden.
key_points: ctDNA was detected by ulpWGS in all baseline CSF samples but in only two of six baseline plasma samples.
Early falls in CSF ctDNA tumour fraction within 1-2 cycles were associated with prolonged radiological control, while plasma ctDNA mainly reflected extracranial disease.
CSF and plasma showed marked genomic compartmentalisation, including copy number alterations and subclonal variants that may relate to response and resistance.

posts.title: Patient-Centered Transition to Clean Intermittent Catheterization After a Sacrectomy for Sacral Chordoma: A Case Report and Narrative Review
posts.authors: Semenenko IG, Abdaev M, Bulatov AV, et al.
posts.summary: Case report of a 57-year-old woman with an S2-S4 sacral chordoma treated with a two-stage procedure (endoscopic mobilisation, then midline S2-S5 sacrectomy). Sacrificing the S2-S5 roots left her with complete bladder atony, and she learned clean intermittent catheterisation.
key_points: Imaging showed a 70 x 50 x 42 mm lesion that had grown to 72 x 51 x 81 mm by week 11, before surgery.
At six months a small stable residual tumour remained; proton therapy had not been given because of a postoperative cerebrospinal fluid collection.
The authors argue that the choice of bladder-emptying strategy after sacral tumour surgery should weigh oncological prognosis, neurological injury, patient preferences and structured education.

posts.title: Sacral chordoma
posts.authors: Turesso VD, Tzu Chen Y, Fabrissin MM, et al.
posts.summary: Case report of a 78-year-old man with low back pain and a 75 mm sacrococcygeal mass, treated by posterior oncological resection with S4-S5 sacral osteotomy. Pathology confirmed chordoma with negative margins.
key_points: MRI showed a lobulated tumour involving the distal sacrum and adjacent soft tissues without visceral invasion.
The authors note that sacral chordoma is hard to manage because of its infiltrative growth and closeness to pelvic structures.
They conclude that complete en bloc resection remains the cornerstone of treatment, within multidisciplinary management.

posts.title: The pan-cancer whole-genome landscape of Adolescent and Young Adult solid cancers
posts.authors: van Putten J, Rosendahl Huber A, Koster R, et al.
posts.summary: Paired tumour-normal whole genomes from 698 adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients and 5,220 older adults (OAs) show how age shapes cancer genomes. AYA tumours carry fewer somatic variants but largely share the same drivers.
key_points: Many apparent age differences reflect age-dependent subtypes such as IDH-mutant glioma and HPV-positive cervical cancer.
Colibactin, APOBEC and homologous recombination deficiency signatures were more prevalent in AYA colorectal, gynaecological and breast cancers, but were not more mutagenic when present.
Tumour type-concordant pathogenic germline variants were enriched in AYAs (10.9% vs 6.6% in matched OAs; p=0.006), often with a somatic second hit.

posts.title: Pan-cancer nucleosome landscapes reveal tumor heterogeneity and inform cell-free DNA-based detection
posts.authors: Yang S, Ye J, Yuan J, et al.
posts.summary: An atlas of nucleosome positioning and occupancy across 410 primary tumours from 23 cancer types, built from ATAC-seq and validated with independent MNase-seq data. Tissue-derived nucleosome signatures were then tested for cancer classification and detection in cell-free DNA.
key_points: Nucleosome occupancy carried information complementary to chromatin accessibility for tumour stratification and revealed heterogeneity within cancers, including Basal-like breast cancer subgroups.
In hepatocellular carcinoma, differential nucleosome analysis revealed cancer-associated chromatin remodelling.
In cfDNA the signatures classified three cancer types (AUROC 0.877) and detected colorectal cancer (AUROC 0.930), with 0.773 in an independent validation cohort.

posts.title: Modulator Resolves Transcript-, Allele-, and Condition-associated RNA Modification Differences from Direct RNA Sequencing
posts.authors: Nelson TM, Goneos M, Aufgebauer CJ, et al.
posts.summary: Modulator assigns every nanopore direct-RNA read, including 5'-truncated ones, to a 'fragmentform' defined by a shared transcript 3' end and its upstream splice junctions, then estimates per-base modification stoichiometry for each fragmentform. It classifies differences as transcript-, allele- or condition-dependent.
key_points: In the HG002 transcriptome it built 23,746 fragmentforms, 15,620 of them candidate novel isoforms, and assigning truncated reads to fragmentforms nearly doubled the number of testable, differentially modified sites.
m6A sites within 100 nt of a splice junction or 1 kb of a poly(A) site were less modified in fragmentforms using that junction or site, suggesting local transcript context shapes m6A deposition.

From the same reads it called SNPs with 93% precision and found 1,358 allele-specific modification differences; in Zika-infected cells, 96% of m6A changes at GLORI-measured sites agreed in direction with GLORI.

posts.title: IsoMatch enables population-scale transcript integration and reveals reference-dependent isoform novelty
posts.authors: Zheng X, Garcia-Ruiz S, Fu Y, et al.
posts.summary: IsoMatch is a scalable framework that merges transcript models and classifies them against reference annotations using explicit, configurable structural criteria for splice junction chains and transcript ends, keeping every merged model traceable to its inputs.
key_points: It merged 163 ENCODE transcript catalogs and classified 7.9 million transcript models, with peak memory of 0.49 GB and 1.1 GB respectively.
Integrating GENCODE, RefSeq and CHESS showed that 71.2% of transcript groups stayed annotation-specific even without terminal constraints.

For 4.84 million merged models from 119 long-read transcriptomes of the 1000 Genomes Project, the integrated reference raised the full-splice-match proportion from 12.0-13.6% with single annotations to 18.0%.

posts.title: Predicting resistance to synthetic lethal therapies in cancer
posts.authors: Yazar M, Lord CJ, Ryan CJ
posts.summary: This study asks whether resistance to synthetic lethal (SL) cancer therapies can be predicted in advance. Using ten genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 chemogenetic resistance screens, the authors trained a random forest on protein-protein interaction, co-expression and essentiality features.
key_points: Resistance genes were enriched among the protein-protein interaction partners of SL pairs, were more co-expressed with the target and showed distinct essentiality patterns.
Under leave-one-SL-pair-out validation the model reached a mean AUROC of 0.72 (range 0.57-0.91) but low average precision (~9%), because resistance genes are under 1% of genes.
The model was also tested on resistance to two SL therapies in clinical trials, MTAP-PRMT5 and ATM-ATR.

posts.title: Biopsy-aware phylogenetic reconstruction from longitudinal single-cell copy number profiles
posts.authors: Paszek J, Mykowiecka A, Gogolewski K
posts.summary: The Cancer Tree Biopsy Framework (CTBF) reconstructs cancer phylogenies from longitudinal single-cell copy-number profiles, distinguishing a profile from its separate observations across biopsies so that sampled ancestors and collection order can be used.
key_points: Biopsy-guided partial methods scored higher mean rooted generalized Robinson-Foulds similarity than pooled neighbor joining and topology-only MEDICC2 across 100 simulated histories.
Under a fixed computational budget they also beat NestedBD-Long at two evolutionary depths, although convergence of its MCMC runs was not established.
An application to three longitudinal KTN152 biopsies showed genome-scale feasibility on patient-derived copy-number estimates.

posts.title: Pervasive expression of early embryonic programs in cancer has stage-dependent survival impact
posts.authors: Wang T, Hernandez-Rodriguez B, Seneviratne JA, et al.
posts.summary: Using EmbryoRadar, a suite of preimplantation stage-specific machine learning classifiers, the authors show that early embryonic gene expression programmes are widespread in human tumours and independently predict overall survival beyond clinical covariates.
key_points: Similarity to the zygote and 2-cell stages was associated with better survival; in kidney cancer this came from stromal and immune cells responding to the tumour.
Trophectoderm-associated programmes in tumour cells were linked to worse survival in breast cancer and melanoma, and to MYBL2-driven cell cycle, oxidative phosphorylation and biosynthesis.
Cell line dependency data identified MYBL2 and FOXM1 as vulnerabilities in trophectoderm-high cancers.

posts.title: Benchmarking the AlphaGenome Variant Impact score against SpliceAI on post-release ClinVar classifications and experimental splicing assays
posts.authors: Cavus OA, Kuskucu A
posts.summary: A pre-planned benchmark of the AlphaGenome Variant Impact (AVI) score against SpliceAI, Pangolin and CADD, using ClinVar classifications made after AlphaGenome's ClinVar release (87,666 rare variants outside its training chromosomes) and six splicing assays.
key_points: For intronic variants at least 3 bases from an exon, AVI reached an AUROC of 0.957, not detectably different from SpliceAI (-0.005) or Pangolin (-0.006) and above CADD (+0.071).
For deep intronic variants AVI trailed SpliceAI (-0.070), and on the assays it ranked splice-altering variants below raw SpliceAI (-0.089).
AVI gave benign evidence to 24% of benign variants versus 90% for SpliceAI, and SpliceAI2, released during the study, led AVI on both kinds of ground truth.

posts.title: Navigating the rapidly evolving landscape of sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics technologies: a comprehensive multi-platform benchmark
posts.authors: Mortier J, Scheyltjens I, Kuznecova E, et al.
posts.summary: A systematic benchmark of a diverse set of sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics platforms across multiple tissue types and preservation methods, comparing capture area architecture, capture efficiency and spatial accuracy. The authors also propose terminology and operational performance metrics.
key_points: Platforms differ in transcript detection chemistry, capture area architecture, imaging capabilities and tissue compatibility.
The proposed metrics aim to link technical performance to downstream data analysis and biological interpretation.
The authors offer the results as a resource for experimental design and a step towards standards for future benchmarking.

posts.title: SF3B1 mutation generates novel peptides from long non-coding RNAs
posts.authors: Bhattacharya S, Fernandez M, Wu Y, et al.
posts.summary: Long-read sequencing of full-length transcripts from cell lines with and without SF3B1 mutation, together with ALLR, a new workflow to identify, quantify and annotate lncRNAs. With matched short-read RNA-seq and proteomics, the authors show SF3B1 mutation generates thousands of novel lncRNAs.
key_points: The mutation-associated lncRNAs show diverse levels of alternative splicing and produce translatable peptides with putative function, immunogenicity and protein-binding potential.
47 lncRNAs were also detected in primary chronic lymphocytic leukaemia samples and were associated with significantly higher risk of adverse prognosis, alongside known CLL risk factors.
The work demonstrates the utility of long-read sequencing for lncRNA research.

posts.title: Structural variant detection across sequencing technologies
posts.authors: Li G, Liu Y, Zhang A, et al.
posts.summary: The authors introduce HitSV, a structural variant caller that recognises breakpoints with awareness of repeats and signature density, then does haplotype-resolved local assembly to reconstruct and genotype SVs at base resolution. It works on short, long and hybrid sequencing data.
key_points: On the HG002 benchmark, HitSV had higher genotype F1 scores than state-of-the-art callers for long reads (15-72%), short reads (10-36%) and hybrid data (12%).
Applied to the 1KGP phase 4 cohort it expanded the SV callset by 31.5% and reshaped allele-frequency landscapes.
In a large Chinese long-read cohort it found tandem-repeat-mobile-element composite arrays to be a common, multi-allelic class of complex SV.
posts.data: HG002 benchmark; 1KGP phase 4; Chinese long-read cohort

figure.caption: HitSV takes short, long or hybrid reads through repeat-aware breakpoint calling and local assembly, and resolves a repeat locus into alleles with different numbers of tandem-repeat and mobile-element units.

posts.title: A telomere-to-telomere map of somatic mutation burden and functional impact in a cancer
posts.authors: Sohn MH, Dubocanin D, Vollger MR, et al.
posts.summary: The authors paired a near-telomere-to-telomere diploid assembly of one donor with deep short- and long-read sequencing of that donor's melanoma. This lets them score somatic variation in sequence that the GRCh38 reference does not contain.
key_points: 16% of somatic variants fall in sequences absent from GRCh38, and satellite repeats are hotspots of UV-associated mutagenesis.

Centromere kinetochore binding domains are focal sites of arm-level aneuploidy breakpoints and somatic variation, also seen in non-cancerous tissue, but their epigenetic remodelling appears specific to the tumour.
Single-molecule telomere analysis reconstructs cycles of erosion and telomerase extension during tumour evolution, and haplotype-resolved chromatin maps show widespread somatic epimutations.

posts.title: A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation
posts.authors: Parada GE, Bretschneider H, Li JD, et al.
posts.summary: Using deep transcriptome profiling, the authors catalogue hundreds of new neuronal microexons, including neuronal subtype-specific ones and some that trigger nonsense-mediated decay. A machine-learning model then learns a sequence code that predicts which microexons are spliced in neurons.
key_points: The code identifies regulatory elements around the expanded microexon set.
It flags genomic variants in autistic individuals predicted to alter microexon splicing, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact.
These variants are mostly in idiopathic cases, are associated with autism status and converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, plus some not previously linked.

posts.title: A phenome-wide structural variant map from 467,152 UK Biobank genomes
posts.authors: Atanur SS, Hu F, Lou H, et al.
posts.summary: The authors ran a phenome-wide association study of 1.6 million structural variants called from whole-genome sequencing of 467,152 UK Biobank participants. It covers 13,322 binary, 2,018 quantitative and 2,923 plasma protein traits.
key_points: 82.25% of the SVs were outside the detectable range of earlier copy-number-variant studies.
Protein QTL analysis linked 3,467 SVs to 1,690 proteins, with effects depending on SV type and location.
The SV-PheWAS found 28,184 associations with health outcomes, including rare SVs with strong effects; at known GWAS loci, 32.21% of associated SVs overlapped functional regions.

posts.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of somatic mutation detection by the SMaHT Network
posts.authors: SMaHT Network
posts.summary: The SMaHT Network ran large benchmarking experiments on cell lines and donor tissues to compare sequencing technologies, experimental approaches and computational methods for detecting somatic mutations. They release more than 1,000x short-read and 100-400x long-read data for nine samples.
key_points: The study defines effective strategies for using short and long reads to detect mutations.
Donor-specific and pangenome-inferred diploid assemblies improved calling and extended catalogues into difficult genomic regions.
Six duplex technologies were benchmarked, and single-cell sequencing resolved cell-type-specific mutational patterns; bulk, single-cell and duplex analyses were complementary.

posts.title: Somatic epimutations cap genetic determinism in the human diploid chromatin epigenome
posts.authors: Vollger MR, Swanson EG, Neph SJ, et al.
posts.summary: The authors present Fiber-seq inferred regulatory elements (FIRE), a method that gives a more complete, quantitative map of accessible chromatin across the diploid human genome and avoids biases in existing regulatory element catalogues.
key_points: FIRE enables comprehensive detection of haplotype-selective chromatin accessibility, including imprinted elements without parent-of-origin DNA methylation differences and modules that let genes escape X inactivation.
The HLA locus carries the most haplotype-selective accessibility in immune cells, and specific transcription factor binding events disrupted by disease-associated variants are resolved.
Autosomal somatic chromatin epimutations are widespread and are propagated by clonal expansion.

posts.title: Alternative splicing fine-tunes modular protein interfaces to control protein localization
posts.authors: Kjer-Hansen P, Pazaky K, Kavanagh D, et al.
posts.summary: The authors combine computational analysis of interactions and localisation data with a high-content imaging screen to ask how alternative exons rewire protein interactions and where proteins sit in the cell.
key_points: Tissue-regulated longer exons tend to reshape local interaction patterns, whereas microexons fine-tune key interfaces linking distinct processes.
38% of tested isoform pairs changed localisation, with microexons (typically under five amino acids) accounting for a substantial share.
A 4-amino-acid microexon in sorting nexin 2 changes localisation through repositioning of a flanking charged residue, not through side-chain chemistry.

posts.title: Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas
posts.authors: Chowdhury T, Tesileanu CMS, Kocakavuk E, et al.
posts.summary: Using whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing of longitudinal samples from 183 patients with IDH-mutant glioma in the GLASS Consortium, the authors compare how astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas evolve with progression and treatment.
key_points: PI3K and NOTCH1 mutations are newly acquired in recurrent oligodendrogliomas and go with higher mutational burden; recurrent astrocytomas instead gain focal oncogene amplifications and CDKN2A/B deletions that go with chromosomal instability, chromothripsis and genome doubling.
In both types, convergence of acquired alterations, genome-wide changes and worse outcomes suggests selection of treatment-refractory clones.
Temozolomide is linked to signatures SBS11 and SBS119 in both types, whereas the radiotherapy-associated ID8 signature rises only in astrocytomas.

posts.title: MassNet: billion-scale AI-ready mass spectral corpus empowering scalable deep learning in proteomics
posts.authors: Jiang A, Zhang X, Zhang X, et al.
posts.summary: The authors build MassNet, an AI-ready corpus of 1.5 billion tandem mass spectra from data-dependent acquisition across 35 species, plus a compact data format (MSDT). They use it to train XuanjiNovo, a transformer model for de novo peptide sequencing.
key_points: Roughly 1.7 million peptide precursors in the corpus come from human samples.
XuanjiNovo, a non-autoregressive transformer trained with curriculum learning, improves 38.35-143.57% over state-of-the-art methods on human Astral data.
The corpus also supports retention time prediction and PSM rescoring.

posts.title: LoL-align: sensitive and fast probabilistic protein structure alignment
posts.authors: Reifenrath L, van Kempen M, Kim G, et al.
posts.summary: LoL-align is a structure alignment method that maximises a local log-odds score for two proteins being homologous, given their intra-protein C-alpha distances. It is integrated into Foldseek.
key_points: It is markedly more sensitive than TM-align and Dali at detecting remote homologs on single- and multidomain benchmarks.
It gives better alignment quality at 5-20 times their speed.

posts.title: NeoBridge: Biophysics-informed neoantigen prioritization and clonal architecture profiling in pancreatic cancer
posts.authors: Mediavilla AL, Cardoso JP, Alvarez-Benayas J, et al.
posts.summary: NeoBridge is a hybrid ensemble of gradient boosting and a deep neural network that ranks neoantigens using HLA binding and processing, differential agretopicity, tumour neoantigen abundance and TCR recognition potential. It targets low-mutation-burden tumours such as pancreatic cancer.
key_points: Trained on 11,188 experimentally validated neoantigens, it reached an AUC-ROC of 0.904 on held-out data and outperformed established tools; cross-cancer AUC was 0.73-0.82, including 0.82 in pancreatic cancer.
Differential agretopicity was the most predictive feature.

In 118 PDAC patients with resolved phylogenies, subclonal neoantigen load was associated with worse progression-free survival (p < 0.001) and overall survival (p = 0.038); the authors call this hypothesis-generating.

posts.title: Detecting low-allele-fraction mosaic mutations: A multi-institution benchmarking with cell-line mixtures
posts.authors: Ha YJ, Maziec D, Markowski J, et al.
posts.summary: The SMaHT Network mixed cell lines at 1:49 and produced ultra-deep short- and long-read whole-genome data at five centres (170x-470x each). Seven institutions then ran twelve pipelines on it, against a cross-validated reference set of mosaic SNVs and indels.
key_points: Callsets were largely discordant across tools and replicates, partly because low-VAF mutations are sampled stochastically.
For SNVs above 2% VAF, sensitivity and precision approached 80% at 300x or more, with little gain from deeper sequencing.
The work gives a framework and best practices for low-VAF mutation detection in non-cancer tissue.

posts.title: A pangenomic method for establishing a synthetic somatic variant resource in HapMap mixtures
posts.authors: Kong N, Tang Z, Ruttenberg A, et al.
posts.summary: Six HapMap cell lines were mixed to create artificial somatic variants at 0.25%-16.5% allele fraction. The authors build pangenome graphs from the individual assemblies to turn this into a technology-agnostic benchmarking set.
key_points: The set has more than 6 million SNVs, 1.8 million small indels, 49,000 structural variants and 10,000 mobile element insertions.
A binomial model estimates the coverage needed for variant detection; aligning to T2T-CHM13 improves SV detection over GRCh38.
Low-allele-fraction detection stays hard in repeat-rich regions and falsely duplicated genes.

posts.title: Ryder: Epigenome normalization using a two-tier model and internal reference regions
posts.authors: Cao Y, Ge G, Zhao K
posts.summary: Ryder is a Python package that normalises epigenomic signal tracks using stable internal reference regions, such as invariant CTCF binding sites, instead of spike-ins or assumptions that may not hold.
key_points: It corrects background noise and signal intensity genome-wide and works across DNase-seq, CUT&RUN, ATAC-seq, MNase-seq and ChIP-seq, with or without spike-ins.
After normalisation it detects a quantitative loss of chromatin accessibility at key enhancers on BRG1 depletion.

posts.title: Revisiting Batch Effect Correction: A Structured Problem Formulation and Novel Solutions
posts.authors: Harrar A, Shaham U
posts.summary: The authors argue that existing batch-effect removal methods rest on an ill-defined problem and unverified assumptions, and propose a principled formulation with two new methods: an unsupervised one based on independent component analysis and a supervised one using domain adaptation.
key_points: Both methods are grounded in mathematical derivations.
They outperform existing methods across multiple datasets.

posts.title: scTransMIL bridges patient-level disease states and single-cell transcriptomics for cancer screening and heterogeneity inference
posts.authors: Tang Z, Wang F, Yang F, et al.
posts.summary: scTransMIL treats a sample as a bag of cells and uses transformer-based multi-instance learning to link single-cell transcriptomes to sample-level labels, without cell-level annotations.
key_points: It predicts sample-level cancer phenotypes, including tissue of origin for metastatic tumours.
At cell level it identifies tumour-associated populations and maps progression trajectories from minimal sample-level labels.
Attention weights support full-transcriptome biomarker discovery.

posts.title: The MODNAP benchmark set for modeling ribose-based modified nucleic acid and nucleic acid-protein complexes: a case study with AlphaFold 3
posts.authors: Fu J, Milam VT, McShan AC
posts.summary: The authors survey ribose-based modified nucleotides in PDB structures, build MODNAP as the first curated set of experimental structures containing them, and benchmark AlphaFold 3 on 1,039 nucleic acid and nucleic acid-protein complexes.
key_points: Modified nucleotides sit mainly on the nucleobase and are chemically and structurally diverse.
AlphaFold 3 succeeds above 80% at a 2.5 A RMSD threshold, but is less accurate at placing modified nucleotides, especially in structures not represented in training.
PoseBusters flags frequent intramolecular validity failures, mainly from non-ideal ribose ring geometry.

posts.title: Systematic evaluation of transcript normalization methods and quantification pipelines across long-read sequencing platforms
posts.authors: Paniagua A, Jetzinger F, Tarazona S, et al.
posts.summary: The authors benchmark five quantification workflows (Bambu, FLAIR, IsoQuant, Oarfish, Kallisto) and five normalisation methods on PacBio and Nanopore long-read RNA-seq, using SIRV and ERCC spike-ins and matched Illumina data.
key_points: TPM scaling corrects short-molecule depletion in PacBio data but distorts Nanopore expression estimates.
For Nanopore, covariate-aware normalisation (CQN, EDASeq) reduces length bias without TPM over-correction; scaled median ratio degrades accuracy in low-variability samples.
Reference-restricted quantifiers (Oarfish, Kallisto) beat transcript-reconstruction tools in short-read validation, and FLAIR had the lowest error on short SIRVs.

posts.title: Beyond the gene: contextualizing novel isoforms through pathway analysis in long-read single-cell RNA sequencing
posts.authors: Doyle PH, Page ML, Ebbert MTW
posts.summary: Long-read single-cell RNA-seq finds thousands of new isoforms and genes whose function is unknown. The authors present CIPI, which places a novel isoform among reference genes with similar cell-type expression and infers its pathway context from those neighbours.
key_points: CIPI builds expression-based neighbourhoods rather than relying on host-gene annotation or protein-domain similarity.
Combined with GO, KEGG or Reactome analysis, it gives a hypothesis-generating way to prioritise novel isoforms.

posts.title: Estimation of splicing metrics for NMD-sensitive transcripts
posts.authors: Zavileyskiy L, Vlasenok M, Kuznetsova A, et al.
posts.summary: Percent-spliced-in underestimates the true splicing rate of isoforms degraded by nonsense-mediated decay. The authors build statistical models that correct for this with a single decay-rate parameter. This is a revised version (v2) of a July preprint.
key_points: Gaussian mixture models separate splicing events into NMD-sensitive and NMD-evading classes; the latter show higher coding potential and stronger translation signals around the stop codon, consistent with readthrough.
Event-specific relative decay rates improve interpretation of differential splicing for NMD-annotated transcripts from short-read RNA-seq.

posts.title: Probing Genomic Foundation Models with Splice-Variant Perturbations
posts.authors: Alavi MV
posts.summary: The author probes generalist genomic foundation models (NTv3 650M, Evo2 40B, Genos 10B) and splicing specialists (SpliceAI, AlphaGenome, Borzoi) with expert-curated substitutions in the splicing regions of OPA1, then a 65-gene set of spliceogenic mutations.
key_points: Generalist models can match task-specific networks at predicting splice-altering variants.
Training data scale, genetic diversity and evolutionary context matter for capturing splicing syntax.
Classification accuracy improved with locus-specific rather than mutation-class thresholds.

posts.title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models reveals an advantage in the low-data regime for cell-type and disease-state prediction
posts.authors: Benhayon H, Danziger MM, Ben-Zvi D, et al.
posts.summary: The authors benchmark cell representations from four single-cell foundation models, with logistic regression, on 868 disease-prediction tasks across 82 datasets and 65 cell-type datasets from CELLxGENE.
key_points: With full data, log-normalised counts beat the best model (TranscriptFormer-Sapiens) for cell type and matched it for disease.
With few labelled cells, TranscriptFormer-Sapiens significantly outperformed the baseline on both tasks, up to about 100 samples per class.

posts.title: Revealing pan-cancer clonal niches of T cells from single-cell RNA sequencing using contrastive learning
posts.authors: Shorer O, Pinhasi A, Amit R, et al.
posts.summary: CloneTrast is a supervised contrastive-learning model that learns clonal-functional T-cell states from paired scRNA/TCR-seq during training but needs only scRNA-seq at inference.
key_points: Using 2.6 million T cells from 16 cancer types, it finds clonal niches not explained by TCR similarity or standard cell-state labels.
An NK-like niche enriched for tumour-blood shared TCRs is consistently associated with poor immunotherapy response across cancers.
Tumour-resident and blood-borne antigen-specific clones fall in different niches.

posts.title: Mathematical Modelling of Stochastic Gene Expression Quantifies mRNA Heterogeneity in Cancer Cell Populations with Extrachromosomal DNA
posts.authors: Ganguly PS, Huang W
posts.summary: The authors use a stochastic model of transcription to ask how ecDNA copy-number variation turns into mRNA heterogeneity, and fit it to single-cell ecDNA and mRNA counts from cell lines.
key_points: The model reproduces realistic mRNA distributions across parameter regimes.
Estimated transcriptional parameters are strikingly similar across cell lines and between ecDNA and chromosomal amplifications.
Modelling genotoxic therapy predicts the mRNA composition of persisting cells.

posts.title: Point-Process Modelling of Cell-Type Interaction Structure in CosMx Glioma Data for Hypothesis-Driven Tumor Inference from scRNA-seq
posts.authors: Carcanholo FP, Cassiano MHA, Panepucci EM, et al.
posts.summary: The authors model cell-type spatial organisation in eight CosMx glioblastoma specimens (2.4 million cells) with Log-Gaussian Cox Processes, then predict the resulting spatial phenotypes from transcript abundance.
key_points: Macrophages, microglia, monocytes, cDCs, neutrophils and T cells show spatial attraction toward malignant states.
Transcriptomic features outperform metabolic pathway scores, but leave-one-patient-out validation lowers performance and harmonisation does not restore it.
Predicted interaction scores stratify subclusters in external non-spatial single-cell datasets; generalisation needs larger spatial cohorts.

posts.title: Global signatures of Ribonucleotide Excision Repair deficiency and its therapeutic vulnerabilities
posts.authors: Toong PJ, Boushaki S, Zhao SJ, et al.
posts.summary: The authors show that loss of ribonucleotide excision repair (RER) leaves a genome-wide scar of indel, substitution and structural variant signatures, and build RERDetect, a whole-genome classifier for it.
key_points: Applied to more than 11,000 primary and metastatic cancers, RERDetect finds a recurrent subset of RER-deficient tumours, most without detectable RNASEH2 gene alterations.
RNASEH2C promoter hypermethylation is a recurrent cause.
RER-deficient cells are sensitive to EXO1 and FANCM inhibition.

posts.title: Benchmarked sequencing methods reveal hidden mosaic variation in the human brain
posts.authors: Weng J, Cha DH, Chun J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors benchmark four duplex sequencing methods alongside bulk and single-neuron genome sequencing in matched human brain tissue, then develop RIVER, which integrates read-level evidence across methods.
key_points: Methods differ in genome representation, yield and mutational profile, with little caller-level concordance but far more cross-method support at the read level.
RIVER expands cross-method-supported candidates about two orders of magnitude; roughly half of those tested validated at about 10,000x orthogonal sequencing.
Recovered variants resolve broadly distributed and regionally restricted clones and lineage among single neurons.

posts.title: Intraosseous Schwannoma of the Spine: A Report of Three Cases
posts.authors: Saha D, Shahi P, Ghavalkar A, et al.
posts.summary: A case series of three spinal intraosseous schwannomas (two thoracic, one sacral). These rare benign tumours are often misdiagnosed on imaging as metastasis, chordoma or giant cell tumour.
key_points: All three patients had gross total resection with instrumented stabilisation, and histology confirmed benign schwannoma.
Both thoracic patients, who presented with progressive myelopathy, had excellent outcomes.
The sacral patient, who presented with chronic low back pain, died after surgery from urosepsis.

posts.title: Design foresight and model humility for omics inference
posts.authors: Yu G
posts.summary: A review-style argument that omics inference should be question-first: decide what must be directly observed before choosing the assay, and say what the data can honestly support. Transcriptomics is used as the central case.
key_points: "Design foresight" means choosing assays, sampling and orthogonal measurements for the question, and stating whether transcriptomics is primary, supporting or insufficient for a claim.
"Model humility" means not promoting computational output beyond what the data and assumptions support.
Measured, inferred and predicted results should be written in voices matched to their support.

posts.title: Attribute Network-based Ranking (ANeR) identifies conserved translational fingerprints of M-phase
posts.authors: Eivers SB, Baumgartner A, Dorn M, et al.
posts.summary: The authors built ANeR, a network-based method that ranks mRNAs by their proximity to a training group across two-condition omics datasets. Applied to 30 datasets of mitotic and meiotic divisions, it found a conserved M-phase translational programme.
key_points: ANeR predictions were benchmarked against independent mitotic datasets and validated experimentally in Xenopus oocytes.
Fam76b and Cdca3 were identified as translationally activated regulators needed for timely Cdk1 activation in meiosis.
Analysis of the oocyte programme tested how broadly CPE/PAS regulatory rules apply and found transcripts that do not conform.

posts.title: scChronos: Hierarchical Temporal Context Learning for Missing Snapshot Prediction in Single-Cell Time Series
posts.authors: Yao J, Zhang Y, Xu Y, et al.
posts.summary: scChronos predicts missing time points in single-cell time-series atlases by treating the task as target-conditioned prediction of a population distribution rather than propagating individual cells. It compresses each snapshot into cluster-representative cells and fuses nearby time points.
key_points: Reported to improve both interpolation-style recovery and extrapolation-style forecasting over state-of-the-art methods.
Better preserves developmental topology and cell-type-specific marker and pathway programs.
Code and data are public on GitHub and Zenodo.

posts.title: CRISPR-HAWK: Haplotype- and Variant-Aware Guide Design Toolkit for CRISPR-Cas
posts.authors: Kumbara A, Tognon M, Carone G, et al.
posts.summary: CRISPR-HAWK designs guide RNAs using individual- and population-scale variants and haplotypes rather than the reference genome alone. Across 79,648 genomes it shows that variation substantially changes predicted guide performance at therapeutic targets.
key_points: For the approved sickle cell disease guide targeting BCL11A, some haplotypes completely abolish predicted cutting activity.
Across seven therapeutic loci, 82.5% of guides contain variants that modify on-target activity.
Variants can also create new PAM sites, giving individual-specific guides that reference-based design misses.

posts.title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
posts.authors: Xiao W, Hann T, Perry Z, et al.
posts.summary: In mouse neurons a long noncoding RNA is exported to the cytoplasm and translated into the M1 micropeptide. The authors map the IRES that drives this cap-independent translation and show it coincides with a B1 SINE repeat folded into a three-stem-loop structure.
key_points: In vivo chemical probing and structural modelling defined the three-stem-loop IRES.
The minimal IRES RNA bound ribosomal subunits, translation factors and the IRES cofactors Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1.
Depleting Rack1 and hnRNP A2/B1 reduced IRES-driven reporter translation and endogenous M1 peptide expression.

posts.title: Differential impact of tumor-derived ESR1 mutations on elacestrant benefit in metastatic breast cancer
posts.authors: Sledge GW, Xiu J, Fuqua S, et al.
posts.summary: Using Caris sequencing data from 3,344 ESR1-mutant breast tumours (transcriptome for 1,663) linked to claims-based time on treatment, the study asks whether different ESR1 mutations predict benefit from the oral SERD elacestrant.
key_points: Tumours with ESR1-L536 mutations had shorter time on elacestrant than those with Y537 or D538G (HR 2.089, p=0.001).
L536-mutant tumours had lower GREB1 expression and weaker estrogen-response pathway enrichment.
Patients with multiple ESR1 mutations had shorter time on treatment than those with a single mutation (adjusted HR 1.62, p=0.038).

posts.title: Loss of the Y chromosome is transcriptionally silent in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and across cancer entities
posts.authors: Waterhoelter A, Scholz R, Tsouris A, et al.
posts.summary: The authors asked whether loss of the Y chromosome (LOY) changes the tumour transcriptome. Using two human ccRCC cohorts (TCGA-KIRC, CPTAC), a mouse ccRCC model and isogenic Y-deficient 786-O clones, they find changes are essentially limited to Y and pseudoautosomal gene dosage.
key_points: A pan-cancer meta-analysis across TCGA entities showed the same pattern, with no autosomal gene showing a large consistent effect.
Human cohorts showed a modest, reproducible pathway-level response in cell cycle, ribosome biogenesis and DNA repair genes.
Cancer/testis antigen expression was higher in LOY tumours in some entities, but not in ccRCC.

posts.title: A Weighted Estimation Approach to Correct for Imperfect Mutation Detection Due to Intra-tumor Heterogeneity in Tumor Sequencing
posts.authors: Mauguen A, Ostrovnaya I.
posts.summary: Somatic mutations are often missed in tumour sequencing because of heterogeneity and limited depth, which biases mutation prevalence and inflates type I error when groups such as responders and non-responders are compared. The authors propose a weighted estimator that adjusts for imperfect detection sensitivity.
key_points: Assumes a surrogate of mutation sensitivity is observed only in patients with a called mutation and derives its unconditional mean.
Gives less biased mutation frequency estimates than the unweighted approach.
Better controls the type I error when comparing mutation prevalence between groups.

posts.title: Multi-omic long-read sequencing reveals nucleosome control of transcriptional fidelity at the isoform level
posts.authors: Bai G, Dhillon N, Meissner B, et al.
posts.summary: In yeast lacking the chromatin remodelers ISW1 and CHD1, the authors profiled chromatin fibres, nascent RNA and full-length mature RNA by nanopore sequencing. A new framework, EpiFLAIR, links single-molecule chromatin states across whole genes to isoform-level outputs.
key_points: Single-molecule chromatin states plus sequence motifs strongly predicted alternative TSS isoform expression.
Loss of ISW1 and CHD1 activated silenced promoters while repressing active ones, with promoter and gene-body accessibility anticorrelated on the same fibre.
Disrupted nucleosome spacing impaired RNAPII processivity and co-transcriptional splicing, changing splice isoform composition.

posts.title: Systematic benchmark of demultiplexing workflows for direct RNA sequencing
posts.authors: Bryson JW, Johansson LB, George A, et al.
posts.summary: The study benchmarks two barcode demultiplexing tools for nanopore direct RNA sequencing, WarpDemuX and SeqTagger, using species identity and matched IVT spike-ins as ground truth across four RNA004 flow cells.
key_points: Both tools achieve high precision but trade off precision against read retention.
SeqTagger performed well at its recommended settings, whereas WarpDemuX varied by model, barcode and read quality.
IVT-derived score cutoffs raised WarpDemuX yield, but precision seen on IVTs did not always carry over to species reads.

posts.title: A high-resolution protein-RNA binding atlas for structure-aware interaction prediction and post-transcriptional regulatory modeling
posts.authors: Karimzadeh M, Fish L, Karner H, et al.
posts.summary: The authors introduce ecCLIP, a high-throughput CLIP-seq platform, and apply it to 67 endogenously tagged RNA-binding proteins in HEK293T cells. They also built Pythia, a structure-aware neural network that predicts RBP binding from sequence and RNA base-pairing.
key_points: Adding ecCLIP data to a Borzoi-derived model improved RNA half-life prediction and 3′ UTR variant effect assessment.
Pythia splits predictions into sequence- and structure-dependent parts, tested with massively parallel reporter CLIP assays for five RBPs.
The same assay confirmed allele-specific binding effects for variants prioritised by Pythia.

posts.title: Fine-tuning genomic models on rare splicing events identifies a novel biomarker of TDP-43 pathology
posts.authors: Martin-Linares CP, Peethambaran Mallika A, Sandal PS, et al.
posts.summary: Using TDP-43 cryptic exons as a test case, the authors ask whether genomic foundation models can learn rare splicing events after fine-tuning. Fine-tuned OpenSpliceAI detected held-out cryptic exons in human and mouse, while AlphaGenome needed all its weights unfrozen to generalise.
key_points: A splicing head trained on AlphaGenome’s frozen backbone failed to predict cryptic exons.
Genome-wide application of fine-tuned OpenSpliceAI found new cryptic events in CLDN11 and ARHGAP23, validated in FTLD-TDP brain tissue.
The CLDN11 cryptic exon is predicted to create a neoepitope that could be an oligodendrocyte-specific biomarker of TDP-43 pathology.

posts.title: Unveiling the Hidden Rules: Enhancing NMD Prediction for Protein-Truncating Variants
posts.authors: Egab I, Schmidt J, Cortazar M, et al.
posts.summary: The canonical 50-55 nucleotide rule explains only about half of nonsense-mediated decay outcomes. Using paired genome and RNA sequencing from 10,306 TOPMed samples, the authors measured NMD efficiency for 5,749 germline truncating variants and trained a classifier, TrunCat.
key_points: TrunCat separates NMD-sensitive from NMD-escape transcripts with about 78% ROC-AUC.
A reduced eight-feature model chosen by SHAP value nearly matched the full model.
Variants of uncertain significance showed higher predicted NMD escape than pathogenic variants.

posts.title: IsoGraph resolves coordinated transcript choice and gene abundance in the aging human brain
posts.authors: Bennett A, Johnson EK, Benjamin KJM.
posts.summary: IsoGraph represents isoform usage and gene abundance as paired network channels, finds gene modules and quantifies each channel’s contribution. Applied to BrainSEQ and GTEx brain transcriptomes, it finds age-associated transcript-usage signals that persist after conditioning on gene abundance.
key_points: In synthetic benchmarks IsoGraph recovered structure when the planted signal was in coordinated transcript usage.
Modules were stable across donor subsets and supported by junction usage, independent long-read data and allelic analyses.
Disease colocalisation prioritised candidate isoform events, including an alternative terminal exon at PRDM2 linked to ALS.

posts.title: tRNAZAP: Deep learning toolkit for nanopore tRNA signal analysis
posts.authors: Daneshwar Kakhaki P, Akeson S, Ghohabi Esfahani N, et al.
posts.summary: Existing nanopore basecallers and aligners are tuned for mRNA and struggle with short, modification-dense tRNA. tRNAZAP works directly on raw current signal with two transformer models: one segments adapter from tRNA, the other classifies the tRNA type to pick the alignment reference.
key_points: Trained on in vitro transcribed RNA and evaluated on yeast tRNA.
