Reached about 98% classification accuracy and about 0.98 intersection-over-union for segmentation.
Together the outputs allow direct pairwise alignment of the tRNA portion to its reference.

posts.title: Towards standards for analysing structural variants from short-read whole genome sequencing data
posts.authors: Slimmer JC, Jones JL, Reay WR, et al.
posts.summary: The study benchmarks short-read SV callers against truth sets (HG002 T2T-Q100, Platinum Pedigree) and long-read databases at base-pair resolution, using 30X Illumina data. Only five of sixteen tools reliably output perfectly matching deletions, insertions and duplications.
key_points: Ensemble pipelines such as GATK-SV, MOPline and Parliament2 cut perfect-match accuracy by up to 98% versus their best constituent tools.
The inaccuracy propagates into gnomAD-SV and likely other short-read SV databases.
A proof-of-concept intra-sample merging strategy gave the highest F1 for deletions and insertions on HG002.

posts.title: Clonal heterogeneity in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and its impact on tumor progression
posts.authors: Kalfakakou D, Cameron DC, Kawaler EA, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell RNA sequencing of 62 primary pancreatic tumours (443,451 cells), 11 of them with matched spatial transcriptomics, resolves genetically distinct clones within each tumour. Focal 8q24 (MYC) amplification is linked to classical-to-basal transitions and loss of immune-response programmes.
key_points: Clones coexist within single tumours and show clone-specific ligand-receptor programmes that follow gene dosage: amplifications enrich interactions, deletions suppress them.
MYC knockdown in murine and primary human models reactivated classical programmes and restored immune-response pathways.
Dispersed clones with EMT and immune-suppression activity correlated with metastatic potential and lymph node colonisation; six tumours were also sampled before and after chemotherapy.

figure.caption: A pancreatic tumour map of three clones, one carrying 8q24 MYC gain, which tips cells from a classical, immune-active state to a basal, immune-off state that MYC knockdown reverses.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations
posts.authors: Shiraishi Y, Ochi Y, Sugawa M, et al.
posts.summary: Rare k-mers in centromeric regions define discrete, lineage-specific haplogroups. The authors built ascairn to infer them from short-read whole-genome sequencing and applied it to more than 3,300 genomes and 142 oligodendroglioma cases.
key_points: Centromere haplogroups show extensive global diversity and carry signatures of population history.
In 142 oligodendrogliomas with 1p/19q co-deletion, breakpoints map to the centromeres of chromosomes 1 and 19, positioned relative to kinetochore attachment sites.
Centromere haplotype structure is linked to susceptibility to rearrangement.

figure.caption: Rare k-mers on three centromere arrays sort them into haplogroups A, B and C, and 1p/19q co-deletion breakpoints in oligodendroglioma fall at the centromeres of chromosomes 1 and 19.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Mutability Dependence of Breast Cancer Metastasis and Latency to Recurrence
posts.authors: Lawrence-Paul MR, Pan TC, Pant DK, et al.
posts.summary: Analysis of genomic data from 662 paired and about 6,000 unpaired primary and metastatic breast tumours finds that metastasis-specific mutations are often acquired after dissemination, with a disproportionate share from APOBEC mutagenesis. The authors propose a mutability-dependent model of metastasis.
key_points: Metastasis-specific mutations converge on recurrent pathways that differ from those altered in primary tumours and depend on metastatic site; 95% of patients carry them in a minimum set of 10 pathways.
More than half of the variation in metastatic latency across patients is explained by when mutations in these pathways were acquired relative to dissemination.
Latency may reflect the time disseminated cells need to acquire the remaining drivers.

figure.caption: Driver mutations in the primary tumour come first, then APOBEC mutagenesis in the disseminated cell adds the remaining mutations, and that time sets the latency to metastatic recurrence.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Transposable element splicing reveals a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts
posts.authors: Li Z, Bao Y, Yu H, et al.
posts.summary: A pan-cancer survey of splicing involving transposable elements defines TEtrans, spliced transcripts that start in TEs, are made mostly of TE sequence and are enriched in tumours independent of host genes. One endogenous retrovirus-derived TEtrans promotes colorectal cancer growth and some encode shared tumour antigens.
key_points: TEtrans expression is linked to stemness and inflammation regulators in a context-dependent way.
An endogenous retrovirus-derived TEtrans promotes colorectal cancer growth by enhancing topoisomerase I-mediated DNA relaxation.
A subset of TEtrans encodes shared tumour antigens that drive antigen-specific cytotoxic T cell responses, and a mouse TEtrans-like transcript controls tumours in vivo.

posts.title: A feedback mechanism of m6A via PARP1-mediated ADP ribosylation of METTL3/METTL14
posts.authors: Bai Y, Zhou Z, Yan X, et al.
posts.summary: In human cell lines, m6A readers IGF2BPs recruit PARP1 to m6A-modified RNAs, and PARP1 then ADP-ribosylates the writer METTL3/METTL14, reducing m6A deposition. This read-orchestrate-write loop is a negative feedback on m6A levels.
key_points: ADP ribosylation impairs METTL3/14 RNA-binding capability and so reduces m6A deposition.
Combining a PARP inhibitor with inhibition of IGF2BP2 or METTL3 gave synergistic anti-tumour effects.
The work extends the writer/eraser/reader model by showing signalling pathways can regulate m6A homeostasis.

posts.title: Double-base deletions and signatures associated with platinum adducts in metastatic cancer
posts.authors: Smid M, van Leeuwen L, Wilting SM, et al.
posts.summary: Platinum drugs make G-G intrastrand adducts, yet existing platinum-linked double-base substitution signatures have no GG component. In a large pan-cancer metastatic cohort the authors derive de novo signatures that include double-base deletions.
key_points: One oxaliplatin-associated signature is dominated by GG deletion and also contains new and known substitutions.
Signatures with TT deletion as the single feature are strongly associated with microsatellite instability in several cohorts, and provisionally in liquid biopsies.
The signatures extend the catalogue of mutational effects of platinum.

posts.title: RiboBA: a bias-aware probabilistic framework for robust ORF identification across diverse ribosome profiling protocols
posts.authors: Bai J, Yang R
posts.summary: RiboBA is a probabilistic framework that models protocol-induced biases in ribosome profiling, which blur the three-nucleotide periodicity that ORF callers rely on. It jointly infers these biases and codon-level occupancy, then calls translated ORFs and initiation sites.
key_points: It improved exact nucleotide- and codon-level P-site assignment over a fixed-offset approach in simulations.

Across simulations and empirical datasets, with immunopeptidomics as orthogonal support, it improved non-canonical ORF identification, most for RNase I libraries with weak periodicity and for MNase and nuclease P1 data.
In Drosophila it flagged candidate ncORFs, including upstream translation in ThrRS and Mettl2.

posts.title: Reconstruction of contact signals from repeated elements with Hicberg
posts.authors: Gradit S, Ortion S, Larrous P, et al.
posts.summary: Hicberg is an algorithm that recovers reads usually discarded because they map to repeats, using statistical inference to place missing 3D contacts of transposons, rDNA and other repeated elements from paired data such as Hi-C.
key_points: It gives new views of how repetitive elements shape the spatial organisation of genomes.
In yeast it placed molecular motors that form chromosomal loops next to certain transposons.

posts.title: TL-iGeneCombo: Transfer Learning for Individual Sample Specific Gene Combination Effect Prediction and Selection in Cancer Cells
posts.authors: Gökbağ B, Wang L, Yang C, et al.
posts.summary: TL-iGeneCombo uses transfer learning to borrow combinatorial double-knockout data from other cancer cell lines to predict synthetic lethality and gene combination effects in a target cell line.
key_points: It improved synthetic lethality classification accuracy by 19% and the Spearman correlation of combination effect scores by 29%.

Gene pairs designed with a model built on the first double-knockout experiment in 22RV1 prostate cancer cells were tested in a second experiment; the combination-effect prediction held, the synthetic lethality prediction did not.

posts.title: DNA-Based Biomarkers as Predictors of Carboplatin Response in Neoadjuvant Treatment for Hormone Receptor Positive and Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
posts.authors: Pladsen AV, Smebye ML, Garred Ø, et al.
posts.summary: In a randomised neoadjuvant trial of 187 patients with high-risk HER2-negative breast cancer, pretreatment whole-exome sequencing gave genome-instability scores (CAAI, LOH fraction, HRD status) that were tested as predictors of benefit from added carboplatin.
key_points: In triple-negative disease, carboplatin raised pCR from 43% to 69% and prolonged event-free survival, with the clearest benefit in tumours with a low genomic LOH fraction (confirmed prognostic effect in an independent cohort of 67).
In hormone receptor-positive disease, pCR was not significantly different, but low residual cancer burden rose from 16% to 35%.
HRD-positive hormone receptor-positive tumours had pCR in 5 of 8 with carboplatin, versus 4 of 47 HRD-negative.

posts.title: Ultrastructural pathological features and clinical significance of recurrent chordoma
posts.authors: Zhang Q, Yang H, Zhang C, et al.
posts.summary: Transmission electron microscopy of 50 recurrent and 50 primary chordoma specimens (16 matched pairs from the same patient) compares subcellular features of recurrence.
key_points: Recurrent tumours showed atypical cytoplasmic vacuolation with giant cystic fusion, mitochondrial injury, loss of mitochondria-associated ER membrane complexes, nuclear atypia, lost desmosomal junctions, invadopodia and stromal microvascular dysplasia, all significantly more often than primary tumours.
Severity of ultrastructural damage rose with the number of prior recurrences.
The series is cross-sectional and not linked to survival, so use for risk prediction remains a hypothesis.

posts.title: Primary spinal bone sarcomas in Japan: a nationwide comparative analysis of demographic and pathologic features, treatment patterns, and survival
posts.authors: Toda Y, Ogura K, Morizane C, et al.
posts.summary: A retrospective national registry study of 3,755 Japanese patients with primary bone sarcoma diagnosed 2016 to 2019, comparing 356 spinal tumours with non-spinal ones. Chordoma is among the spinal histologies.
key_points: Spinal sarcomas presented at older age and at a more advanced stage, were less often managed at specialist centres, and had lower 3-year survival (45% vs 69%).
Within the spinal group, osteosarcoma had significantly worse survival than chordoma (HR 5.98), and distant disease predicted worse survival than localised disease (HR 3.54).

posts.title: Inferring ecDNA Evolution from Allele Frequency Spectra
posts.authors: Dameracharla B, Prasad G, Luebeck J, et al.
posts.summary: ecEvol infers when an extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) arose, its selection strength, mutation rate and clonal dominance from allele frequency spectra in bulk whole-genome sequencing of one tumour biopsy.
key_points: In primary, treatment-naive tumours ecDNA typically emerges early and is under strong positive selection, with variation across cancer types; ecDNA carrying known oncogenes emerges earlier and becomes more dominant.
In advanced, mostly treated tumours ecDNA emerges later than in matched primaries, and earlier emergence is associated with poorer overall survival.

posts.title: Optimizing copy number profiles for tumor cell phylogeny inference from low-coverage single-cell sequencing data
posts.authors: Ahmed N, Weiner S, Payne C, et al.
posts.summary: Tumour cell phylogenies built from low-coverage single-cell DNA sequencing depend heavily on the bin size used to infer copy number profiles. The authors show this on three real datasets and in simulations, and propose a way to choose bin size.
key_points: Small changes in bin size can strongly change reconstructed phylogenies, even in idealised simulations.
The proposed selection approach significantly improved reconstruction accuracy over baselines across coverage levels and reconstruction methods.

posts.title: Linking somatic variants to altered methylation profiles in nanopore-derived breast and pancreatic cancer genomes using unduliner
posts.authors: Atanda HC, Ewing AD
posts.summary: unduliner is a framework with a pretrained convolutional neural network that predicts which somatic SNVs and structural variants are associated with methylation changes in cancer genomes, using nanopore reads that carry both variants and base modification.
key_points: The model reached 0.803 accuracy on validation and 0.897 on held-out test data.

On MCF7 subline-specific variants it found variant-linked methylation differences independent of haplotype effects; in one pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma it linked coding and non-coding variants to tumour-normal and allele-specific methylation.

posts.title: Calibrated analysis framework for nanopore direct RNA sequencing uncovers cell-specific m6A proportions at conserved sites
posts.authors: Ohnezeit D, Loliashvili E, Putzel G, et al.
posts.summary: This work benchmarks m6A mapping by nanopore direct RNA sequencing with Dorado modification-aware basecalling, using primary-cell RNA, unmodified in vitro transcripts and a methyltransferase inhibitor as controls, and compares it with GLORI on the same RNA.
key_points: Stringent filtering is needed to remove background, and Dorado calls capture more GLORI sites at high m6A/A proportions.
Applied to human fibroblasts and HD10.6 neurons, it detected differences in predicted m6A/A proportions at conserved sites between the two cell types.

posts.title: phyloDS: phylogeny-aware differential splicing across species, beyond reference annotations
posts.authors: Liehrmann A, Carrel Billiard L, Bastide P, et al.
posts.summary: phyloDS compares alternative splicing across species by defining orthologous splice junctions on alignments of one-to-one orthologous genes, testing differential usage with a regularised Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model, and checking shifts against sequence-based splice-site predictions.
key_points: On primate brain and rodent heart RNA-seq it recovered up to 2.9-fold more shared orthologous junctions than a reference-based strategy and kept type I error near nominal where other methods inflate it more than two-fold.
It found 234 differentially used junctions in hominoids and 502 in mole-rats (86 and 141 unannotated), including a mitochondrial and contractile splicing signature in mole-rats.

posts.title: Robust ORF Deconvolution from Multiple Ribo-seq Datasets with Group LASSO Penalty
posts.authors: Maidhof K, Schlosser A, Erhard F
posts.summary: PRICE 2 resolves short, weakly translated and overlapping ORFs in Ribo-seq by adapting isoform deconvolution: a generative model with group LASSO regression infers active ORFs jointly across runs.
key_points: It outperformed thirteen other tools on short and overlapping ORFs in a benchmark.
ORFs it called yielded about 40% more cryptic MHC-I peptides than the best competing tool at a fixed false discovery rate.
Public ribo-seq from 45 cell and tissue types was used to build ORF-stock, a database of non-canonical ORFs.

posts.title: WarpDemuX-custom - Multiplexed sequence-specific direct RNA sequencing
posts.authors: Naarmann-de Vries I, van der Toorn W, Mishra S, et al.
posts.summary: An improved sequence-specific nanopore direct RNA protocol for ribosomal RNA, with longer reads and better capture of human 28S rRNA, plus an expanded WarpDemuX toolbox for flexible (de)multiplexing of non-polyadenylated RNAs.
key_points: Validated in human cell lines with knockouts of different C/D box snoRNAs that direct 2'-O-methylation of 28S rRNA, detecting the associated modification changes.
The approach was also validated on another panel of non-polyadenylated RNAs.

posts.title: STARgrid: an open-source pipeline from Visium HD sequencing reads to count matrices
posts.authors: Hung L-H, Yeung KY
posts.summary: STARgrid is an open-source pipeline from Visium HD FASTQ files to count matrices at 2, 8 and 16 um, offered as an alternative to Space Ranger, which cannot be modified or redistributed.
key_points: On three human slides gene totals correlate at least 0.9989 with Space Ranger, with 20-35% less wall time.
It resolves location per molecule rather than per read, giving molecule totals 1.9-7.6% higher; against an adjacent Xenium section its counts were closer for 15 of 20 cancer panel genes.
The authors call the results preliminary.

posts.title: DECONVersation: Single Cell Foundation Model-Derived Embeddings for Robust Cell Type Deconvolution of Bulk RNA-seq
posts.authors: Oku A, Geiger H, Robine N, et al.
posts.summary: DECONVersation uses embeddings from pretrained or fine-tuned single-cell foundation models with a non-negative least squares solver to estimate cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq, avoiding explicit marker gene selection.
key_points: Benchmarked against MuSiC, DWLS and BayesPrism, it was comparable or better across diverse tissues.
Tissue-specific fine-tuning improved performance further.

posts.title: A unified framework for quantitative splicing and transcript prediction
posts.authors: Jaganathan K, Chen J, Liu X, et al.
posts.summary: SpliceAI2 is a deep learning model trained end to end on splice site, junction and transcript usage across mammalian species. It rebuilds whole transcripts from genomic sequence and quantifies the effect of splice-altering variants.
key_points: It improved detection and quantification of splice-altering variants across benchmarks of cryptic splicing, splicing QTLs and massively parallel reporter assays.
In a rare disease cohort, predicted splice-altering variants were enriched in disease genes and accounted for 15% of the excess genetic burden, about half of them deep intronic.

posts.title: Micronuclear ecDNA constrains tumor cell fitness and is associated with favorable patient survival
posts.authors: Brückner L, Xu R, Tang J, et al.
posts.summary: Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) lets tumours keep many copies of an oncogene, but its link to micronuclei was unclear. This study shows that damaged ecDNA is a major source of micronuclei and that ecDNA mis-segregation into them limits tumour cell fitness.
key_points: Replication stress promotes mitotic ecDNA clustering, asymmetric inheritance, mis-segregation into micronuclei and lower transcriptional output.
Single-micronucleus sequencing shows several distinct ecDNA species can coalesce within one micronucleus.
In MYCN-amplified neuroblastoma, a higher frequency of ecDNA micronuclei at diagnosis is associated with better overall survival.

figure.caption: Replication-stressed ecDNA is mis-segregated into a micronucleus in the daughter cell, which cuts output and survival of the cell, while more ecDNA micronuclei in neuroblastoma go with better patient survival.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: PHYHD1-mediated translational control regulates renal cell carcinoma progression
posts.authors: Liang Q, Zurlo G, Jin J, et al.
posts.summary: PHYHD1 is lost progressively as renal cell carcinoma advances. It binds the elongation factor eEF1A1, changes how eEF1A1 sits on ribosomes and restrains translation, and this works independently of its dioxygenase activity.
key_points: Integrative deep learning analysis of pan-cancer datasets links PHYHD1 loss to tumour advancement and poor prognosis.
Ribosome profiling and RNA-seq identify ceramide transporter 1 (CERT1) as the key effector: PHYHD1 depletion raises CERT1 translation.
Restoring PHYHD1 suppresses growth in RCC cells and patient-derived xenografts, and targeting CERT1 impairs PHYHD1-deficient cells.

figure.caption: Where PHYHD1 binds eEF1A1, translation of CERT1 mRNA is held in check; where PHYHD1 is lost, CERT1 translation runs freely and RCC progresses.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: RAISE quantifies RNA binding protein activity via transcriptomic profiling
posts.authors: Liu Y, Lo Y, Zheng Y, et al.
posts.summary: RAISE is a computational framework that infers the activity of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) on alternative splicing. It combines CLIP-seq, sequence motifs and splicing changes from RNA-seq to build RBP-exon regulatory networks.
key_points: It accurately inferred RBP activity across multiple cell lines and perturbation experiments, including changes independent of RBP expression.
Applied to TCGA, it revealed RBPs with altered activity in cancer.
The authors provide RAISEDB, a database of predicted RBP-exon interactions.

posts.title: Cardiac fibroblast deletion of PTBP1 modulates the profibrotic response by alternative splicing
posts.authors: Ricketts SN, Farber GM, Verma SK, et al.
posts.summary: The RNA-binding protein PTBP1 regulates activation of cardiac fibroblasts. Deleting Ptbp1 in these cells reduces fibrosis and preserves heart function in three mouse injury models.
key_points: Ptbp1 deletion in cardiac fibroblasts helped after angiotensin II infusion, transverse aortic constriction and myocardial infarction.
Transcriptomic and splicing analyses found PTBP1-dependent expression and alternative splicing programmes in extracellular matrix and cytoskeleton genes.
PTBP1 regulates Fgfr1 alternative splicing, and restoring the FGFR1β isoform partly rescued the contractile defect.

posts.title: CMGL: Confidence-guided Multi-omics Graph Learning for Cancer Subtype Classification
posts.authors: Fan B, Yin H, Yi S, et al.
posts.summary: CMGL is a multi-omics graph learning method for cancer subtype classification. It estimates how reliable each omics layer is for each patient before fusing them, and uses consensus patient neighbourhoods for graph classification.
key_points: Two problems are addressed: uninformative omics layers weakening the fused representation, and noisy layers adding wrong patient links.
The reliability estimate is made separately, before fusion, rather than inside the classification objective.

posts.title: Dynamic Graph Prior-Guided Latent Adaptation for Generalizable Single-Cell Perturbation Response Prediction
posts.authors: Bie Y, Fan P, Yin Q, et al.
posts.summary: DGP-LA predicts single-cell transcriptional responses to drugs in cell types the model has not seen. It refines a biological graph prior for each perturbation and injects it as gated latent corrections into a cell-state transition model.
key_points: On the Tahoe and NeurIPS datasets it improves Pearson Delta over State by 8.7% and 35.8% for unseen cell types.
In zero-shot drug response prediction on unseen cell types it improves Pearson Delta over CRISP by 79.1% and 67.6%.
It also improves DE-gene recovery and Hallmark pathway recovery.

posts.title: smiMAD: Adaptive multi-view graph learning for paired spatial omics integration
posts.authors: Tao Y, Wang F
posts.summary: smiMAD integrates paired spatial omics data, where RNA is measured together with chromatin accessibility or protein in the same tissue. It models spatial-neighbourhood and molecular-feature graphs with separate and shared branches.
key_points: Across 17 simulated and 15 real RNA-ATAC and RNA-protein datasets it gave competitive clustering accuracy, spatial coherence and multimodal integration.
A dynamic strategy gradually relaxes the spatial constraint during training.

posts.title: Paired Single-Cell Profiling Reveals Glutathione-Dependent Immune Evasion in Breast Cancer Liver Metastasis
posts.authors: Lyu C, Wang M, Wang H, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq of matched primary tumours and liver metastases from 13 treatment-naive breast cancer patients shows metastases that are immune-infiltrated yet evade destruction. Metastatic cells keep the clonal and genomic diversity of the primary tumour, pointing to polyclonal spread.
key_points: Liver metastases show cytotoxic T cell expansion and fewer regulatory T cells, yet still escape immune attack.
Elevated glutathione metabolism in the liver fosters glutamine addiction, and network analysis points to NRF2 as a regulator.
Inhibiting NRF2 and glutathione reduced liver metastasis in vivo and was associated with stronger antitumour immunity.

posts.title: hpci improves reproducibility of computational biology research by integrating Continuous Integration with High Performance Computing clusters
posts.authors: Menzies IJ, Urng E, Bouras G, et al.
posts.summary: hpci links continuous integration platforms such as GitHub Actions and GitLab CI to HPC schedulers (Slurm, PBS), so analysis pipelines can be tested automatically on a cluster. It runs as an unprivileged user over SSH and needs no cluster-side installation.
key_points: It ends with the same exit code as the HPC job, so CI steps stop when the job fails.
The authors show it on five computational biology workflows.
Written in Haskell, GPL-3.0.

posts.title: A Ribosomal RNA modification regulates translation of PI3K/AKT activators in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma
posts.authors: Rivera Pizana A, Faucher-Giguère L, Scott MS, et al.
posts.summary: SNORA81 directs pseudouridylation of 28S rRNA at U4636 and is linked to high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma. Depleting it changes the ribosome association of hundreds of mRNAs, many of them PI3K/AKT regulators.
key_points: Polysome profiling after SNORA81 depletion found 524 mRNAs with altered ribosome association, 485 independent of RNA abundance, including 29 PI3K/AKT regulators.
Depletion reduced AKT phosphorylation, cell growth and migration, and lowered ITGB4 and RASGRP2 protein.
ITGB4 expression partly restored growth after depletion.

posts.title: The impact of sex and ancestry on the molecular landscape of pancreatic adenocarcinoma
posts.authors: Chen CY, Arbet JY, Zhu C, et al.
posts.summary: A re-analysis of 7,527 pancreatic cancers from five datasets asks how sex and ancestry shape genomic instability and driver events. Ancestry was linked to both global and gene-specific mutation patterns.
key_points: SNV burden was higher in African-ancestry tumours and lower in Asian-ancestry tumours than in European-ancestry tumours.
GNAS driver SNVs were found more often in Asian and less often in African ancestry.
No sex or ancestry associations were found for KRAS overall, though individual KRAS variants trended with ancestry.

posts.title: An androgen-derived transcriptional state reveals signaling and mitochondrial vulnerabilities in cancer
posts.authors: Miao Y, Baba T
posts.summary: A transcriptional signature derived from dihydrotestosterone-treated mouse adrenal cells is projected onto human cancer cell lines as an 'androgen-suppressed transcriptional state' (ASTS). Using pharmacogenomic and CRISPR dependency data, the state is linked to drug resistance and dependencies.
key_points: Higher ASTS goes with resistance to EGFR-targeted drugs and lower EGFR dependency.
It also goes with greater dependency on mitochondrial translation and respiratory electron transport.
The associations are not due to one lineage and hold after adjusting for oncogenic drivers.

posts.title: sORF-Trans2MS: a two-module deep learning framework for sORF translation and MS-supported microprotein prediction
posts.authors: He J, Sui J, Chen Q, et al.
posts.summary: sORF-Trans2MS predicts which small open reading frames are translated, using two modules: one for Ribo-seq-supported sORFs and one for microproteins supported by mass spectrometry but not Ribo-seq.
key_points: Module I combines RNA-FM representations with a Transformer and reached an AUROC of 0.870 internally and 0.930 on an independent GENCODE set.
Module II adds ESM-2 protein representations and reached AUROC 0.804 internally and 0.785 on an independent mass spectrometry set.
Ablation highlighted upstream RNA context, including a signal about 50 nt upstream of the AUG.

posts.title: pre-miRBench: a multispecies benchmark and reference model for animal precursor microRNA prediction
posts.authors: Tzimotoudis D, Chatzitolios VK, Alexiou P, et al.
posts.summary: pre-miRBench is a benchmark of 7,056 pre-miRNA windows and 70,560 genomic negatives from 71 animal species, with four test sets that hold out species, miRNA family, both or neither. Six published predictors were retrained on it.
key_points: The reference model, an ensemble of three neural networks built with an LLM-agent system, had the highest mean AP (0.9809 versus 0.9719 for dnnPreMiR).
On the joint species-and-family holdout dnnPreMiR was slightly ahead, and the difference was not significant.

posts.title: ASTRA enables zero-shot super-resolution of spatial transcriptomics across capture geometries
posts.authors: Ye J, Cui Q
posts.summary: ASTRA is a pretrained model that reconstructs higher-resolution spatial expression from histology and measured RNA without fitting a model to each section. Training on arbitrarily shaped count-bearing regions lets one frozen model handle dense bins and separated spots.
key_points: On six held-out Visium HD sections it had higher correlations, lower errors and shorter run times than existing methods.
It improved colorectal tissue segmentation and tumour-boundary recovery.
The same checkpoint was applied to 43 invasive lobular carcinoma and 92 triple-negative breast cancer sections.

posts.title: lisaR: An LLM-Inferred Semantic Annotation of biological categories for gene set enrichment analysis
posts.authors: Velasco-Lopez C, de la Vega-Barranco G, Olmeda D
posts.summary: lisaR is an R package that runs GSEA on existing differential expression results and groups the output into 158 biological categories using fixed LLM-inferred dictionaries. No language model is queried during an analysis.
key_points: The dictionaries place 13,511 gene sets from GO, Reactome, WikiPathways, KEGG, BioCarta and PID into categories scored by four open-weight models.
Closed testing with Hommel's procedure gives a simultaneous lower bound on enriched gene sets per category.
Examples: melanoma biopsies on nivolumab and clear cell renal carcinoma proteomics.

posts.title: gRely: Relyability for genome trained sequence-to-expression models
posts.authors: Rafi AM, Eraslan G, Fletez-Brant K
posts.summary: gRely is a meta-model that estimates how likely a Borzoi variant-effect prediction is to get the eQTL direction right, instead of filtering by prediction magnitude alone.
key_points: On held-out tissues it reached a mean average precision of 0.885 (random baseline 0.744).
Among low-magnitude predictions it found a high-confidence subset with 76% accuracy against a 58% baseline.
It also improved AlphaGenome predictions.

posts.title: Oligo(uridine) tailing and exonucleolytic decay drive 40S ribosome degradation in response to stress
posts.authors: Diehl FF, Buskirk AR, Green R
posts.summary: When cells are starved, they destroy mature 40S ribosomal subunits, which means breaking down a large, stable RNA-protein complex. This study shows that the kinase RIOK3 recruits the uridylyl-transferase TUT7 and the exonuclease DIS3L2, and that U-tails on 18S rRNA drive its decay.
key_points: TUT7 adds oligo(uridine) tails to the 3' end of 18S rRNA in 40S ribosomes, and DIS3L2 recognises the tailed rRNA and degrades it 3'-5'.
Major decay intermediates are themselves uridylated again, so tailing and decay repeat in cycles.
Loss of DIS3L2 slows 18S rRNA decay during starvation and uridylated 18S rRNA accumulates.

figure.caption: Starvation-activated RIOK3 brings TUT7 to the 40S subunit; TUT7 adds U-tails to 18S rRNA and DIS3L2 trims them, in repeated rounds.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: 40S ribosome remodeling triggers 18S rRNA U-tailing and DIS3L2-dependent decay
posts.authors: Shah A, Coria AR, Miller JT, et al.
posts.summary: This companion study asks how defective 40S ribosomal subunits are committed to decay. Using in vitro reconstitution and nanopore direct RNA sequencing, it shows that RIOK3-driven remodeling exposes the 3' end of 18S rRNA, which is then uridylated and degraded by DIS3L2.
key_points: The atypical kinase RIOK3 remodels 40S subunits in vitro, exposing the 3' end of 18S rRNA.
Nanopore direct RNA sequencing shows this remodeling promotes oligo-uridylation, giving uridylated 18S rRNA decay intermediates.
DIS3L2 degrades the uridylated rRNA, and its exonucleolytic cleavage triggers endonucleolytic decay of 18S rRNA, amplifying turnover.

figure.caption: RIOK3 remodels the closed 40S subunit to expose the 18S rRNA 3' end, which is U-tailed, trimmed by DIS3L2 and then cut; nanopore sequencing reads the tails.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Mapping transcriptional responses to cellular perturbations with RNA fingerprinting
posts.authors: Grabski IN, Lee J, Blair JD, et al.
posts.summary: RNA fingerprinting is a statistical framework that maps the transcriptional response in a new experiment onto reference single-cell perturbation dictionaries. It learns a "fingerprint" for each perturbation and probabilistically assigns each query cell to one or more candidate perturbations.
key_points: Benchmarks on ground-truth datasets show accurate assignments at single-cell resolution, scaling to genome-wide screens and resolving combinatorial perturbations.
Applied to identify context-specific regulators of p53 under ribosomal stress and to characterise dose-dependent drug mechanisms of action.
Also used to uncover cytokine-driven B cell heterogeneity during secondary influenza infection in vivo.

figure.caption: A query single cell is matched probabilistically to perturbation fingerprints in a reference dictionary (CRISPR knockout, drug dose, combination).
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Himito: a graph-based toolkit for mitochondrial genome analysis using long reads
posts.authors: Su H, Huang Y, Durham TJ, et al.
posts.summary: Himito is a toolkit for analysing the mitochondrial genome with long reads. It filters nuclear mitochondrial insertions (NUMTs), builds a sequence graph of mtDNA diversity, assembles haplotypes, calls variants and analyses 5mC in one framework.
key_points: Benchmarking on reference datasets shows better assembly and variant calling than existing tools.
Applied to the All of Us v8 dataset, it identified pathogenic mtDNA variants and population-scale haplogroup diversity.
It also uncovered age-related genetic and epigenetic patterns in mtDNA.

posts.title: Punctuated mutagenesis promotes multi-step evolutionary adaptation in human cancers
posts.authors: Graser CJ, Wu W, Christini C, et al.
posts.summary: This modelling study asks how bursts of mutations (punctuated mutagenesis) change a tumour's ability to gain and keep fitness-enhancing adaptations. It also checks the predictions against TCGA data.
key_points: Punctuation helps most when adaptation needs several mutations that are individually harmful but jointly beneficial (crossing a fitness valley).
Mutations in close succession give mutants more chance to reach a fitness peak before going extinct.
TCGA tumours with APOBEC mutagenesis signatures show patterns consistent with higher rates of crossing fitness valleys.

posts.title: Protein large language model-assisted one-to-one gene homology mapping in cross-species single-cell transcriptome integration
posts.authors: Kuang ZY, Sun YC, Wei NN, et al.
posts.summary: Cross-species single-cell integration needs gene correspondences, and default many-to-many Ensembl mappings can create microclusters with no clear cell-type identity. This paper adds a protein language model to recover more one-to-one homology pairs.
key_points: A strict one-to-one scheme removes about 8% of homology pairs (about 900); the new fused mapping combines pLLM representations with sequence similarity to boost the number of pairs.
It achieves top performance in a benchmark of nine datasets, 11 species and more than 3.2 million cells.
It also identifies previously unannotated cell-type marker pairs across species.

posts.title: Single-cell transcriptome analysis reveals onco-fetal reprogramming with implications for drug resistance and clinical outcome
posts.authors: Xu Y, Chen S, Lu Z, et al.
posts.summary: The authors build a computational pipeline that compares fetal and tumour single-cell transcriptomes to identify onco-fetal (OF) cells across several cancer types. OF cells are stem-like and appear to shape the tumour microenvironment.
key_points: Core transcription factors in the programme include PTMA, ATF5, TCF4 and FOS.
OF cells impair B cell function and are linked to drug resistance and recurrence.
Pan-cancer analyses show OF cell markers universally predict adverse prognosis.

posts.title: Explainable data generation from observed small samples by matrix tri-factorization
posts.authors: Zhang B, Tao P, Ren J, et al.
posts.summary: Explainable Data Generation (EDG) represents a handful of high-dimensional samples with a low-dimensional latent representation that has a larger sample size, using matrix tri-factorization. It targets extreme sample scarcity, such as a single patient with a new disease.
key_points: Because the decomposition and reconstruction are transparent, the generated samples are explainable.
Tested on classification, clustering, feature selection and tipping-point prediction.
Used simulated and real datasets, including single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq data.

posts.title: The HDAC8-U2AF1 Axis Dysregulates DNA Damage-Responsive RNA Splicing and Creates Targetable Vulnerabilities in Acute Myeloid Leukemia
posts.authors: Zhang L, Fu YH, Hua WK, et al.
posts.summary: HDAC8 is overexpressed in over half of AML cases in patient datasets. This study shows it deacetylates the splicing factor U2AF1, which disrupts DNA damage-responsive splicing and homologous recombination repair.
key_points: TIP60 acetylates U2AF1 at lysines 23 and 175, needed for U2AF1 to join BRCA1 and BCLAF1 in a splicing complex; HDAC8 removes these marks.
HDAC8 hyperactivity causes widespread splicing dysregulation and raises sensitivity to splicing modulators and PARP inhibitors.
In preclinical models including PDXs, H3B-8800 plus talazoparib reduced leukemia burden and leukemia stem cell activity, with enhanced efficacy in combination.

posts.title: Citron kinase activity controls alternative splicing events that drive prostate cancer growth
posts.authors: Rawat C, Singh N, Dahiya UR, et al.
posts.summary: Citron (CIT) kinase drives prostate cancer progression, and its substrates are enriched in alternative splicing regulators. The study follows the splicing regulator THRAP3 as a representative substrate.
key_points: CIT phosphorylates THRAP3 directly, which sets THRAP3's RNA binding to CIT-controlled pre-mRNA targets (identified by CLIP-seq).
CIT-dependent THRAP3-bound transcripts stimulated growth in cell lines, xenografts and patient-derived organoids.
An antisense oligo that blocks THRAP3 recruitment inhibited growth of cell lines and PDX-derived organoids but not benign cells.

posts.title: Targeting SUV39H2 exon skipping reverses resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors via transcriptional activation of p21
posts.authors: Yu S, Gong X, Yang Y, et al.
posts.summary: CDK4/6 inhibitors are standard care for ER-positive breast cancer but resistance limits them. This study finds a splicing-mediated mechanism: exon 2 inclusion in SUV39H2 drives its overexpression in resistant cells.
key_points: Higher exon 2 inclusion in SUV39H2 correlates with poor prognosis in patients with breast cancer.
Gapmer antisense oligonucleotides or a methyltransferase inhibitor overcome resistance and restore therapy-induced senescence.
Mechanistically, this removes H3K9me3 at enhancers and opens chromatin at promoters of senescence-associated secretory phenotype genes.

posts.title: PNLDC1 deadenylase affects translational rate and cell proliferation in mESCs
posts.authors: Skeparnias I, Shaukat AN, Katsioulas C, et al.
posts.summary: PNLDC1 is a deadenylase known for pre-piRNA trimming, but its wider role in poly(A) tail removal is poorly understood. This study maps its regulation during mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation and tests what happens when it is lost.
key_points: Pnldc1 promoter methylation pattern is linked to its repression during differentiation; knockout mESCs stay viable and pluripotent.
RNA-seq and polysome profiling show Pnldc1 loss downregulates translation gene networks and lowers overall translation rate.
Virtual screening with a PARN-based homology model led to 12 compounds; two affected stress-response and signal-transduction genes and suppressed aberrant proliferation.

posts.title: Risk factors for postoperative recurrence of sacral chordoma: an eleven-year single-centre retrospective study
posts.authors: Du X, Wei H, Zhang B, et al.
posts.summary: A retrospective review of 34 consecutive patients with sacral chordoma, all with R0 resection, treated at one centre between 2013 and 2024. It looks for independent risk factors for recurrence.
key_points: Recurrence occurred in 19 of 34 patients (55.9%) after a median 36 months; median recurrence-free survival was 33 months and nine patients developed distant metastases.
Tumour diameter of 65 mm or more (HR 3.42) and previous surgery (HR 4.57) were independent risk factors.
Postoperative targeted therapy was associated with lower recurrence (HR 0.31), but treatment was not randomised so this needs caution.

posts.title: Rural-Urban Disparities in Survival Among Patients With Malignant Primary Osseous Neoplasms of the Spine and Sacropelvis: A Population-Based Cohort Study
posts.authors: Dietrich G, Tambunan J, Haynal E, et al.
posts.summary: A SEER-based cohort of 3,631 patients (2000-2023) with chordoma, chondrosarcoma, osteosarcoma or Ewing sarcoma of the spine or sacropelvis, asking whether rural residence independently affects survival.
key_points: Rural residence was not independently associated with overall survival (HR 0.95) or cause-specific survival (HR 0.94).
Higher county income was associated with better survival in a graded way (HR 0.68 for counties above $120,000).
Surgery was associated with lower mortality, whereas radiotherapy was not.

posts.title: Osteochondroma of the Sella Turcica: A Rare Mimic in the Spectrum of Sellar Masses
posts.authors: Jain S, Osama MA, Gupta A, et al.
posts.summary: A case report of what the authors call the sixth known sellar osteochondroma, in a 30-year-old woman with progressive visual loss. The calcified sellar-suprasellar mass was first suspected to be a calcified pituitary adenoma or chordoma.
key_points: Endoscopic transsphenoidal resection and histology confirmed osteochondroma.
Chordoma is mentioned only as an initial differential diagnosis.
Vision improved significantly after surgery, and adjuvant radiotherapy was given.

posts.title: Sphenoid Sinus Mucocele with Clival and Sellar Extension Mimicking a Neoplastic Lesion: A Case Report
posts.authors: Ovalles-Álvarez HK, Calderón-Garcidueñas AL, Villegas-Hernández JC, et al.
posts.summary: A case report of a 28-year-old man whose lesion eroded the sphenoid sinus and clivus and was first thought to be a chordoma. Intraoperative study showed a sphenoid sinus mucocele.
key_points: Clival extension is a rare presentation and can mimic neoplasms such as chordoma.
The lesion was resected and the patient did well.
Sphenoid mucoceles can be dangerous because they compress nearby critical structures.

posts.title: A gene-centric analysis of copy number variation reveals tumour suppressor modulation of cancer risk and novel associations with common diseases
posts.authors: Matthews S, Seoighe C, Wheeler GL
posts.summary: Instead of analysing CNVs one by one or by region, this work links whole-gene copy number changes to phenotype. It first checks the approach against gene expression in GTEx, then tests cancer risk and other diseases.
key_points: Found 34 gene deletions associated with cancer incidence, including a germline link for 13q14 deletions that region-based methods missed.
Whole-gene loss of tumour suppressor genes was associated with overall cancer risk.
The total number of whole-gene losses predicted cancer risk even without known cancer-related genes; associations were also found for asthma and heart attack.

posts.title: Niche-dependent epistasis within the cancer genome shapes metastatic fitness
posts.authors: Liu X, He L, Zhao M, et al.
posts.summary: Using lung metastasis in mice, the authors mapped gene-by-gene-by-environment (GxGxE) epistasis with combinatorial CRISPR perturbation plus depletion of defined host myeloid populations.
key_points: The metastatic niche first selects tumour cells on gene-by-gene epistatic fitness, then drives transcriptome convergence regardless of genotype.
Removing anatomically distinct myeloid populations reshaped the epistasis landscape despite identical tumour genotypes.
The interaction size and sign were set by niche cells.

posts.title: RBFOX2 restrains oncogenic cell plasticity in Group 3 medulloblastoma
posts.authors: Sah RK, Yan X, Louis L, et al.
posts.summary: This study identifies the splicing regulator RBFOX2 as a suppressor of cell plasticity in Group 3 medulloblastoma. OTX2 opposes it by directing a different alternative splicing programme.
key_points: OTX2 alters the RBFOX2 RNA-binding landscape, limiting RBFOX2 at cytoskeletal loci and suppressing exon inclusion.
RBFOX2 loss rewires splicing and transcription towards plastic, mesenchymal-like and undifferentiated states.
RBFOX2-low states mark highly plastic cells in patient tumours and xenografts.

posts.title: Nuclear RNA cap-chaperones eIF4E and NCBP2 govern distinct fates for 1000s of mRNAs uncovering an unexpected regulatory point in gene expression
posts.authors: Mars J-C, Embree CM, Kraljacic B-C, et al.
posts.summary: The nuclear cap-binding protein NCBP2 is usually seen as a single housekeeping checkpoint for mRNA processing. This preprint shows the translation factor eIF4E also acts in the nucleus and affects mostly different mRNAs.
key_points: Changing eIF4E or NCBP2 levels gives distinct transcriptomic and splicing signatures across thousands of transcripts, with few shared splicing events.
The authors propose mRNA Specification by Cap Chaperones (SOCCs).
The two proteins sit in separate nuclear regions and have non-overlapping protein-partner networks.

posts.title: Circular Data Analysis for Spatial Omics
posts.authors: Shin J, Yoo J, Cho Y, et al.
posts.summary: Many omics quantities such as circadian phase, cell-cycle position and cell orientation are periodic, and treating them as ordinary linear variables creates artificial breaks. This paper gives practical guidance, with R software, for circular analysis in single-cell and spatial omics.
key_points: Covers circular representation, inference, clustering, regression, machine learning and spatial analysis.
Case studies use spatial transcriptomics: circadian peak phase in a mouse Alzheimer's model and cell-cycle position in human ovarian cancer.
Shows when spatial modelling is not warranted, depending on how the angle and tissue heterogeneity are defined.

posts.title: Pervasive Backdoor Vulnerabilities in Genomic Foundation Models
posts.authors: Ni S, Wang Q, Wei C, et al.
posts.summary: This preprint shows that genomic foundation models can be backdoored during fine-tuning by poisoning a small fraction of training data with short DNA motifs, including triggers derived from transposon terminal inverted repeats.
key_points: Attacks work across encoder-based and autoregressive models, tasks and scales, while clean-task performance stays almost unchanged.
Larger models were not more resistant.
A two-stage auditing framework flags poisoned sequences using single-nucleotide mutation sensitivity, without knowing the trigger.

posts.title: A Measure of Transcriptional Dyscoordination for Quantifying Aging in Single Cells
posts.authors: Yang Y, Hess PR, Chen XE, et al.
posts.summary: An unsupervised framework that scores transcriptional dyscoordination in single cells as deviation from a learned, predictable structure that accounts for technical noise.
key_points: Dyscoordination rises after genotoxic injury and senescence induction, then falls after senolytic depletion.
It increases with chronological age across mouse, rat and human tissues, especially in regenerative compartments.
In human T cells it rises with clonal expansion and effector function, and links to chromatin-based mitotic age and genome instability.

posts.title: Identifiable inverse optimal transport for single-cell state transitions
posts.authors: Dong H, Gong Y, Liu Y
posts.summary: In balanced optimal transport, signed effects of target-state programmes are unidentifiable. UOT-IOT is a semi-relaxed inverse transport framework that restores measurable effects and gives a rank condition for local identifiability.
key_points: Recovers coefficients in ground-truth benchmarks and has the lowest transition error against seven methods under matched conditions.
IFN/HLA programmes are associated with patient treatment response, and EMT with drug sensitivity and perturbation-induced state changes.
The PERSIST-IOT module improves prediction of future population composition in an independent experiment.

posts.title: Primary Intraosseous Cavernous Hemangioma of the Petrous Bone Involving the Jugular Fossa Mimicking a Jugular Paraganglioma: A Radiologic-Pathologic Correlation and Review of Relevant Literature
posts.authors: Kedar K, Arora D, Rao AK, et al.
posts.summary: Case report of a benign vascular tumour (primary intraosseous cavernous hemangioma) in the petrous temporal bone with jugular fossa involvement, which looked like a jugular paraganglioma on imaging. Chordoma appears only as one item in the differential diagnosis.
key_points: A 46-year-old man presented with progressive unilateral sensorineural hearing loss; MRI showed a heterogeneously enhancing jugular foramen lesion with cerebellopontine angle extension.
High-resolution CT showed a coarse "honeycomb" trabecular pattern with smooth bone expansion, pointing to an intraosseous origin.
Histology confirmed cavernous hemangioma; the authors list imaging features that help separate it from paraganglioma, schwannoma, meningioma, chordoma, chondrosarcoma and metastasis.

posts.title: Tangermeme: a toolkit for understanding cis-regulatory logic using deep learning models
posts.authors: Schreiber J
posts.summary: Tangermeme is a highly optimised toolkit for the steps that come after a genomic deep learning model has been trained. It is meant to turn the cis-regulatory patterns a model has learned into insights a person can read.
key_points: Covers "everything-but-the-model" for genomic deep learning, so the analysis is separated from model training.
Aims to distil learned cis-regulatory patterns from models into human-interpretable results.
The abstract gives no benchmark numbers; the paper demonstrates typical uses of the toolkit.

figure.caption: Tangermeme sits around a trained genomic deep learning model and helps turn what it learned about DNA motifs into readable cis-regulatory logic.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Spatial omics resolves adrenergic and mesenchymal cell states in neuroblastoma
posts.authors: Patel AG, Ashenberg O, Collins NB, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq, bulk RNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics of 54 neuroblastoma tumours show tumour cells sitting in neighbourhoods separate from immune and stromal cells. Signatures taken from cell lines failed to find mesenchymal (MES) tumour cells, so the authors built new adrenergic (ADRN) and MES signatures from early-passage patient-derived xenografts.
key_points: The new PDX-derived signatures identify MES tumour cells in patient tumours, validated by transcriptomic, epigenomic, proteomic, ultrastructural and functional assays.
Established cell line-derived signatures could not identify MES neuroblastoma cells in patients.
High MES gene expression correlates with worse event-free and overall survival.

figure.caption: Cell-line signatures miss mesenchymal cells in patient neuroblastomas, while signatures from early-passage xenografts find them and link them to worse survival.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Universal Germline Genetic Testing after a Diagnosis of Cancer
posts.authors: Stadler ZK, Maio A, Khurram A, et al.
posts.summary: Germline sequencing of 39,184 unselected patients with solid tumours across 32 tumour types, covering more than 90 cancer predisposition genes, tests whether age at diagnosis is a good rule for who should be tested. Patients were grouped as early, average or late onset relative to each tumour type.
key_points: Pathogenic variant prevalence fell with age at diagnosis: 18.4% in early-onset, 15.6% in average-onset and 12.3% in late-onset tumours.
Variants in high- and moderate-penetrance genes accounted for the excess in early-onset cases.
Testing only patients diagnosed before age 50 would miss 4,601 carriers, 72% of all variants found.

figure.caption: Pathogenic germline variant carriers appear at every age at diagnosis, so an age-50 testing rule leaves most of them untested.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: A preinvasive regulatory T cell axis for lung cancer interception
posts.authors: Gamble S, Whiteman ZE, Peinador-Marín C, et al.
posts.summary: Multi-omic, cross-tissue immune profiling of patients with preinvasive lung lesions followed by bronchoscopy and CT shows that effector regulatory CD4 T cells expressing BATF build up in high-grade premalignant airway lesions. These cells are clonally related to circulating counterparts, so progression can be followed in blood.
key_points: Circulating effector regulatory T cells rose during preinvasive progression, and a clonally coordinated circuit marked rapid progression in early-stage NSCLC found by CT screening.
In a mouse carcinogen model, an analogous blood-airway-lymph node axis appeared, with expansion of lung BATF-positive T cells and immature tertiary lymphoid structures.
PI3Kδ inhibition blocked these structures, raised local cDC1s and reduced lung tumour incidence and size.

posts.title: Mapping the functional dark proteome in cancer
posts.authors: Prensner JR, Freed-Pastor WA, Abelin JG, et al.
posts.summary: This Perspective, indexed as a review, surveys the cancer "dark proteome": uncharacterised proteins that come from alternative genomic loci or altered RNA translation. It covers the classes found so far, their functions in cancer cells and their potential as therapeutic targets.
key_points: Over the past decade the dark proteome has been resolved in much greater depth, with diverse classes of dark proteins each having thousands of members.
Individual dark proteins are being shown to act in cancer cell biology and to be possible targets.
Open gaps include how they are regulated, how they contribute to cancer phenotypes and antigenicity, and whether they can be made into clinical-grade therapies.

posts.title: Interpretable machine learning enables de novo mapping of cell type-specific RNA splicing regulation from scRNA-seq data
posts.authors: Xiang X, Yang X
posts.summary: CASREL is a machine learning framework that infers candidate regulatory links between RNA-binding proteins and alternative splicing directly from single-cell RNA-seq, without needing prior protein-RNA binding annotations. It combines ensemble learning with Shapley additive explanations to interpret the model.
key_points: It uses features specific to single-cell splicing profiles: polarised isoform usage, little averaging of regulatory programs and resilience to expression noise.
Applications across several tissues and cell types showed robustness, accuracy and biological relevance, according to the authors.
Offers a way to map cell-specific splicing regulation where CLIP and RNA-binding protein perturbation experiments are too low-throughput or only bulk.

posts.title: Wavelet-based whole genome doubling aware single-cell copy number calling
posts.authors: Wesley BK, Wos F, Germer S, et al.
posts.summary: Songbird is a copy number caller for low-coverage single-cell whole genome sequencing (such as Direct Library Preparation+). Unlike tools that rely on read depth ratios in fixed bins, it can detect whole genome doubling, and it is built for frozen samples with variable DNA preservation.
key_points: Outperforms existing tools at both breakpoint identification and true copy number detection.
Robust down to very low coverage (below 0.1x for the method it targets).
Works across genome versions (hg19, hg38, hs.1) and extends to other Tn5-tagmentation single-cell WGS methods.

posts.title: Multimodal Gene Expression Deep Learning for Predicting Sentinel Lymph Node Macro-metastasis in Early Breast Cancer: Development and Validation in the SCAN-B Cohort
posts.authors: Zhang D, Staaf J, Bendahl PO, et al.
posts.summary: Three deep learning models (a multilayer perceptron, a pathway-informed sparse neural network and a transformer) were trained on tumour gene expression, with or without preoperative clinical data, to predict sentinel lymph node macro-metastasis in 6,836 node-negative breast cancer patients from SCAN-B. They were compared with XGBoost in an independent test set.
key_points: The transformer did best on gene expression and needed the least prior gene selection.

Adding gene expression to clinical data raised ROC AUC from 0.596 to 0.693 in the test set, and could spare 27.2% of patients a sentinel node biopsy at 92.1% sensitivity; the combined model did not beat expression alone.
Paired biopsy and surgical specimens (n=116) agreed well, supporting future biopsy-based use.

posts.title: Latent causal diffusions for single-cell perturbation modeling
posts.authors: Lorch L, Zhang J, Bunne C, et al.
posts.summary: The latent causal diffusion (LCD) model treats single-cell gene expression as a stationary diffusion process seen through measurement noise, and predicts how unseen combinations of perturbations shift expression. A companion method, CLIPR, reads direct causal effects between genes out of the learned dynamics.
key_points: LCD outperformed established approaches at predicting distribution shifts for unseen perturbation combinations in scRNA-seq screens.
CLIPR provably identifies causal effects under a linear drift assumption and recovered causal structure in simulations and a genome-wide perturbation screen.
In that screen it grouped genes into coherent functional modules and resolved causal relationships that standard differential expression cannot.

posts.title: METANet: a supervised ensemble learning framework for reconstructing direct and functional tissue-specific transcription factor networks
posts.authors: Jung WJ, Acharya S, Ruskin DP, et al.
posts.summary: METANet is a supervised ensemble learning framework that predicts which genes a transcription factor directly binds in a given tissue. It combines TF motifs, cis-regulatory element activity and both linear and non-linear expression-derived features.
key_points: Applied to 36 human tissues, its maps beat established methods at finding direct, likely functional TF targets validated by ChIP-seq and gene ontology.
Tissue-specific regulation was captured as well as by existing methods.
The maps allow reproducible gene-trait associations to be identified.

posts.title: NoiBic: a noise-tolerant biclustering algorithm for high-throughput gene expression data analysis
posts.authors: Long C, Li J, Liu B, et al.
posts.summary: NoiBic is a biclustering algorithm for finding gene modules in transcriptomic data when technical and biological noise hides coherent patterns. It uses a longest approximate common subsequence step to find seeds, then expands columns in a noise-aware way.
key_points: On simulated data with controlled coherency, size, noise and overlap, it recovered planted biclusters accurately, especially under noise and overlap.
On bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data it found biologically meaningful gene modules and cell type-associated biclusters.
Implemented in C++17 with benchmark data archived on Zenodo.

posts.title: ProFormer: generalizable classification of single-cell and plasma proteomes using deep learning
posts.authors: Krull KK, Kühn A, Höhn J, et al.
posts.summary: ProFormer is a transformer pipeline that classifies samples directly from tabular MS1-level features of peptide ions, skipping the usual protein identification and interpretation step. It was tested on single-cell and plasma proteomes.
key_points: Outperformed traditional machine learning and image-based CNNs across 14 evaluated architectures.
Classified single-cell proteomes by cell type, cell cycle stage or differentiation trajectory, and patient disease status from plasma proteomes.
Explainable AI analysis works at single-peptide resolution.

posts.title: RAFA: RNA all-atom structure reconstruction from sparse anchor coordinates
posts.authors: Wang L, Zeng Z
posts.summary: RAFA is a C++ command-line tool that rebuilds a full all-atom RNA structure from sparse or partial anchor coordinates, as produced by coarse-grained modelling or low-resolution fitting. It retrieves known 3-5 nucleotide all-atom fragments, fits them to local anchors and combines overlapping estimates by weighted consensus.
key_points: On an RNA3DB train/test split with no library-test pair above 80% sequence identity, RAFA gave lower all-atom RMSD than Arena in 73.3% of target-mode comparisons.
Gains were largest when the input had the fewest structural constraints.

posts.title: STAT3D as a new image-tailored Xenium-based spatial transcriptomics tool for accurately dissecting the tumor microenvironment
posts.authors: Ajazi K, Volpe M, Roylands J, et al.
posts.summary: STAT3D is a customisable pipeline for whole-tumour Xenium slides that does 3D cell segmentation on only the sharpest optical z-planes, to avoid blur and signal bleed-through from out-of-focus layers. It then maps transcripts to cells and annotates them automatically using standard tools such as Seurat and SingleR.
key_points: The "image-tailored" strategy combines only the sharpest z-planes to compute single-cell features and spatial distances.
Fully automated annotation supports exploring infiltrating cell types, interactions and tissue architecture.
Aimed at problems that built-in platform tools such as Xenium Explorer cannot solve.

posts.title: SLC39-driven zinc influx orchestrates pleiotropic tumor-immune system cross-talk to establish immune suppression in colorectal cancer
posts.authors: Hong SJ, Park S, Kim S, et al.
posts.summary: Bulk multi-omics of 258 colorectal cancer patients, single-cell transcriptomics, spatial profiling and functional assays identify a zinc-driven immunosuppressive circuit. Three solute carrier archetypes emerged, with an SLC39-enriched subtype matching CMS2-like immune-desert tumours.
key_points: SLC39-mediated zinc influx activates CDX2, which uses a distal enhancer to switch on CD24 in tumour cells; CD24-high cells form spatial niches with SIGLEC10-expressing macrophages and dendritic cells.
CD24 blockade restored macrophage engulfment of tumour cells in vitro.
A seven-gene signature predicted immunotherapy response across five colorectal cancer cohorts.

posts.title: Cell-type separability predicts annotation accuracy and outweighs algorithm choice: a factorial benchmark across seven scRNA paradigms
posts.authors: Wardhana O, Zeng Z, Lu X
posts.summary: A benchmark of 63 cell-type annotation tools from seven families (marker-based, similarity-based, classical ML, deep learning, semi-supervised, LLM and foundation models) on a Taguchi orthogonal array that varied cell number, class imbalance, cell-type number and differential-expression strength independently, then extended to real data and cross-platform transfer.
key_points: How separable cell types are in a shared expression embedding (kNN purity) predicted accuracy near-linearly, R2 0.85-0.99.
Dataset identity accounted for about 84% of kappa variance and tool identity about 4%; leading cell-level families were within 0.06 kappa of each other.
Strong performers were spread across families, e.g. Seurat label transfer, singleCellNet and mLLMCelltype.

posts.title: methylTFR: Computational quantification of transcription factor activity from DNA methylation
posts.authors: Gunduz IB, Nitsch R, Murugan SK, et al.
posts.summary: methylTFR is an R package that scores transcription factor activity from DNA methylation across TF-binding sites, giving a low-dimensional, interpretable activity profile.
key_points: In 147 human immune cell methylomes it found cell-type-specific regulators, including CEBP and ETS family activity in myeloid cells.
In CD4+ T cells the scores resolved the naive-to-memory trajectory and pointed to AP-1 factors as memory regulators.
It works on sparse single-cell methylomes and can be combined with expression and accessibility in joint factor models.

posts.title: Reconstructing donor genotypes from scRNA-seq for downstream eQTL and HLA-TCR analysis
posts.authors: Kockelbergh H, Astley J, Kichula KM, et al.
posts.summary: scTAPAS reconstructs donor genotypes directly from single-cell RNA-seq reads, so single-cell eQTL and HLA analyses become possible when no matched genotype data exist. It was applied to 5-prime scRNA-seq from the COMBAT COVID-19 blood atlas.
key_points: Despite testing only 18.0% of the variants from array genotyping plus imputation, it recovered 68.6% of cell type-eGene pairs with strong effect-size concordance.
The derived variants support imputation of classical HLA alleles and HLA-aware QTL analysis.
With matched single-cell TCR data it found CD4+ T cell-specific associations between HLA class II alleles and TCR V-alpha gene usage.

posts.title: Slide-level batch structure limits histology-guided supervision of transcriptomic foundation models
posts.authors: McConnell U, Nonchev K, Koelzer VH, et al.
posts.summary: Tests whether matched H&E histology can improve transcriptomic foundation model representations when used as a training-time supervisory signal that is dropped at inference, using spot-based spatial transcriptomics.
key_points: Across three foundation models, histology-guided supervision gave no consistent aggregate gain in cross-donor annotation transfer, even though histology alone transferred much better.
Spot-based expression embeddings are low-dimensional and strongly structured by slide identity, which limits the shared gene-morphology signal.
Guidance helped some morphologically distinctive classes but reduced held-out gene predictivity broadly; the authors advise diagnosing slide-specific structure first.

posts.title: Downstream mRNA Secondary Structure, Not Codon Elongation Supply, Coordinates Co-Translational Protein Folding Across the Human Ribosomal Exit Tunnel
posts.authors: Saad Ul Hassan M, Jabeen I, Kiani YS
posts.summary: Analysis of 1,270 high-resolution human crystal structures (410,151 residues) mapped to their mRNA transcripts asks what paces translation to help nascent proteins fold. Synonymous codon choice was separated from amino acid identity by orthogonal linear projection.
key_points: Codon supply metrics (tAI and CAI) showed negligible independent coupling with downstream structure once amino acid identity was removed.

Downstream mRNA minimum free energy showed a small, consistent correlation centred about +15 to +16 codons, matching the ribosome geometry (packing density r = -0.0699, B-factor r = +0.0614, SASA r = +0.0492).
The effect explains about 0.49% of local packing variance, so it is modest.

posts.title: Quantification method affects replicability of eQTL analysis, colocalization, and TWAS
posts.authors: Cole N, Wu WH, Head ST, et al.
posts.summary: Asks how the transcriptomic reference annotation and the RNA-seq quantification method change eQTL mapping, colocalization and TWAS, across 48 GTEx tissues and seven phenotypes. This is a newly listed version (v3) of a preprint first posted in 2025.
key_points: These upstream choices substantially affect eQTL detection and gene expression prediction, with downstream effects on colocalization and TWAS.
Concordant results across pipelines are enriched for longer genes, genes with more isoforms and higher expression heritability.
The authors call for standardised practices to make genetic association studies reproducible.

posts.title: scDEcrypter: Uncertainty-aware differential expression analysis for viral infection in scRNA-seq
posts.authors: Zhong L, Ensberg K, Tibbetts S, et al.
posts.summary: scDEcrypter is a penalised two-way mixture model for differential expression in virus-infected single-cell data, where viral reads are sparse, infected cells are under-labelled and bystander cells respond too. It uses partial infection and cell-type labels to estimate latent cell-state probabilities and gives fast permutation-based p-values. This is a newly listed version (v2).
key_points: In simulations and two viral infection datasets it recovered infected cell states better than existing approaches.
It identified more biologically coherent infection-associated genes and enriched pathways.

posts.title: Mechanistic Decoding of Pharmacodynamic Intratumoral Heterogeneity: A Pan-Cancer Regulatory Framework
posts.authors: Ren Z, Ren Y, Li Z, et al.
posts.summary: Links single-cell transcriptomes from 1,279 samples across 24 cancer types to drug response profiles for 1,218 compounds to explain why coexisting subclones respond differently to drugs ("pharmacodynamic intratumoral heterogeneity"). A multi-omics network analysis in lung adenocarcinoma adds regulation, mutations, cell-cell communication and alternative splicing.
key_points: 425 hub genes were consistently linked to predicted response heterogeneity.

In the lung adenocarcinoma case study: 3 transcription factors, 41 genomic alterations, 5 ligand-receptor pairs and 8 genes with opposing splice isoforms were associated with the response programs, converging on 6 core pathways.
Reports experimental validation and an online platform, PharmITH.

posts.title: PIE: Generalizing perturbation effects across unseen perturbations, contexts and datasets
posts.authors: Verma R, Adduri A, Bevilacqua B, et al.
posts.summary: PIE predicts the population-level effect of a perturbation in a given cellular context, directly outputting differentially expressed genes and expression changes. It uses external biological knowledge, baseline expression and observed perturbation responses, and handles input sources with variable feature sets.
key_points: On the Replogle Nadig dataset it reaches state-of-the-art performance on most metrics in all tested generalisation settings, including unseen contexts and perturbations together.
For differentially expressed gene prediction it achieves 1.2 to 3.2 times the AUPRC of the strongest baseline in each setting.

posts.title: MERFISH-based pooled genetic screening reveals cell non-autonomous phenotypes in intact tissue
posts.authors: Jin K, Saunders RA, Zhang J, et al.
posts.summary: An imaging-based pooled screening method that detects perturbation identities and endogenous RNAs by amplification-free MERFISH, so both perturbed cells and their neighbours can be profiled in intact tissue. It was applied to a genetic mosaic mouse liver screen of about 200 genes in hepatocytes.
key_points: Amplification-free detection raised perturbation barcode recovery about 10-fold and endogenous transcript recovery 2.5-fold.
1.5 million cells were profiled, mapping both cell-autonomous hepatocyte responses and changes in neighbouring immune and vascular cells.
Examples include pDC-like cells gathering near hepatocytes with impaired V-ATPase function, and angiogenic responses near Vhl-perturbed hepatocytes.

posts.title: Recurrent Dedifferentiated Clival Chondrosarcoma Presenting 32 Years after Initial Treatment: A Case Report
posts.authors: Ravindran PK, Keizer ME, Erdem ZB, et al.
posts.summary: Case report of a 66-year-old woman with a recurrent clival lesion first suspected to be a chordoma. Histology showed a conventional chondrosarcoma with a small dedifferentiated component and an IDH1 R132 mutation, 32 years after subtotal resection and radiosurgery.
key_points: Illustrates the diagnostic challenge of telling skull-base chondrosarcoma from chordoma.
Careful histologic sampling found a dedifferentiated focus of under 5% of the tumour that could otherwise be undergraded.
Argues for subtype-driven treatment, molecular annotation and multicentre registries for these rare tumours.

posts.title: Mechanism of spliceosome termination
posts.authors: Boreikaite V, Faraway R, Vorländer MK, et al.
posts.summary: Cryo-EM structures of human spliceosomes at two stages of termination show how the post-catalytic complex is taken apart. The RNA helicases DHX15 and Aquarius unwind the active site, DBR1 debranches the intron, and DHX35 then ejects it so the spliceosome can be recycled.
key_points: A previously unknown debranched-intron spliceosome is described, with DBR1 tethered to the complex.
DHX35 with GPATCH1-WDR83, assisted by YJU2B, ejects the intron from the U6 snRNA-5' splice site duplex.
On defective spliceosomes stalled on aberrant introns, YJU2B partners with LENG1 to guide the same helicase for quality-control termination.

figure.caption: Three stages end the spliceosome: DHX15 and Aquarius unwind it, DBR1 debranches the intron, and DHX35 ejects the intron, with YJU2B and LENG1 steering the quality-control route.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: tRNA dosage regulates lineage dependency and resistance in prostate cancer
posts.authors: Kim YS, Arora S, Young D, et al.
posts.summary: Small RNA sequencing in prostate cancer identified tRNA(UCU) as a regulator of lineage transitions and therapy resistance. Its level tunes a translational programme centred on SWI/SNF chromatin remodellers that keeps tumour cells in their lineage.
key_points: TARDBP and ZSCAN29 bind the tRNA(UCU) genomic locus and regulate its expression.
Changing tRNA(UCU) can reprogram lineage dependence and restore sensitivity to therapies that target the androgen receptor.
In patients, tRNA(UCU) is lower in neuroendocrine prostate cancer, and its loss is linked to faster metastasis and poorer survival.

figure.caption: TARDBP and ZSCAN29 set tRNA(UCU) level; high levels keep the SWI/SNF programme and lineage, low levels give a neuroendocrine, resistant state.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Dynamics of human cardiogenesis and its disruption in trisomy 21
posts.authors: Cranley J, Kanemaru K, Bayraktar S, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell and spatial multiomics of the developing human heart define 21 tissue niches, which the authors use to build TissueTypist, a niche classification tool that works across resolutions. Hearts with trisomy 21 had fewer compact cardiomyocytes and more apoptosis than euploid hearts.
key_points: High-resolution profiling of the sinoatrial node resolved three pacemaker cell subtypes along a linear axis.
Trajectories mapped atrial and ventricular cardiomyocyte maturation and pointed to a lipid-metabolic switch.
The trisomy 21 finding was checked in isogenic trisomy 21 and euploid iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes.

figure.caption: A map of heart niches with the sinoatrial node showing three pacemaker subtypes on one axis, and trisomy 21 hearts with fewer compact cardiomyocytes and more apoptosis.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Ribosome remodeling drives translation adaptation during viral infection and cellular stress
posts.authors: Tsai HY, Liu L, Fleming RH, et al.
posts.summary: Ribosome composition is reprogrammed in response to infection and stress. During infection with non-segmented negative-sense viruses, rpL40 moves to a non-canonical site on the small subunit near the mRNA entry site, giving ribosomes that preferentially bind viral mRNAs.
key_points: These specialised ribosomes boost viral protein synthesis that is needed for replication.
Viruses appear to have co-opted a previously unrecognised endogenous ribosome remodeling programme triggered by metabolic stress.
Presented as a conserved mechanism for dynamic protein synthesis in pathogen and cellular adaptation.

posts.title: Translocation-induced enhancer rewiring reveals cryptic oncogenic circuits in multiple myeloma
posts.authors: Zheng E, Li Q, Dou X, et al.
posts.summary: TransFinder integrates SMRT long-read sequencing, Hi-C, H3K27ac profiling and RNA-seq to resolve cryptic IGH enhancer translocations and the oncogenes they hijack by reading the enhancer-promoter neo-loops at the breakpoints. It found previously unrecognised translocations in multiple myeloma.
key_points: Identified t(5;8)(q35;q24) and t(1;22)(q25;q13) as new enhancer-hijacking events, and CRISPR-engineered t(1;22) recapitulated the induction.
Pharmacological inhibition of CBX7 suppressed myeloma cell proliferation.
Also found enhancer hijacking in chronic myeloid leukaemia and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma.

posts.title: Systematic benchmarking of ambient RNA decontamination tools to advance precision in single-cell transcriptomic analysis
posts.authors: Nie Y, Zhang C, Tan J, et al.
posts.summary: Seven tools that remove ambient RNA from single-cell RNA-seq were compared on simulated and experimental datasets from several tissues and species. The tools showed distinct strengths in accuracy, robustness and handling of subtype-specific contamination.
key_points: DecontX gave the most accurate contamination-level estimates.
scAR was the most robust across conditions but tended to overestimate contamination.
CellClear did best at resolving closely related cell subtypes.

posts.title: Error correction algorithms for efficient gene expression quantification in single cell transcriptomics with Arcane
posts.authors: Zentgraf J, Schmitz JE, Keller A, et al.
posts.summary: Arcane is a new tool for turning droplet-based scRNA-seq reads into an expression matrix, with new algorithms for barcode correction, read-to-gene mapping and UMI resolution. It builds on the Fourway method for finding k-mers within Hamming distance 1.
