posts.title: CSGDA: A Cell State-Guided Graph Domain Adaptation Network for Single-Cell Drug Response Prediction
posts.authors: Yan F, Xie D, Cao X, et al.
posts.summary: CSGDA predicts single-cell drug response when the training and target data differ, for example from cell lines to tissue or from primary to metastatic tumours. It maps gene expression into functional cell states and uses graph domain adaptation with an overlap penalty to cope with the shift.
key_points: On five scRNA-seq datasets it beat the previous best method SSDA4Drug by about 6 percentage points in accuracy and AUPR.
Integrated gradients on a cross-metastasis cisplatin dataset highlighted genes linked to drug resistance.

posts.title: scURL: Uncertainty-Sharpened Representation Learning for Single-cell Multi-omics Clustering
posts.authors: Liu H, Yu D, Li W, et al.
posts.summary: scURL clusters single-cell multi-omics data while estimating how reliable each omics layer is for each cell. It turns that uncertainty into cell-wise weights for fusing the layers and calibrates each layer before fusion.
key_points: It outperformed existing clustering methods on ten datasets.
It stayed robust under dropout noise and found cell populations supported by marker genes.

posts.title: RAGCell: Retrieval-Augmented Generation as Supervision for Versatile Single-cell Analysis
posts.authors: Liu T, Zhang F, Chen J, et al.
posts.summary: RAGCell is a single-cell analysis framework that uses a language model to build cell-level and feature-level knowledge databases, then aligns cell representations with text embeddings from them. This avoids the heavy pretraining that single-cell foundation models need.
key_points: It was tested on six downstream single-cell tasks.
The authors report performance matching or beating state-of-the-art single-cell foundation models at lower training cost.

posts.title: OrchAlign: Orchestrated Multimodal Alignment for Gene Expression Prediction
posts.authors: Liu L, Xv G, Liu S, et al.
posts.summary: OrchAlign predicts gene expression from DNA sequence and epigenomic signals. Instead of simple concatenation, it aligns the two modalities token by token on a shared representation within a key regulatory region.
key_points: Each modality is split into shared and specific parts, and the aligned parts keep their internal structure through a consistency term.
A BiMamba backbone fuses the representations, and the authors report state-of-the-art gene expression prediction.

posts.title: ScanTCR Enables Early Cancer Detection by Repertoire-Scale Representation of Cancer-Associated T-Cell Receptors in Peripheral Blood
posts.authors: Zhang J, Cai Y, Que J, et al.
posts.summary: ScanTCR is a computational framework that detects cancer early from the T-cell receptor repertoire in peripheral blood. It encodes the whole repertoire against a reference instead of using only high-frequency receptors.
key_points: In a pan-cancer analysis of seven cancer types it separated patients from non-cancer individuals and detected cancer types not seen in training.
It beat existing TCR-based methods and found cancer-associated TCRs whose T cells show stronger immune capacity.

posts.title: Phosphoproteomic dysregulation promotes tumor proliferation in Cushing's disease
posts.authors: Asuzu DT, Bhatt D, Mullaney D, et al.
posts.summary: The authors profiled chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, transcriptome, proteome and phosphoproteome in paired Cushing disease pituitary adenomas and adjacent normal pituitary. In the adenomas, a neurodevelopmental phosphoprotein program that is normally lost after birth is switched back on.
key_points: Adenoma cells overexpress PPP1R17, an inhibitor of the phosphatase PP2A; overexpressing it in normal mouse pituitary cells reproduced the hyperproliferation.
Fingolimod reversed that growth in a PP2A-dependent way in vitro and in vivo.

posts.title: Placenta-Related PEG10 Inhibits mRNA Decay to Promote Glucose Metabolism and Tumor Progression in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
posts.authors: Yao X, Wu B, Yang C, et al.
posts.summary: The authors screened placenta-specific genes that are abnormally expressed in liver cancer and found the retrovirus-like gene PEG10 overexpressed with poor prognosis. PEG10 acts as an RNA-binding protein that blocks Staufen1-mediated mRNA decay.
key_points: Blocking decay stabilises GLUT1 and HK2 mRNAs, raising glucose uptake and glycolysis in tumour cells.
Liver-specific Peg10 deletion slowed hepatocarcinogenesis in mice, and retinoic acid suppressed PEG10 and worked with sorafenib.

posts.title: dioscRi enables transferable prediction of clinical outcomes in multi-parameter cytometry data
posts.authors: Willie E, Rao S, Figtree G, et al.
posts.summary: dioscRi is a deep learning framework for predicting clinical outcomes from multi-parameter cytometry data in a way that transfers across datasets. A variational autoencoder normalises and de-noises the data, and an overlapping group LASSO uses cell type hierarchies.
key_points: It recovered known immune associations in a coronary artery disease study.
It outperformed existing methods on three of four benchmark datasets when moving between cohorts with compatible marker panels.

posts.title: Benchmarking single-cell foundation models for aging biology
posts.authors: Ni X, Liang Y, Zhu J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors benchmarked ten general single-cell foundation models, three aging-specific models and conventional methods on five aging questions using more than 2.5 million single-cell transcriptomes. Performance depended on the question.
key_points: Geneformer was best among foundation models for age prediction, though 2,000 highly variable genes scored higher on average.
SCimilarity was best for rare cell state identification, and scGPT recovered the most reference TF targets.

posts.title: NexuST: A Hierarchical Foundation Model for Spatial Transcriptomics
posts.authors: Liu H, Zhao Q, Lin L, et al.
posts.summary: NexuST is a spatial transcriptomics foundation model that alternates gene-level molecular modelling with cell-level spatial modelling during pretraining. It was pretrained on HumanST-46M, 45.7 million human cells from 72 datasets.
key_points: On four held-out datasets (about 2.6 million cells) it was state of the art or competitive for cell-type annotation, region prediction, gene recovery and neighbourhood composition.
An expression-only PCA baseline stayed informative even for spatial tasks.

posts.title: AtlasOT - The Fused Unbalanced Gromov-Wasserstein for Multimodal Integration of Disease Atlases
posts.authors: Peng K, Ruiz M, Caron B, et al.
posts.summary: AtlasOT integrates unpaired single-cell and spatial modalities with optimal transport. It maps cells only within the same donor or specimen and allows different cell recovery between modalities.
key_points: It beat baselines on scRNA-scATAC and scRNA-spatial mapping.
The transport plan also helps with rare cell detection, spot-level deconvolution, spatial gene imputation and spatial regulatory dynamics.

posts.title: Mutation Order and Selection Shape Intratumor Heterogeneity in Tumor Evolution
posts.authors: Chu Y, Sheng X, Zhang X, et al.
posts.summary: The authors model a tumour where malignancy needs two driver mutations, acquired in either order, using a multitype branching process. They derive a closed-form expression for clonal concentration (Simpson index).
key_points: A strong driver acquired early increases the supply of independent malignant founders; the same driver acquired last favours the growth of early clones.
Additive fitness can give a non-monotone link between selection and concentration, and threshold-like effects give highly concentrated populations.

posts.title: Unsupervised transcriptomic analysis of paired pre- and post-treatment specimens reveals divergent chemoimmunomodulatory induction trajectories in breast cancer
posts.authors: Lopes de Lima I, Molchan E, Streeks K, et al.
posts.summary: The authors built CIMIC, an unsupervised pipeline that clusters the change in expression of 3,189 immune-related genes between pre- and post-chemotherapy breast tumours. It finds two trajectories, a functional and a dysfunctional one.
key_points: The functional trajectory shows inflammatory cell death, antigen presentation and adaptive immune programs; the dysfunctional one shows stress-adaptation programs and lower cytotoxic activity.
Baseline scores for each trajectory tracked with better or worse outcomes in METABRIC and SCAN-B.

posts.title: Pervasive Somatic Mutations in NF1 Drive Cell Type and Spatially Specific Clonal Selection in Neurofibromatosis
posts.authors: Snellings D, Essuman K, Finander B, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell genomics in more than 1.7 million cells from people with neurofibromatosis type 1 shows that somatic second-hit NF1 mutations are common and positively selected in oligodendrocytes and their precursors, but very rare in neurons.
key_points: Spatial genotyping shows mutant precursor clones expand more in gray matter than white matter.
NF1-null oligodendrocyte lineage cells upregulate CDKN2A, while tumours from the same people lose it, suggesting CDKN2A loss is a key progression step.

posts.title: ctDNA Release Heterogeneity in Luminal Breast Cancer Revealed by Single-Cell Multi-Omics Spatial Analysis
posts.authors: Xu H, Pu P, Liu B, et al.
posts.summary: The authors developed scMASTER, combining single-cell transcriptomes and mutations, spatial transcriptomics and matched tumour and plasma DNA sequencing in ten HR+/HER2- breast cancer patients, to find which tumour cells release ctDNA.
key_points: Eight recurrent malignant states differed in release; antigen-presentation, stress, mitosis and mesenchymal-like states released most.
Three spatial regions (EMT-enriched, intraductal luminal progenitor, hypoxic) released most, and a stratification model was validated in external cohorts.

posts.title: Integrative Nanopore and Illumina sequencing reveals age-associated tRNA modification and CCA-tail dynamics in yeast
posts.authors: Brazell K, Prevost C, Zawrotna N, et al.
posts.summary: The authors present a benchmarked nanopore direct RNA sequencing (RNA004) resource for the yeast tRNAome during replicative aging, validated with Illumina sequencing and in vitro transcribed controls.
key_points: Overall tRNA abundance stays largely stable, but mature tRNAs lose the terminal A of the 3' CCA tail with age.
They also see targeted T-loop and anticodon modification changes and single-molecule co-occurrence of modifications.

posts.title: m6A-Driven Intratumoral Cholesterol Biosynthesis Fuels Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Progression
posts.authors: Lee J, Zhang Z, Hong J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors show that METTL3 interacts with the nucleoporin NUP93 to export m6A-modified mRNAs, and that this is coupled to cholesterol biosynthesis in castration-resistant prostate cancer.
key_points: Overexpressing wild-type METTL3 or NUP93, but not catalytically dead METTL3 or a METTL3-binding-defective NUP93, raised androgen levels and androgen-independent growth.
Inhibiting METTL3 or demethylating cholesterol-enzyme mRNAs suppressed growth.

posts.title: Critical assessment of nanopore sequencing for the detection of multiple forms of DNA modifications
posts.authors: Kong Y, Zhang Y, Mead E, et al.
posts.summary: The authors introduce modFDR, a framework that uses negative controls and false discovery rates to assess nanopore detection of DNA modifications. Detection is reliable for abundant marks but not for rare ones.
key_points: 5mC at CpG sites and 5hmC in brain cells are detected reliably.
Low-abundance marks (5mC at CpH, 5hmC, 6mA) in most mammalian cell types have many false positives, and 5mCpG shows elevated false negatives.

posts.title: An epigenetic program dictates MYC amplification dynamics that promote transient, extrachromosomal, and inherited genomic events
posts.authors: Ferman BI, Azadegan C, Santoro J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors ask how MYC copy gains first arise from a diploid genome. They show that H3K4 methylation primes MYC for amplification by the demethylase KDM4C, while the methyltransferase SETD2 holds copy gains back.
key_points: SETD2 loss or inhibition recruits active KDM4C, which starts and drives stepwise MYC copy gains; the same relationships appear in tumour datasets.
Blocking apoptosis or losing TP53 speeds up higher-level amplification, including extrachromosomal circular DNA and inherited copy gains.
Non-transformed cells with these changes are tumorigenic, and KDM4C inhibition suppresses MYC amplification.

figure.caption: H3K4me-primed MYC is amplified through KDM4C and restrained by SETD2, giving stepwise copy gains that end in ecDNA, sped up by TP53 loss or blocked apoptosis.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Euchromatin forms condensed domains with short active regions on the surface
posts.authors: Paggi JM, Long LY, Zhang B
posts.summary: The authors built a simulation framework that turns region-capture micro-C contact maps into conformational ensembles of megabase-scale regions at nucleosome resolution. The inferred structures contradict the classical view of euchromatin as uniformly open.
key_points: A micro-C balancing step corrects for variation in contact density, and the simulations reproduce distances measured by chromatin tracing.
Euchromatin forms condensed domains of similar density but smaller size than heterochromatin domains.
Kilobase-scale promoters and enhancers often protrude from these domains and become highly accessible, which may help protein binding and enhancer-promoter contact.

figure.caption: Instead of an open fibre, simulated euchromatin forms condensed domains from which promoters and enhancers protrude.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Photolabile oligonucleotides with topological light gradients enable spatially resolved single-cell transcriptomics and epigenomics
posts.authors: Piscopio RA, Chialastri A, Wang C, et al.
posts.summary: scSTAMP-seq labels live or fixed cells with cholesterol-conjugated, photocleavable hashtag oligonucleotides. Patterned light then 'stamps' spatial coordinates onto cells before standard single-cell multiome sequencing.
key_points: Spatial information is kept while using standard single-cell platforms, so no specialised spatial instrument is needed.
The method is modular and works for both transcriptomics and multiome profiling.
Applied to human embryoids, it shows how spatial organisation and epigenetic states jointly regulate cellular programs.

figure.caption: Photocleavable tags on cells are cut by a patterned light gradient, so each cell's position is read out with its RNA and chromatin profile.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Population-scale immune multiome atlas reveals regulatory disease mechanisms
posts.authors: Kanai M, Delorey TM, Honkanen J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors profiled chromatin accessibility and gene expression together in 10 million PBMCs from 1,108 Finnish individuals. The paired data link non-coding variants to disease through chromatin-to-expression cascades.
key_points: They report 51,083 cis-eQTLs, 338,100 cis-chromatin accessibility QTLs, 119,094 putative causal variants and 593,765 peak-gene links.
Variants that complete a chromatin-to-expression cascade show twice the disease colocalisation of chromatin-only effects; 10,428 fine-mapped QTLs were validated by massively parallel reporter assays.
At evolutionarily constrained genes, accessibility changes are buffered before reaching expression, through weaker and more numerous enhancer-gene links.

posts.title: The early RNA decay factor ZC3H18 directs first intron splicing
posts.authors: Le Rest M, El Houda Benbahouche N, Kuhn CC, et al.
posts.summary: The authors show that ZC3H18, known as an early RNA decay linker, also stimulates splicing of the first intron genome-wide. It does this by interacting with the splicing factors PRPF40A, PRP4K and FNBP4.
key_points: Disrupting the CBC-ARS2-ZC3H18 axis corrupts first intron splicing, linking the effect to the cap-binding complex.
ZC3H18's binding to splicing factors is mutually exclusive with its binding to the NEXT decay complex.
The model: splicing factors displace NEXT, sending nascent RNA down a productive splicing path instead of decay.

posts.title: Profiling extracellular vesicle glycoRNAs defines their function in vesicular communication
posts.authors: Chen X, Hao C, Chen X, et al.
posts.summary: The authors show that extracellular vesicles carry glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs). Metabolic tagging with bioorthogonal handles let them enrich and sequence these RNAs and track them by imaging.
key_points: EV glycoRNAs differ by sequence, vesicle type and transfer dynamics; large and small EVs show distinct repertoires.
EVs deliver glycoRNAs to recipient cells, and hybridisation-based blockade of glycoRNAs strongly reduces EV uptake.
The authors suggest EV glycoRNAs are biomarkers of cell state and regulators of vesicle tropism.

posts.title: Lineage identity governs oncogene dependence in mouse NSCLC models of KRAS inhibitor resistance
posts.authors: Mathey-Andrews N, Rodriguez CL, Shui B, et al.
posts.summary: Using mouse models of Kras-driven lung adenocarcinoma treated with KRAS inhibitors, the authors model both KRAS-dependent and KRAS-independent resistance. Genetic Kras amplification arises with continued treatment, while squamous lineage transformation gives oncogene-independent resistance.
key_points: Residual tumour after initial treatment transcriptionally resembles alveolar epithelial cells.
ΔNp63 is sufficient to push alveolar organoids to a squamous state that ignores KRAS inhibition; Nkx2-1 loss and ectopic Sox2 poise tumours for squamous commitment in vivo.
Squamous-transformed tumours show no KRAS/MAPK reactivation, pointing to lineage transcription factors as the cause of KRAS independence.

posts.title: Single-allele nanoscale mapping of regulatory variants
posts.authors: Hamley JC, Zhang W, Willmott D, et al.
posts.summary: The authors developed MCCv, a Micro Capture-C platform that reads single-allele chromatin structure to link regulatory variants to their target genes. They applied it to 405 cis-regulatory elements tied to immune-mediated inflammatory disease in CD4 T cells.
key_points: MCCv can phase heterozygous variants to connect regulatory variants with allelically imbalanced expression, and reads variant effects on chromatin contacts after genome editing.
It found a gain-of-function mechanism where a neo-CTCF motif blocks super-enhancer contacts with the SESN3 promoter and raises autoimmunity risk.
SESN3 regulates mTOR by sensing tryptophan, and mouse models support its role in autoimmunity.

posts.title: Machine learning and statistical methods for molecular quantitative trait loci
posts.authors: Engelhardt BE, Weinstock JS, Nyquist SK, et al.
posts.summary: This review covers statistical and machine-learning methods for mapping molecular quantitative trait loci (molQTLs), such as genetic effects on gene expression or chromatin accessibility. It focuses on how these methods improve standard mapping, downstream analyses and mechanistic insight.
key_points: Larger cohorts and more molecular phenotypes have increased the power of molQTL mapping.
Statistical models and, increasingly, machine learning are being developed for mapping and downstream analysis.
The emphasis is on understanding mechanisms linking genetic variation to phenotype in a gene regulatory context.

posts.title: GLM-Prior: a genomic language model for transferable sequence-derived priors in gene regulatory network inference
posts.authors: Skok Gibbs C, Chen A, Bonneau R, et al.
posts.summary: GLM-Prior is a genomic language model fine-tuned to predict transcription factor-target gene interactions from nucleotide sequence. It supplies sequence-derived priors for gene regulatory network inference when curated priors are missing.
key_points: Paired with PMF-GRN, it combines sequence-derived priors with single-cell expression for prior-conditioned network inference.
Across six cell-line contexts, it beats accessibility-based priors in four of five mammalian cell lines.
Prior quality largely limits network inference performance, and species-transfer training gives informative priors across related mammals.

posts.title: Mapping genetic regulation of gene expression to cellular contexts identifies long non-coding RNAs associated with brain disorders
posts.authors: Jia Y, Chen L, Song L, et al.
posts.summary: The authors map interaction eQTLs for long non-coding RNAs in cortical RNA-seq from 2,443 individuals, using deconvolution-derived cell-type proportions. This gives cell-context-dependent genetic regulation without single-nucleus data.
key_points: 3,763 of 17,541 analysed lncRNAs have cellular-context-dependent effects, and 74% of those are not annotated by GENCODE.
Colocalisation with GWAS of brain-related traits gives 118 lncRNA-trait events, about two-thirds detectable only after modelling cell context.
The result is a map for nominating lncRNAs that may mediate genetic risk for brain disorders.

posts.title: pileup-hi: an ultra-high-throughput, customizable alignment pileup program for large datasets
posts.authors: Piliper E, Greninger AL
posts.summary: pileup-hi is a multi-threaded alignment pileup engine built for billions of reads and high-depth clinical sequencing, where variants down to 0.01% may be called. It also supports custom output formats.
key_points: In mpileup format it is up to 13x faster than samtools mpileup, 3.2x faster than sambamba mpileup and up to 8x faster than perbase base-depth.
Aimed at time-sensitive uses such as cancer screening on Illumina NovaSeq X and Ultima UG 100 data.

posts.title: scLDM: a conditional diffusion framework for single-cell perturbation prediction
posts.authors: Wu B, Liu Y, Cheng Y, et al.
posts.summary: scLDM predicts single-cell responses to perturbations with a latent diffusion model. A variational autoencoder compresses expression, and a conditional diffusion process generates post-perturbation states guided by cell state, cell type and perturbation.
key_points: Tested on six datasets spanning drugs, viral and helminth infection, genetic perturbations and multi-species immune responses, with better accuracy than state-of-the-art methods.
Learned perturbation embeddings align with known biological mechanisms.

posts.title: Urine cell-free RNA for bladder cancer detection and treatment response prediction
posts.authors: Liu KJ, Shi WY, Nesselbush MC, et al.
posts.summary: The authors describe uRARE-seq, a liquid-biopsy method that profiles urine cell-free RNA, and apply it to 683 urine samples from patients with cancer and controls. It detects tumour-derived transcripts in prostate, kidney and bladder cancer.
key_points: It detects localised bladder cancer with 95% sensitivity at 90% specificity, outperforming urine tumour DNA analysis and unaffected by field-effect mutations.
It detects minimal residual disease and separates complete molecular responses after surgery from those after BCG.
Pretreatment urine from BCG responders is enriched for T cell signatures, and a biomarker built in 114 patients predicts likelihood of response.

posts.title: Meso-scale spatial analysis of papilloma formation and clonal expansion in cancerized skin
posts.authors: Busa VF, Behm M, Baeza-Centurion P, et al.
posts.summary: Using the two-stage DMBA/TPA mouse skin model, the authors profile genotype and transcriptome from the same coordinate-registered 1-mm punches across several centimetres, plus matched single-cell RNA-seq. This links clonal selection to local transcriptional programs.
key_points: All sequenced papillomas carried a driver mutation, but the driver was necessary and not sufficient for tumorigenesis within the study period.
Field-level signalling is rewired before tumours appear: TNF-associated necroptosis rises broadly and TGFB activity becomes spatially 'rugged', measured by a new Laplacian-based score.
Papillomas sit at local TGFB signalling minima.

posts.title: Diagnostic yield of cancer predisposition in a nationwide prospective childhood acute leukemia cohort
posts.authors: Taylan F, Staffas A, Sjögren S, et al.
posts.summary: In a nationwide prospective study of 181 children with acute leukaemia, the authors tested germline whole-genome sequencing with a 189-gene panel, plus tumour sequencing of positive cases and trio-WGS in 11 high-suspicion families.
key_points: Nine patients (about 5%) had pathogenic germline alterations: six leukaemia predisposition syndromes (TP53, CEBPA, DNMT3A, trisomy 21) and three solid tumour syndromes (MSH6, PALB2, SDHA).
Six of the nine diagnoses were previously unrecognised; findings changed surveillance in 8 of 9 patients and treatment in 4 of 9.
The diagnostic yield is modest but actionable.

posts.title: Persistent chromatin alterations and gene expression reprogramming follow widespread DNA damage in glioblastoma
posts.authors: Modrek AS, Chandradoss KR, Do C, et al.
posts.summary: The authors introduced many simultaneous Cas9-induced double-strand breaks at defined sites in glioblastoma cells and followed genetic and non-genetic changes over time. This models widespread DNA damage such as chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
key_points: Megabase-scale changes persisted two weeks after damage, including a shift from transient intra-TAD contacts to lasting long-range cis and trans contacts.
Gene expression changed and large structural variants appeared.
The findings suggest widespread DNA damage can leave long-term genetic and non-genetic changes that may affect tumour outcome and resistance.

posts.title: Isolated clival Langerhans cell histiocytosis in a pediatric patient: systematic review and illustrative case report
posts.authors: Abdallah AM, Hulliel AF, Dabash TY, et al.
posts.summary: The authors report a 3.5-year-old boy with isolated clival Langerhans cell histiocytosis and add a PRISMA systematic review of 11 published cases. Chordoma appears here as a skull base tumour that the lesion can mimic on imaging.
key_points: Osteolytic clival lesions mimicked chordoma and other skull base tumours; abducens palsy and diplopia were the most common symptoms.
Histology showed typical LCH with CD1a and S100 positivity, so biopsy confirmation is essential.
Management varied (biopsy, resection, chemotherapy, radiotherapy) and outcomes were mostly favourable.

posts.title: Nailpolish: Reference-free UMI deduplication and consensus read generation
posts.authors: Cheng OY, Tan JW, Davidson NM
posts.summary: Nailpolish is a fast, reference-free tool that error-corrects and deduplicates UMI-tagged long reads by building consensus sequences with partial order alignment. It also separates false duplicates caused by UMI collisions.
key_points: Tested on eleven Oxford Nanopore and PacBio datasets spanning bulk, single-cell, spatial and targeted protocols.
It lowered per-read error rates and outperformed existing deduplication tools.

posts.title: Accurate isoform quantification in bulk and single-cell RNA-seq by integrating multi-platform sequencing data and sequence-to-expression models
posts.authors: Apostolides M, Wang J, Saberi A, et al.
posts.summary: MPAQT is a probabilistic framework that combines short- and long-read RNA-seq while modelling each platform's biases. It quantifies transcript isoforms in bulk and single-cell data.
key_points: It gives state-of-the-art isoform quantification from short reads alone, and improves further when short and long reads are analysed jointly.
Sequence-to-expression models (RNA-binding protein motifs, co-expression) can be added as priors, improving single-cell quantification.
The models point to isoform-specific UTR sequence features as strong contributors to isoform abundance and exon usage.

posts.title: DECIPHER integrates disentangled representation learning and prototype-based cell-type deconvolution across molecular modalities
posts.authors: Lai W, Li C, Deng Q, et al.
posts.summary: DECIPHER is an end-to-end deep-learning framework for cell-type deconvolution of bulk omics that works across molecular modalities. It learns a domain-constant representation for deconvolution and a domain-specific one for batch-like variation.
key_points: Nonlinear representation learning is combined with differentiable non-negative least squares to estimate cell-type proportions.
It performs robustly on simulations, experimental bulk mixtures and real datasets.
The learned representation also supports age prediction across cohorts and prognostic stratification in lung adenocarcinoma.

posts.title: Benchmarking niche identification via domain segmentation for spatial transcriptomics data
posts.authors: Wang Y, Chen Y, Yang L, et al.
posts.summary: The authors annotated single-cell-resolution CosMx data of a human follicular lymphoid hyperplasia lymph node as a reference. They benchmarked 16 domain segmentation algorithms for finding tissue niches.
key_points: Most methods in default settings fail to recover biologically defined niche boundaries.
Stochastic infiltration of peripheral cell types lowers the spatial signal-to-noise ratio, which prioritises local variance over architecture.
Weighting core functional lineages restores niche resolution in some frameworks.

posts.title: A gene program association study (GPAS) delineates novel patterns of lineage plasticity and aggressiveness in non-small cell lung cancer
posts.authors: Campbell JD, Hong R, Klockner P, et al.
posts.summary: The authors built an atlas of gene co-expression modules in cancer cells from 127 primary NSCLCs using a new framework, GPAS, and linked the modules to clinical and histopathological features.
key_points: Lung adenocarcinoma shows extensive lineage infidelity, with modules from several alveolar cell types; late-stage modules appear in early-stage tumours.
Basal- and squamous-like cells are proposed intermediates in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma.
A new squamous subtype has lower canonical squamous modules and higher fibrinogen; squamous modules also appear in smoke-exposed normal basal cells.

posts.title: Three-Year Longitudinal Analysis of Splicing Changes in Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1
posts.authors: Legare C, Planco L, Merritt R, et al.
posts.summary: The authors measured a splicing index (SI) by targeted RNA-seq in vastus lateralis biopsies from 20 people with myotonic dystrophy type 1, taken three years apart, to see how splicing dysregulation progresses.
key_points: Baseline SI correlated with percent predicted muscle strength in ankle, knee and hand-grip muscles.
SI worsened on average, but progression varied widely between participants; adult versus juvenile phenotype and lower baseline SI were linked to faster progression.
The authors say clinical phenotype and baseline severity should be considered when reading longitudinal SI in trials.

posts.title: RNA-sequencing as an expression-informed alternative for somatic variant detection and cancer driver identification
posts.authors: Akutagawa J, Mak AJ, Damle T, et al.
posts.summary: The authors called somatic variants and cancer drivers from tumour RNA-seq alone in 1,359 PCAWG and TCGA samples that have matched WGS.
key_points: RNA-seq alone found at least one putative driver gene in 15 of 16 cancer types, consistent with WGS-based predictions.
Variant allele frequency of RNA-derived variants reflects predicted functional impact.
The work offers a pan-cancer resource of RNA-seq-derived variants.

posts.title: Accurate and scalable demultiplexing of single-cell RNA sequencing using BEACON
posts.authors: Ji BW, Lammers M, Houser A, et al.
posts.summary: BEACON is a sample demultiplexing method for barcode-multiplexed single-cell RNA-seq. It learns the background count distribution from the data and removes it from each cell, improving classification.
key_points: It outperforms other state-of-the-art methods on several human datasets.
Applied to cancer cell line time courses, it helped identify genes associated with aggressive tumours in vivo.
Adapted to protein-transcriptome profiling, it improves protein signal recovery and found a CD161-positive effector memory CD4 T cell population that was validated.

posts.title: Hyper-mutational processes provide a head-start for weak cancer drivers: explaining atypical KRAS variants
posts.authors: Nicholson MD, Tomlinson I
posts.summary: Using mathematical modelling, the authors show that aberrant mutational processes alone can explain why hypermutant cancers carry weak rather than canonical driver mutations.
key_points: Raising the mutation rate per cell division, without changing selection, can let weak drivers dominate because further driver events arrive quickly.
In POLE-mutant colorectal cancers, mutation bias plus elevated rate is enough to explain enrichment of atypical KRAS drivers; predictions fit mismatch-repair-deficient colorectal cancer too.

posts.title: DisenTE: Sparse Pattern-Context Modeling for Interpretable Translation-Efficiency Matrix Completion
posts.authors: Huo M, Yu Y, Li S
posts.summary: DisenTE is a sequence-conditioned neural model that completes a translation-efficiency atlas of 9,494 5' UTRs across 78 cellular and tissue contexts. It pairs sequence-derived modules with context-specific weights.
key_points: Under five-fold masking it reaches a UTR-centred residual Spearman correlation of 0.641, versus 0.304 for the strongest reference model.
Of 20 candidate modules, 11 are retained; module CTM 6 matches a cap-proximal pyrimidine pattern and overlaps an external TOP set.

posts.title: Deep learning perturbation models can outperform baselines on calibrated metrics
posts.authors: Miller HE, Mejia GM, Leblanc FJA, et al.
posts.summary: Recent benchmarks said deep-learning models of genetic perturbation fail to beat uninformative baselines. The authors add a positive-control baseline and a metric calibration framework and re-test across 14 datasets and 18 metrics.
key_points: Common metrics such as mean squared error and Pearson Δ are often miscalibrated and insensitive to real model skill.
With calibrated metrics, deep-learning perturbation models can outperform uninformative baselines.

figure.caption: On common metrics models and baselines look alike; calibrated metrics separate the deep-learning model from the uninformative baseline.

posts.title: Genomic alterations and treatment define spatiotemporal patterns of glioblastoma recurrence
posts.authors: Artzi SB, Harwood DSL, et al.
posts.summary: Histology-guided sampling and single-cell spatial transcriptomics of the surgical margin, adjacent recurrent tumour and matched primaries from 40 glioblastoma patients. The margin is a distinct wound-healing microenvironment where mesenchymal-like malignant states are enriched.
key_points: A 'stromal' subtype emerges at recurrence in patients with early TP53 mutation, sustained proliferation during temozolomide and shorter survival.
TP53 wild-type tumours recurring on temozolomide shift toward the mesenchymal subtype with higher p53 pathway activity and less proliferation.
TP53 loss increased temozolomide resistance in a patient-derived model.

figure.caption: Recurrence arises around the resection cavity; early TP53 mutation leads to a stromal subtype, TP53 wild type to a mesenchymal one.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Spatial evolution of a cachexia-promoting microenvironment in pancreatic cancer
posts.authors: Hu Y, Lv G, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell RNA-seq, Xenium spatial transcriptomics, multiplex IHC and bulk data from non-cachexia, pre-cachexia and cachexia pancreatic cancer samples, plus mouse models, define a cachexia niche. It is made of SEMA4A+ tumour cells, AQP9+ macrophages and LOXL2+ cancer-associated fibroblasts.
key_points: SEMA4A signalling drives BMP2-dependent AQP9+ macrophages, whose CXCL8 activates LOXL2+ fibroblasts.
Fibroblasts feed back to tumour FOSL1/SEMA4A signalling through exosomal N-glycosylated LOXL2.
The niche grows with cachexia severity and is linked to later cachexia in previously non-cachectic patients.

figure.caption: Tumour SEMA4A+ cells, AQP9+ macrophages and LOXL2+ fibroblasts form a signalling loop whose niche grows with cachexia severity.

posts.title: Genome-wide mapping of common and rare variant effects on adiposity across childhood
posts.authors: Kentistou KA, Sundfjord J, et al.
posts.summary: Age-stratified genetic association studies of childhood adiposity (up to about 600,000 children) find 624 common variants, a third without a matching adult BMI signal. Single-nucleus RNA-seq and exome sequencing in 479,615 people add cell types and rare coding variants.
key_points: Leptin-melanocortin (BSX, GNAS, LEPR, PCSK1) and incretin (GIPR, GLP1R) signals show childhood-specific effects.
Childhood-specific adiposity cell populations were found in the arcuate nucleus and mammillary bodies.
Rare variants in ADCY3, CALCR, MC4R, MRAP2, POMC and MYH13 have stronger effects in childhood.

posts.title: Times are changing but order matters: transferable prediction of small-molecule liquid chromatography retention times
posts.authors: Kretschmer F, Harrieder EM, et al.
posts.summary: Retention times shift between chromatographic systems, but retention order is more conserved. The 2-step method first predicts a retention order index with machine learning, then maps it to absolute retention times.
key_points: Predicts retention times across conditions and compound classes with no training data from the target system.
Outperforms existing methods trained on the target dataset.
Also maps which chromatographic conditions change retention order.

posts.title: Microbiome signatures linked to cancer and treatment adverse events in a real-world cohort
posts.authors: Yang L, Singh V, et al.
posts.summary: A mixed-cancer cohort of 1,364 patients and 287 healthy controls (Mayo Clinic Cancer Microbiome) is analysed with a framework that accounts for comorbidities and clinical variables. This separates cancer-specific from non-specific microbiome associations.
key_points: 341 cancer-associated species were identified across five cancer classes.
Early-onset breast cancer showed lower fecal bile acids and C. scindens; early-onset colorectal cancer showed more lactate and Veillonella parvula.
Anaerostipes hadrus encoding dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase was protective against 5-fluorouracil-induced diarrhea.

posts.title: Single-cell analysis of chromatin accessibility in the human intestine identifies regulatory programs and clarifies genetic associations in Crohn's disease
posts.authors: Zhao Y, Zhou R, et al.
posts.summary: A cell-type-resolved atlas of 557,310 candidate cis-regulatory elements from terminal ileum and ascending colon of 23 patients with Crohn's disease and 16 healthy controls.
key_points: Crohn's disease heritability is mainly enriched in T cells and neutrophils.
30 fine-mapped noncoding Crohn's variants fall within cCREs.
Regulatory programs behind inflammatory responses in the mucosa are characterised.

posts.title: Germline homologous recombination deficiency influences TP53-mutant clonal hematopoiesis fitness during platinum and PARP inhibitor treatment
posts.authors: Baeten JT, Chan ICC, et al.
posts.summary: Serial blood sampling in patients on PARP inhibitors shows DNA-damage-response clonal hematopoiesis is common after therapy, mostly explained by prior carboplatin. A Trp53-mutant mouse model supports the findings.
key_points: DDR clonal hematopoiesis expanded during carboplatin and, less so, during PARP inhibitor treatment.
Expansion was largely reduced in patients with germline HRD.
Risk of therapy-related myeloid neoplasm after PARPi may depend on earlier therapy and germline HRD status.

posts.title: Cell atlas of the developing human meninges reveals a dura-like nature of meningiomas
posts.authors: Vinsland E, Marco Salas S, et al.
posts.summary: A single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlas of human fetal meninges (post-conceptional weeks 5-13) is compared with meningioma transcriptomes. Meningioma cells resemble the dura lineage rather than the arachnoid.
key_points: Meningeal layers develop concurrently; the inner CDH1+ dura layer expresses tight-junction genes.
Common meningioma driver genes are expressed in the dura lineage.
Suggests meningiomas could originate from dura-lineage cells.

posts.title: Spatially resolved chromatin architectures in mammalian brain tissues
posts.authors: Chen Z, Guo M, et al.
posts.summary: Spatial Hi-C resolves genome-wide 3D chromatin structure directly in tissue sections of mouse embryo and brain. In the cerebellum, granular-layer subclusters defined by distinct 3D genomes align with anatomical lobules.
key_points: Reconstructs single-spot 3D chromatin structures at 10 µm resolution in adult cortex, similar to single-cell data.
A radial gradient of the short-versus-long interaction ratio in developing brain tracks neuronal maturity.

posts.title: Handling biological replicates in long-read RNA sequencing data by joining or not joining
posts.authors: Jetzinger F, Paniagua A, Cormack S, et al.
posts.summary: Compares two ways to build a consensus transcriptome from replicated long-read RNA-seq: Join & Call (pool reads, then reconstruct) and Call & Join (reconstruct per sample, then merge). Tested on mouse brain and kidney with PacBio and ONT and six reconstruction tools.
key_points: The best strategy depends on the tool and the goal.
Join & Call is generally better for finding novel isoforms.
Call & Join is often better for highly replicated datasets when novelty matters less.

posts.title: Regulation of mRNA poly(A) tail length governs mammalian body plan formation in gastruloids
posts.authors: Taborsky D, Valdivia-Francia F, Serrano P, et al.
posts.summary: A single-cell CRISPR screen in mouse gastruloids maps post-transcriptional drivers of germ layer specification and identifies the deadenylase Cnot8.
key_points: Loss of Cnot8 lengthens poly(A) tails widely and stabilises transcripts.
Mesoderm shifts toward ectopic notochord fate, disrupting axial patterning.

posts.title: Multiplatform single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal sex-specific malignant states and architecture in male breast cancer
posts.authors: Shi H, Zhang X, Cai S, et al.
posts.summary: An atlas of over 660,000 cells from male and female breast cancer integrating scRNA-seq, SeekSpace, Visium HD, Xenium and multiplex IHC.
key_points: Male-specific tumour cells are enriched in male breast cancer and linked to poorer disease-free survival.
They show neural programs, higher inferred copy-number burden and lower antigen presentation.
Spatial association with macrophages suggests a tumour-macrophage axis.

posts.title: Fusion-driven oncogenic programs shape the immune landscape in translocation renal cell carcinoma
posts.authors: Konda P, Wakolbinger AJ, Cui Y, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell transcriptomes and chromatin accessibility from TFE3-fusion translocation RCC show six conserved tumour meta-programs, including EMT and proximal tubule identity.
key_points: TFE3 fusion activity balances the EMT and proximal tubule programs.
The EMT program drives a suppressive microenvironment with progenitor-exhausted CD8+ T cells, SPP1+ macrophages and matrix fibroblasts.
May explain weaker immunotherapy response than clear cell RCC.

posts.title: Uncovering pan-cancer signatures of chemoresistance
posts.authors: Inayatullah M, Demirdizen E, Keepers Z, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell, spatial, regulatory network and TF-binding data across cancer types define a conserved chemoresistant state. Resistant cells are proliferative rather than quiescent, with E2F and MYC target activity.
key_points: MYC is a central regulator of the resistant state.
SRM (spermidine synthase), a new MYC target, supports polyamine biosynthesis and predicts poor survival.
Inhibiting MYC, SRM or WNT restored chemosensitivity in cells, organoids and mice.

posts.title: stFormer integrates spatial ligand signaling into a foundation model for spatial transcriptomics
posts.authors: Cao S, Yang K, Cheng J, et al.
posts.summary: A transformer for spatial transcriptomics that uses cross-attention over spatial ligand genes. A biased cross-attention lets it learn single-cell resolution from low-resolution Visium data; pretrained on about 4.1 million spatial samples.
key_points: Improves on scFoundation for clustering, batch correction, cell type and gene function prediction.
In silico perturbation reveals ligand-receptor signalling responses.

posts.title: Spatial Analysis Dissects the Microenvironmental Architecture of Local Recurrence after Breast-Conserving Surgery
posts.authors: Qu FL, Zhu XH, Chen F, et al.
posts.summary: Single-cell spatial transcriptomics of primary breast cancers and matched ipsilateral recurrences from 22 patients (over 600,000 cells), separating true recurrences from new primaries.
key_points: Recurrence is driven by a proliferative, immune-excluded epithelial subpopulation.
CD24+ tumour cells meet BGN+ cancer-associated fibroblasts with MDK and CXCL12 signalling.
Their colocalisation independently predicted recurrence.

posts.title: Site-specific inhibition of translation initiation via 2'-O-methylation
posts.authors: Suh A, Mou S, Patrasso EA, et al.
posts.summary: Cryo-EM structures suggest hydrogen bonds between 2'-OH groups of mRNA start codons and 18S rRNA. Methylating these 2'-OH groups (Nm) blocks start codon recognition by the preinitiation complex.
key_points: Nm at upstream AUG and near-cognate codons represses uORF translation.
This can raise expression of the canonical ORF.

posts.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing Single-Cell Expression through the Lens of Topic Modeling
posts.authors: Buznah Y, Ishon T, Shaham U.
posts.summary: Finds overlapping gene-expression programs in scRNA-seq with Latent Dirichlet Allocation, using a prior estimated from gene co-expression. No reference dataset or pathway database is needed.
key_points: Across 15 human and mouse datasets it matches cNMF and scHPF on GO Biological Process metrics.
Never ranks last, unlike the specialised methods.
Also orders genes within programs to recover developmental cascades.

posts.title: MultiSpaceNet: graph-based joint representation learning for paired spatial transcriptome-proteome data
posts.authors: Zhang Z, Chen B, Bai J, et al.
posts.summary: A cell-graph framework with typed spatial, transcriptomic and proteomic edges and per-cell attention fusion for paired spatial RNA and protein data.
key_points: Beat nine published methods at spatial domain identification on five benchmarks.
Leakage-free RNA-to-protein imputation matches or exceeds existing methods.
One model gives domains, imputation and cross-section embeddings.

posts.title: RNA isoform-resolved multiplexed sequencing with bioorthogonal barcoding
posts.authors: Malik T, Berlind J, Khan A, et al.
posts.summary: Bioorthogonal barcodes (bobcodes) are attached at internal positions along RNAs so samples can be pooled while keeping splice-junction information. Poly(dT) priming gives 3'-end counting; random hexamers give full-length isoform capture.
key_points: Reverse transcriptase switches to the bobcode with over 99% accuracy in species-mixing tests.
A BOB-seq v0.1 drug screen found on- and off-target splicing effects genome-wide.

posts.title: Structural variation in repeat elements is widespread in normal human tissues and in tumorigenesis
posts.authors: Annapragada AV, White J, Orjuela H, et al.
posts.summary: Long- and short-read WGS of 47 normal individuals (168 samples) finds mosaic structural variants in every individual, mostly repeat-mediated. Repeat alterations are then measured across 15 cancer types.
key_points: Mosaic SVs affect a median 285.2 kb per genome; 8.3% overlap functional elements.
Tumour-related repeat variation is similar in scale to normal mosaic variation.
Repeat changes in cell-free DNA offer noninvasive tumour monitoring.

posts.title: The strength of a gene's first 5' splice site is a key determinant of its expression
posts.authors: Sakai Y, McGurk MP, Kowal EJ, et al.
posts.summary: A reporter assay of thousands of natural human introns tests intron-mediated enhancement (IME) of expression. IME needs major-spliceosome introns and grows with 5' splice site strength, independent of 3' splice site strength.
key_points: Minor introns often repress expression.
Variants altering the first 5' splice site may change expression without changing splicing.
U1 snRNP perturbations that improve recognition up-regulate the associated genes.

posts.title: RNA splicing factor mutations drive myeloid neoplasm oncogenesis through protein complex poisoning
posts.authors: Moura PL, Branca RMM, Kaminskiy Y, et al.
posts.summary: Long/short-read single-cell transcriptomics and low-cell proteomics in 62 myeloid neoplasm patients and 20 healthy donors follow splicing factor mutations through haematopoietic differentiation.
key_points: Mis-splicing decouples RNA and protein dynamics in a mutation-specific way.
Early protein effects poison whole functional protein complexes, which transcriptomics could not predict.
iPSC models of early haematopoiesis validate the proteome dynamics.

posts.title: The Genome In A Bottle HG002 assembly-based variant benchmark set enables comprehensive benchmarking of small and structural variants
posts.authors: Olson ND, Dwarshuis N, Hansen NF, et al.
posts.summary: The GIAB HG002 v5.0q benchmark is derived from a fully phased diploid assembly, covering segmental duplications, homopolymers, tandem repeats and complex immune loci. Available for GRCh37, GRCh38 and CHM13.
key_points: Adds about 200 Mbp of callable sequence versus v4.2.1.
Variant counts rise 18% for small variants and 3-fold for structural variants.
Validated across several sequencing technologies and variant-calling pipelines.

posts.title: Genomic correlates of metastatic competence and progression in human melanoma
posts.authors: Chatziioannou E, Luthria K, Shah P, et al.
posts.summary: Sequencing of 247 stage I/II primary melanomas and 60 matched metastases, integrating copy-number, mutation, protein and spatial transcriptomic data.
key_points: Relapse is marked by copy-number alterations and chromosomal instability, not point mutations.
OncoCycle, a six-gene copy-number signature, predicted relapse independently of clinicopathological features.
Both monoclonal and polyclonal metastasis seeding were seen.

posts.title: Base modification analysis in long read sequencing data using Minimod
posts.authors: Samarasinghe S, Robinson CM, Goeke J, et al.
posts.summary: Minimod is a vendor-independent tool to extract and analyse DNA and RNA base modifications from MM/ML tags in ONT and PacBio data. Written in C.
key_points: About 1.3-1.6x faster than modkit and pb-CpG-tools on DNA on a server, about 4x on a laptop.
On RNA data about 12x faster on a server and 55x on a laptop than modkit.

posts.title: A framework for designing splice-junction experiments in deep 3' single-cell RNA sequencing
posts.authors: Saferali A, Liu C, Vendrame AS, et al.
posts.summary: Deep scRNA-seq of human airway epithelium (12 samples) benchmarked against matched bulk RNA-seq from a 190-donor cohort to quantify how depth governs junction recovery in 3' chemistries.
key_points: Junction detection does not saturate with depth.
Recovering 90% of observed junctions needs about 52,250 reads per cell, several-fold more than gene-level analysis.
Rare cell types are limited by cell number, not depth.

posts.title: Post-transcriptional dysregulation precedes morphological transformation in chemically induced liver cancer
posts.authors: Izuogu OG, Jackson M.
posts.summary: Reanalysis of total RNA and matched genomes from 438 mouse liver lesions (diethylnitrosamine-induced) across four backgrounds, plus normal liver from treated animals.
key_points: Splicing efficiency falls, circRNA output rises and A-to-I editing sites fall in every background.
Coordination between these three outputs is lost after exposure, including in paired normal liver.
Histologically normal liver already looks tumour-like about eight months after one exposure.

posts.title: Complete timing of copy-number amplification histories reveals whole-genome duplication dynamics and coincident oncogene amplification bursts
posts.authors: Gulhan DC, Brew J, Park PJ.
posts.summary: Tau enumerates every allele-specific gain route to a copy-number state and derives an analytical timing for each gain, using co-amplified mutation multiplicity.
key_points: Across pan-cancer genomes about three-quarters of clonal gains are punctuated multichromosomal events, most of them whole-genome duplication.
The highest copy-number states arise in abrupt bursts around WGD, recurring at oncogenes.

posts.title: En Bloc Resection of a Giant Sacrococcygeal Chordoma Presenting with Urinary Bladder Distension to the L4 Level: A Case Report
posts.authors: John S, Khaliq T, Brohi G, et al.
posts.summary: A 54-year-old man with a giant S3-S5 sacrococcygeal chordoma presented with urinary retention and bladder distension to L4. A nerve-sparing posterior en bloc resection with neuromonitoring gave an R0 resection and restored voiding.
key_points: Bladder distension from mechanical outlet obstruction had not been described with sacrococcygeal chordoma.
Bilateral S1-S2 nerve roots were preserved and bowel and limb function stayed intact.
No recurrence at one-year follow-up.

posts.title: International Consensus Guidelines for Radiation Target Volume Delineation for Skull Base Chordoma - A Particle Therapy Co-operative Group Initiative
posts.authors: McDonald MW, Zhou J, Holtzman AL, et al.
posts.venue: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys
posts.summary: Fifteen particle-therapy radiation oncologists contoured three skull base chordoma cases, and a modified Delphi process turned the overlap into consensus target-volume guidelines. Preoperative tumour volumes were contoured consistently, while residual disease varied most.
key_points: Preoperative GTV agreement was highest (mean Dice 0.85); residual GTV was lowest (0.45).
Intermediate-dose CTV should cover the tumour bed plus the rest of the clivus with a median 5 mm margin.
High-dose CTV covers bone and mucosa of the primary tumour bed and any residual disease.

posts.title: Pre-Spondylectomy Radiofrequency Ablation for Spinal Chordoma: An Illustrative Case and Systematic Review of Clinical Applications and Outcomes
posts.authors: Husbands H, Johnston D, Tharakan M, et al.
posts.summary: A systematic review of 13 studies (33 patients) found that thermal ablation, mostly cryoablation or RFA, has been used for spinal and sacral chordoma before resection, as primary treatment, or for palliation. The authors add an L4 case treated with RFA before staged en bloc spondylectomy.
key_points: Most reports described pain relief and few major complications.
The L4 case had no new neurological deficit or recurrence at 18 months.
Evidence is sparse and heterogeneous; ablation should not replace en bloc resection when that is safe.

posts.title: CytoVI: deep generative modeling of antibody-based single cell data
posts.authors: Ingelfinger F, et al.
posts.summary: CytoVI is a probabilistic generative model for flow cytometry, mass cytometry and CITE-seq protein data. One model handles embedding, batch correction, imputation, differential protein testing and cell annotation.
key_points: Used to build a B-cell maturation atlas covering 350 proteins.
Found disease-associated T-cell states in B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
Open source in scvi-tools.

posts.title: ResolVI: addressing noise and bias in spatial transcriptomics
posts.authors: Ergen C, et al.
posts.summary: resolVI is a probabilistic model that runs after any cell segmentation tool on subcellular-resolution spatial data. It corrects molecule-to-cell misassignment, batch effects and other nuisance factors.
key_points: Improves separation of cell states and detection of subtle spatial expression changes.
Works with any segmentation method.
Enables integration across spatial datasets.

posts.title: The dual-enhanced graph learning framework DePass allows paired data integration in single-cell and spatial multiomics
posts.authors: Li W, et al.
posts.summary: DePass is a graph-learning framework that couples denoising and integration for paired single-cell and spatial multi-omics. It was benchmarked on 6 modalities, 9 tissues and 13 platforms, and applied to in-house colorectal cancer data.
key_points: Iterative denoise-and-integrate design.
Superior integration accuracy across a broad benchmark.
Revealed immune niche substructure and spatial heterogeneity in colorectal cancer.

posts.title: ArchMap is a web-based platform for reference-based analysis of single-cell datasets
posts.authors: Lotfollahi M, et al.
posts.summary: ArchMap is a no-code web platform for mapping query single-cell data onto integrated reference atlases and annotating cell types automatically. It supports collaborative use and extension of atlases such as the Human Cell Atlas.
key_points: Lowers the compute and expertise barrier to reference mapping.
Automated cell-type annotation against integrated references.
Reference atlases can be extended by users.

posts.title: Single-nucleus transcriptome-wide association study of human brain disorders
posts.authors: Venkatesh S, et al.
posts.summary: The authors built cell-type-specific models that impute genetically regulated expression from PsychAD single-nucleus data, then applied them to neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative GWAS. The models revealed gene-trait associations that bulk tissue models miss.
key_points: Thousands of associations were not visible in bulk-tissue TWAS.
Results were replicated across ancestries in the Million Veteran Program.
Purely computational, built on existing single-nucleus and GWAS data.

posts.title: Genetic factor analysis for characterizing phenome-wide patterns of genetic pleiotropy
posts.authors: Morrison J, et al.
posts.summary: Genetic factor analysis (GFA) is a multi-phenotype method that finds shared patterns of association across traits. It chooses the number of factors automatically, handles overlapping samples and allows non-orthogonal factors.
key_points: Decomposed 22 coronary artery disease and type 2 diabetes risk factors into 15 pleiotropic components.
Improved multivariable Mendelian randomization.
Applied to blood-cell traits.

posts.title: Single-cell profiling and genetic regulation of alternative polyadenylation in the human brain
posts.authors: Nan J, et al.
posts.summary: A single-cell atlas of alternative polyadenylation (APA) built from about 2 million cells across 379 aged human brains. Mapping cell-type 3'aQTLs for 4,288 genes linked 168 GWAS loci to 3' UTR choice.
key_points: Only 17.5% of these GWAS loci are shared with eQTLs, so APA adds distinct information.
3'aQTLs colocalise with pQTLs more than eQTLs do.
The SNCA 3' UTR choice changes mRNA localisation.

figure.caption: A 3′aQTL changes which poly(A) site is used, mapped per brain cell type; these GWAS loci overlap little with eQTLs.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: Peripheral Blood as the Sole Source for Cancer Neoantigen and Reactive T-Cell Discovery
posts.authors: Garcia-Garijo A, et al.
posts.summary: Neoantigens were predicted from cell-free DNA exome sequencing, and reactive T cells were isolated from blood by PD-1/CD39 co-expression. In 8 patients the blood-only pipeline recovered most biopsy-derived neoantigens and found extra ones.
key_points: Needs no tumour biopsy.
Roughly half of 69 metastatic patients may be eligible.
Combines cfDNA genomics with T-cell reactivity.

posts.title: Divergent medulloblastoma chromatin states disclose KDM2B as a selective dependency
posts.authors: Tao R, et al.
posts.summary: Integrating histone marks, mutations, methylation and transcriptomes across medulloblastoma subgroups showed a bivalent enhancer state at neurodevelopmental promoters in Group 3/4. KDM2B emerged as a selective dependency.
key_points: Aberrant KDM2B binding recruits PRC1 and PRC2 and represses neuronal differentiation.
Knockout or degradation of KDM2B suppresses growth in vitro and in vivo.
Combines new chromatin profiling with computational integration.

figure.caption: KDM2B binds bivalent neuronal promoters in Group 3/4 tumours and recruits PRC1/PRC2; losing KDM2B slows growth.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: MMEJ repair of breaks at TA repeats maintains ecDNA and cancer fitness
posts.authors: Billing D, et al.
posts.summary: Inhibiting microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) selectively depletes extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA). TA-rich loci on ecDNA are break hotspots, protected by FANCM and repaired through ERCC1-ERCC4 and Pol theta.
key_points: Single-cell whole-genome sequencing and human tumours show ecDNA rearrangement breakpoints at TA repeats.
Pol theta inhibition destabilises ecDNA.
Points to a therapeutic vulnerability of ecDNA-bearing cancers.

figure.caption: Breaks at TA repeats on ecDNA are repaired by MMEJ; blocking Pol θ loses the ecDNA and the cells' growth advantage.
figure.credit: Illustration drawn by Claude from the abstract, not a figure from the paper

posts.title: PeakATail: precision-first poly(A)-site calling and calibrated alternative polyadenylation analysis in single-cell RNA-seq
posts.authors: Tabat AA, Zendeh EB, Kaymaz Y
posts.summary: PeakATail calls polyadenylation sites from single-cell reads that still carry part of the poly(A) tail and ranks them by supporting molecules. It pairs them with a differential test whose false-positive rate was measured on shuffled labels.
key_points: 71-83% of calls fall within 100 bases of a curated atlas.
Cell-type switches replicated across twelve lung cancer patients and none appeared in shuffled-label runs.
Built for precision, at a cost to sensitivity; one pre-registered target was missed.

posts.title: FlowMap: Geometry Dynamics Consistent Embedding of RNA Velocity for Interpretable Cellular Trajectories
posts.authors: Hu J, Singh H, Das J, et al.
posts.summary: FlowMap jointly learns a low-dimensional manifold of gene expression and constrains RNA velocity to follow its local geometry. This gives coherent, denoised cellular trajectories.
key_points: Recovers continuous progressions, branching, cycles and stable-like states.
Highlights genes and programs involved in development.
Extends to spatial transcriptomics.

posts.title: Copy number signatures in targeted gene panels associate with patient outcomes in routine clinical data
posts.authors: Netz E, Moris C, Hasanovic A, et al.
posts.summary: Copy-number signatures were recovered from targeted gene panels in two real-world cohorts of 1,726 patients across 62 tumour types. They recapitulated genome-wide signature associations and tracked survival in ovarian, pancreatic and colorectal cancer.
key_points: Links to homologous recombination deficiency and TP53 alterations were reproduced.
In ovarian cancer, CN2 tracked CCNE1 amplification and shorter survival under paclitaxel/carboplatin, validated in an independent SNP-array cohort.
The underlying data are public.

posts.title: Somatic DDX41 mutations confer neomorphic splicing activity in the pathogenesis of myelodysplastic neoplasms
posts.authors: Venkataraman R, Puccio N, Hsueh T-Y, et al.
posts.summary: Hotspot somatic DDX41 mutations (R525H, G530D) behave as gain-of-function alleles that drive widespread splicing changes, unlike germline mutations. DDX41-R525H binds RNA more tightly, and its aberrantly spliced targets overlap its binding.
key_points: SEPTIN7 mis-splicing creates a premature stop codon and lowers protein level.
SEPTIN7 mis-splicing was seen in CD34+ cells only from patients with both germline and somatic DDX41 mutations.
Consistent across isogenic AML lines, mouse progenitors and patient cells.

posts.title: Ultra-fast and scalable high-resolution full-length single-cell RNA sequencing using CHART-seq
posts.authors: Zhang W, Chen A, Ye K, et al.
posts.summary: CHART-seq uses orthogonally indexed Tn5 complexes on RNA/cDNA heteroduplexes so samples can be pooled early, up to 96 cells per library. Library prep takes about 3 hours at under US$1 per cell.
key_points: Detected more genes and annotated isoforms than Smart-seq2, Smart-seq3, Flash-seq and SHERRY2 at matched depth.
Compatible with 384-well expansion.
The biological findings in vascular smooth muscle cells are exploratory (no independent replicates).

posts.title: An open imaging and AI resource enabling unbiased quantification of extrachromosomal DNA at scale
posts.authors: Behnamie P, Summers R, Chen J, et al.
posts.summary: The authors release 2,986 metaphase FISH image sets with manual annotations and benchmarks for ecDNA quantification. Comparing rule-based, deep-learning and probabilistic methods exposed count-dependent underestimation, which motivated the new method ecCount.
key_points: ecCount reaches an object-level F1 of 0.939 on held-out images with minimal count bias.
Images, annotations, retrainable models and workflows are shared.
Mixed: new imaging data plus computational methods.

posts.title: STAR Suite: Integrating transcriptomics through AI software engineering in the NIH MorPhiC consortium
posts.authors: Hung L-H, Yeung KY
posts.summary: STAR Suite folds trimming, feature-barcode assignment, probe handling, SLAM-seq analysis and quantification into the STAR codebase as a drop-in executable. It handles bulk RNA-seq, scRNA-seq, Perturb-seq, 10x Flex and SLAM-seq.
key_points: Up to 41-fold faster than Cell Ranger 9.0.1 on Flex, with high concordance (gene-level correlation 0.98-1.0).
First open-source Perturb-seq feature-barcode processing at production scale, per the authors.
Built through a human-directed, AI-implemented workflow; MIT licence.

posts.title: Evaluating the reliability of tools for mRNA annotation and IRES studies
posts.authors: May GE, Akirtava C, McManus J
posts.summary: The authors show that back-splicing circRNA plasmids create linear mRNA artifacts that give false-positive cellular IRES signals. Orthogonal assays validated with viral IRESes found no activity in putative cellular IRESes.
key_points: smFISH and qRT-PCR can misidentify nuclear ncRNAs as mRNAs.
A single-molecule sequencing assay is validated for identifying mRNA 5' ends.
A response to proposed approaches for IRES studies.
